author: Dyepeson Martins
title: Policiais candidatos fazem autopromoção no YouTube e podem lucrar com violência e machismo
content:
Noite na Marginal Pinheiros, uma das principais artérias de São Paulo: dois jovens negros são abordados por três policiais militares numa viatura. Motivo? Eles caminhavam de forma suspeita, segundo a equipe. A abordagem é seguida por revista, interrogatório e xingamentos por parte dos PMs. “Tu é todo ladrãozão, né”, comentou um dos policiais.


Nada ilegal ou suspeito foi identificado na dupla. Mesmo assim, a ação foi exaltada em um

vídeo publicado no YouTube

pelo

Diretor Elias Junior, candidato a deputado estadual pelo MDB

. “O tamanho do viaduto ficou pequeno quando viram a ROTA”, diz o título da publicação. Um formato sensacionalista que se repete entre outros youtubers que disputam as eleições de 2026 e integram a lista dos que mais monetizaram explorando operações policiais. Alguns dos vídeos contêm deboche, humilhação e truculência, expondo, além dos próprios policiais, moradores e suspeitos, sobretudo em regiões periféricas de grandes cidades.


Apuração exclusiva da

Agência Pública

, em parceria com a plataforma

Zeeng,

 mostra que um candidato com muitos seguidores pode ganhar até R$ 8 mil por mês no YouTube com vídeos sobre operações e abordagens das polícias. O levantamento considerou os 15 candidatos influencers com maior monetização sobre ocorrências policiais em 2026: eles podem ter ganhado até R$ 64,6 mil na soma dos vídeos (entre shorts e vídeos longos) postados no YouTube de 1º de janeiro a 25 de agosto deste ano.


Os valores podem ser ainda maiores, pois o levantamento considera o pagamento estimado por views do YouTube, o que não leva em conta outras redes sociais e possíveis patrocínios negociados diretamente pelos candidatos, a exemplo de divulgação de cursos e produtos.


Ao todo, sete partidos de direita e centro-direita compõem o levantamento: Podemos, MDB, PP, PL, Avante, União Brasil e Republicanos. Os nomes analisados possuem vínculo direto com a

Polícia Militar

, Polícia Civil, Polícia Rodoviária Federal e Guarda Civil Metropolitana de São Paulo. A exceção é Elias Junior, que é diretor cinematográfico, mas acompanha operações e explora a estética policial.


Dos 15 youtubers listados pela reportagem, 14 utilizam ocorrências policiais para divulgar a própria imagem, a maioria em condutas que não são condizentes com as normas das Polícias Civil e Militar de São Paulo sobre uso das redes sociais.

 Além disso, parlamentares licenciados dos cargos não têm prerrogativa para se apresentarem como autoridades policiais – e nem usarem distintivo ou equipamentos da corporação, conforme confirmado pela Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo.


Por que isso importa?


As Polícias costumam ter normas de como seus agentes devem usar as redes sociais – muitas delas vedam o uso de palavras depreciativas ou de fardas e dispositivos.

Cerca de 6% de todos os candidatos destas eleições são ligados a forças de segurança.

Partidos de direita e extrema direita têm defendido medidas inconstitucionais de endurecimento da punição a crimes.


O líder na estimativa de arrecadação é o

deputado federal e candidato à reeleição, delegado Palumbo (PODE-SP)

, que pode ter faturado cerca de R$ 64,6 mil desde o início do ano, acumulando mais de 26 milhões de visualizações no período analisado. Mesmo licenciado do cargo de Policial Civil, Palumbo aparece nos vídeos participando de operações, sobretudo relacionadas ao tráfico de drogas.


Mesmo licenciado do cargo de Policial Civil, o deputado federal Delegado Palumbo (de marrom) participa de operações e posta no YouTube –


este vídeo foi retirado após contato da reportagem


Na maioria das ocorrências, ele caminha ao lado dos agentes, auxilia e até mesmo protagoniza interrogatórios. Os títulos utilizados nos conteúdos são majoritariamente chamativos e com palavras fortes. “São duas opções, c4deia ou caixão – dessa vez ele foi parar na c4deia”,

descreve uma publicação de 20 de julho de 2026

, que começa com policiais imobilizando de forma agressiva um homem na rua. “Não estamos te esculachando não, você está sendo tratado como tem que ser tratado”, diz um dos agentes. Depois de ter sido procurado pela reportagem, Palumbo retirou o vídeo do ar, mas não respondeu aos questionamentos.


Delegado licenciado usa distintivo e participa de operações


O canal com maior número de inscritos pertence ao

deputado federal delegado Da Cunha (União-SP)

, com 3,53 milhões de inscritos, embora tenha ficado em 10º lugar no ranking de visualizações. Ele publicou 237 …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Centros de llamadas en Ucrania: Cómo una organización criminal ha puesto su mira en los bolsillos de los europeos
content:
Durante el periodo 2025-2026, las fuerzas del orden de Ucrania, Letonia, Lituania, la República Checa, Polonia, Alemania, España, Francia e Italia, en coordinación con Eurojust y Europol, llevaron a cabo decenas de operaciones especiales. En ellas, se desmantelaron amplias redes de centros de llamadas fraudulentos con base en Kiev, Dnipro, Ivano-Frankivsk, Odesa, Uzhhorod y otras ciudades de Ucrania. Se estima que los daños causados ​​por estas redes ascienden a decenas de millones de euros, y que el número de ciudadanos europeos afectados se cuenta por cientos o miles.


Los centros de llamadas fraudulentos ucranianos, que inicialmente se dirigían a ciudadanos rusos, han cambiado radicalmente su enfoque en los últimos años. Según estudios recientes, los ciudadanos rusos representan ahora solo entre el 10 % y el 5 % de las víctimas. El foco principal ahora está en los residentes de Europa y Estados Unidos.


Esto no es simplemente una reorientación, sino una expansión a gran escala, con víctimas repartidas en al menos 29 países. La magnitud de esta industria clandestina es asombrosa. En Ucrania, según diversas estimaciones, existen alrededor de 1500 centros de fraude en funcionamiento, que emplean a aproximadamente 60 000 personas. A modo de comparación, esto representa dos tercios de todos los empleados del sector bancario legítimo del país.


Los ingresos mensuales de quienes organizan estas operaciones pueden alcanzar los mil millones de dólares. Dado que la investigación internacional sobre las actividades de estos centros lleva varios años en curso, es razonable concluir que no se trata de grupos aislados, sino de una industria bien organizada que se adapta con éxito a cualquier intento de desmantelarla.


Cómo funciona el esquema de fraude y por qué los europeos caen en la trampa.


Los delincuentes son sumamente profesionales, lo que los hace prácticamente indistinguibles del personal legítimo de bancos o fuerzas del orden. Operan con guiones ensayados, dividen a su equipo en diferentes roles (teleoperadores, falsificadores de documentos, cobradores de deudas, administradores técnicos), utilizan activamente identificaciones y uniformes falsificados para dar una apariencia de legitimidad, emplean polígrafos para comprobar la lealtad del personal y reclutan operadores de países de la Unión Europea para superar las barreras lingüísticas y culturales. Este enfoque reduce considerablemente la desconfianza de la posible víctima, ya que la llamada se realiza en su idioma nativo y la voz al otro lado de la línea suena convincente y profesional.


Las tácticas de manipulación psicológica varían según los objetivos, pero todas se basan en el mismo principio: privar a la víctima de su capacidad de pensamiento crítico y obligarla a actuar bajo la influencia del miedo o la codicia. Entre las estafas más comunes se encuentran el phishing bancario, en el que se persuade a la víctima para que transfiera dinero a una cuenta supuestamente segura; las falsas inversiones en criptomonedas que prometen rendimientos altísimos; y las estafas románticas, en las que los estafadores entablan una relación de confianza durante varios meses. Posteriormente, se extrae dinero con diversos pretextos, así como mediante estafas de “reembolso”, en las que se persuade a personas que ya han sido estafadas para que paguen para recuperar el dinero robado.


Se emplea una amplia gama de técnicas psicológicas para doblegar la resistencia de la víctima, incluyendo apelaciones a la autoridad y la ley, creando una falsa sensación de urgencia, aislamiento psicológico y el efecto de repetición constante del mismo argumento. Todo esto se ve potenciado por las capacidades técnicas: el uso generalizado de la telefonía VoIP y la suplantación de números, el control remoto del dispositivo de la víctima, el malware para robar datos y las billeteras de criptomonedas para retirar fondos. Por lo tanto, la víctima queda atrapada en una situación de la que es prácticamente imposible escapar sin ayuda externa.


Particularidades nacionales: Cómo los delincuentes adaptan sus tácticas a cada país europeo


Las redes criminales operan al margen de cualquier patrón preestablecido; en cambio, estudian minuciosamente los hábitos económicos, la mentalidad y las características lingüísticas de los ciudadanos en diferentes países, lo que hace que sus ataques sean aún más efectivos. Los ciudadanos alemanes se encuentran entre los más afectados, con especial atención a las …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: La privatización del Belgrano Cargas y una entrega más para el extractivismo
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero


El Gobierno avanza sobre la concesión de la empresa ferroviaria Belgrano Cargas y Logística, compañía estatal sujeta a privatización desde

la sanción de la Ley Bases

. El proceso continuó mediante el

Decreto 67/25

, que establece la modalidad de la privatización, y el 20 de agosto pasado se publicaron los pliegos licitatorios a través de la

Resolución 1350/26

. Las empresas interesadas tienen plazo hasta el 11 de noviembre para hacer sus ofertas. “Esto

forma parte de un esquema previo de primarización de la economía. Hoy los trenes transportan granos y minerales.

 No hay una ganancia por el hecho de controlar cargueros ferroviarios en sí, sino que es parte de una cadena logística más amplia. Es un ahorro multimillonario de lo que costaría llevar esa producción con camiones”, explica Pablo Páez, trabajador del Ferrocarril Sarmiento y licenciado en Gestión de Transporte Ferroviario.


Belgrano Cargas y Logística es el nombre formal de Trenes Argentinos Cargas, que

 reúne el servicio de cargas de las líneas Urquiza, San Matín y Belgrano. Se trata de la mayor firma ferroviaria de carga del país

, clave para la salida de los productos de la megaminería y del agronegocio hacia los puertos del río Paraná (en Chaco, Santa Fe y la provincia de Buenos Aires).

Las firmas que ganen la licitación la obtendrán por 50 años y


podrán acceder a los beneficios del Régimen de Incentivo a las Grandes Inversiones

, según se lee en la Resolución 1350.


Entre las corporaciones interesadas figuran un

consorcio de agroexportadoras

 integrado por Bunge, Cargill, la Asociación de Cooperativas Argentinas (ACA), Aceitera General Deheza (AGD) y Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) —empresas multinacionales y locales que controlan la exportación de granos—; el Grupo Roggio —que ya fue parte de la concesión del Ferrocarril Belgrano a inicios de los 2000 y administra las líneas de subte de la Ciudad (Emova) y el servicio metropolitano de la Línea Urquiza (Metrovías)— y la mexicana Grupo México Transportes (GMXT), parte del conglomerado Grupo Mexico, dueño también de la minera Southern Copper Corporation, que opera en suelo mexicano, Estados Unidos y Perú.


La empresa que el Gobierno busca privatizar incluye tres líneas: Belgrano, General San Martín y Urquiza. Recorre 16 provincias y se conecta con cinco pasos internacionales: Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Brasil y Uruguay. En términos logísticos cumple un rol clave para la exportación de materias primas. Su privatización volverá aún más opaco el control de los trenes argentinos atados a un modelo de país bajo la lógica de exportación de commodities.


El argumento oficial para esta medida es que, al inicio de esta gestión, la empresa presentaba una situación operativa y financiera crítica. Según

un comunicado del Gobierno

, los informes técnicos señalaron "significativas pérdidas económicas de la empresa, sumado a un deterioro importante de la infraestructura, una elevada cantidad de descarrilamientos, falta de mantenimiento cíclico y un incumplimiento de entre el 20 por ciento y el 40 por ciento del mantenimiento programado del parque tractivo durante 2023".


Foto: Ministerio del Interior.


De la inversión estatal a la privatización, el transporte para el extractivismo


Pese a las falencias señaladas, lo cierto es que el gobierno de Javier Milei realizó inversiones para sostener el transporte de cargas.

En marzo pasado

, cuando inició la cosecha gruesa (sobre todo de soja y de maíz), el Gobierno anunció la compra de 45 vagones a la empresa china CMEC, “con vistas al tráfico que generará el sector agroindustrial”. Los mismos se destinaron a la Línea Belgrano, que conecta Jujuy, Salta, San Juan, Chaco, Santiago del Estero, Santa Fe, Córdoba con los puertos de Barranqueras (Chaco), Rosario (Santa Fe) y Zárate (Buenos Aires). 


En diciembre de 2025

, el Estado invirtió un millón de dólares en tareas de infraestructura (como renovación de durmientes y mejoramiento de vías) en la Línea Urquiza, que conecta Entre Ríos, Corrientes, Misiones y Buenos Aires. El Coordinador Ejecutivo de la Unidad Técnica del Fondo para la Convergencia Estructural del Mercosur (Focem), Luciano Wexell Severo, resaltó en ese momento: “Se podrá ampliar y mejorar la capacidad de transporte de productos agrícolas, cemento y pasta de celulosa, entre otros”.

author: Rizomatica
title: Comunidad Pallaco de Tirúa denuncia violento desalojo por parte de guardias privados de forestal Minico
content:
Comunicado comunidad Pallaco, de Tirúa, denuncia que esta mañana se produjo un violento e irregular desalojo, por parte de guardias particulares de forestal Minico, quienes destruyeron viviendas con maquinaria pesada.


«En estos momentos, nosotros, como comunidad de Pallaco, estamos enfrentando una situación de máxima preocupación en nuestro territorio.


Existe una alta presencia de guardias forestales y maquinaria pesada, incluyendo retroexcavadora y camión tolva, que se encuentra interviniendo en el predio en disputa, intentando desalojar nuestra recuperación y destruyendo viviendas levantadas en el territorio.


Lo que está ocurriendo no afecta solamente a determinadas familias o viviendas. Nos afecta como comunidad en su conjunto, porque en este territorio vivimos, nos organizamos, educamos a nuestros niños y niñas, desarrollamos nuestra vida comunitaria y mantenemos nuestros espacios de encuentro, espiritualidad y ceremonia.


Hoy también están en riesgo nuestros espacios ceremoniales, lugares fundamentales para nuestra vida espiritual, nuestra cultura, nuestra memoria y nuestra relación con el territorio. Su afectación no representa solamente una pérdida material: significa intervenir espacios que poseen un profundo valor cultural y espiritual para nuestra comunidad.


Aquí también se encuentra nuestra Escuela Autónoma Mapuche Pallaco, que nace y se sostiene desde nuestra comunidad y nuestro territorio. Para nosotros, la escuela no está separada de esta realidad: es parte de nuestra vida comunitaria, de nuestra identidad, de nuestra memoria y de la transmisión de nuestros conocimientos y saberes a las nuevas generaciones.


Por ello, nuestra principal preocupación en estos momentos es resguardar la integridad de nuestros niños y niñas, nuestras familias, nuestra comunidad educativa, nuestros espacios ceremoniales y de todas las personas que permanecemos en Pallaco.


Frente a esta situación, hacemos un llamado urgente a las comunidades organizaciones sociales y a todas las personas que puedan acompañarnos, a mantenerse atentos y ayudarnos a visibilizar lo que está ocurriendo.


Defender nuestro territorio forma parte de una misma defensa: la continuidad de nuestra comunidad, nuestra cultura, nuestra espiritualidad y el derecho de nuestros niños y niñas a crecer y aprender vinculados a su territorio y a su identidad mapuche.


Hoy necesitamos que Pallaco sea escuchado, respetado y acompañado».


*Enviado a la radio


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Bianca Bortolon
title: Bolsonaristas capturam perfis nas redes para inflar apoio religioso a Mendonça
content:
Perfis no Instagram que promovem políticos bolsonaristas, como o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) e o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), passaram a atuar de forma articulada para impulsionar perfis dedicados ao ministro André Mendonça nas redes sociais em meio à crise no STF (Supremo Tribunal Federal) provocada pelo caso Master.


Um levantamento do

Aos Fatos

 identificou na rede social da Meta ao menos 24 perfis dedicados ao magistrado e promovidos por meio de publicações colaborativas e convocações para que seguidores de contas políticas de extrema-direita passassem a acompanhá-los.


Há entre esses perfis aqueles que nem mesmo foram criados originalmente para enaltecer Mendonça: ao menos dois são contas preexistentes que trocaram de nome e passaram a se dedicar exclusivamente ao magistrado em setembro, após o estopim da crise.


Essa prática é conhecida como

astroturfing

, movimento que simula um apoio popular espontâneo, mas que é, na verdade, orquestrado por grupos de interesse.


Por que isso importa?


Redes bolsonaristas atuam de forma articulada para inflar apoio a Mendonça em meio à crise no STF


O maior perfil, com 1,9 milhão de seguidores, existe desde novembro de 2024, mudou de nome oito vezes desde então e recebeu o selo de verificação do Instagram em agosto. Antes de aderir de vez a Mendonça, o perfil já republicava posts religiosos, anti-LGBTQIA+ e sobre futebol.


Reposts do perfil @andremendoncas2 demonstram que página já existia e publicava conteúdo religioso


O segundo com maior engajamento, criado em abril, mudou de nome duas vezes e, assim como o primeiro, não exibe publicações anteriores a setembro. O Instagram não informa quais eram os nomes anteriores das contas. 


A movimentação ocorre enquanto Mendonça é ungido como símbolo religioso nas redes. Entre 1º e 9 de setembro, 156 publicações analisadas pelo

Aos Fatos

 que equiparam a atuação do ministro a uma jornada do herói evangélica somaram 228 milhões de visualizações. 


Em geral, esses conteúdos pedem orações pelo magistrado, o apresentam como um “servo de Deus” e retratam sua performance no STF como se fosse uma missão divina. No entanto, não é possível determinar em que medida esse engajamento é autêntico.


Cruzada nas redes


Desde que a crise transbordou no STF, no início de setembro, o

Aos Fatos

 identificou ao menos 24 perfis dedicados a Mendonça no Instagram, que somavam 5,6 milhões de seguidores até quarta-feira (16). Destes, 12 já existiam antes da crise no STF e apenas trocaram de nome.


As contas @andremendoncas2 e @andremendoncas3, que, juntas, têm quase 3 milhões de seguidores, já existiam antes de setembro e passaram por mudanças de nome antes da identidade atual.


A @andremendoncas2, hoje com 1,9 milhão de seguidores, foi criada em novembro de 2024, mas não mantém nenhuma publicação anterior a setembro deste ano.


Apesar das mudanças, a plataforma não informa quais eram os nomes anteriores do perfil


O mesmo padrão aparece na @andremendoncas3. A conta foi criada em abril, mudou de nome duas vezes e também não exibe publicações anteriores a setembro.


Os primeiros posts atualmente disponíveis nesses perfis foram publicados em 5 e 7 de setembro. Desde então, os dois passaram a funcionar como perfis de apoio a Mendonça, compartilhando publicações quase idênticas, muitas das quais também distribuídas por outras contas identificadas no levantamento do

Aos Fatos

.


Diferentes contas publicam posts quase idênticos com o objetivo de angariar seguidores para os perfis de apoio a Mendonça


A identidade religiosa que impulsiona a mobilização aparece desde os primeiros posts disponíveis dos dois perfis. Ambos, inclusive, enganam ao associar uma

pregação feita pelo ministro em fevereiro deste ano

, durante uma conferência cristã de apoio a mães de pessoas atípicas, às discussões recentes no STF. Até esta quarta-feira (16), essas publicações acumulavam cerca de 2 milhões de visualizações.


Ministro é retratado em tom messiânico por perfis de apoio


As novas identidades das contas passaram a ser impulsionadas por perfis com audiências já consolidadas. O @nikolasferreiradms3, que usa o nome e a imagem do deputado federal mineiro, por exemplo, publicou uma chamada para que seu público seguisse a @andremendoncas2.


Aos Fatos

 identificou ainda um padrão que sinaliza a existência de uma articulação na rede social: o uso do recurso de collabs do Instagram entre esses perfis e outros dedicados a políticos …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Santa Fe: Mumalá alertó sobre el aumento de suicidios de mujeres que habían denunciado violencia de género
content:
El Observatorio Nacional Mumalá advirtió que siete de cada diez suicidios de mujeres en el país estuvieron atravesados por situaciones de violencia de género.


Escuchá el reporte de Roque Caballero desde FM Chalet. 


La provincia de Santa Fe atraviesa un escenario crítico en la materia, lo que motivó reclamos urgentes por la declaración de emergencia. Gabriela Sosa, coordinadora de Mumalá en Santa Fe, advirtió sobre la gravedad de la situación de violencia de género en la provincia y reclamó una respuesta urgente de los poderes del Estado.


“Estamos por arriba de la tasa del mundo que mide la Organización Mundial de la Salud cuando hablamos de suicidios, pero en particular a nosotras nos interesaba incorporarle la perspectiva de género, la perspectiva de derechos humanos y la perspectiva de diversidad sexual”.


Según señaló, Santa Fe registra una de las tasas de femicidios más altas del país. Desde el primero de enero del 2020 al 31 de agosto de este año se registraron 79 suicidios femicidas y un 10% que se registraron dentro del personal de seguridad.


“En el caso de las mujeres que se han suicidado, el 71% había denunciado violencia de género previa. También hay otro dato muy particular, es que el 10% pertenecía a las fuerzas de seguridad”, aseguró la coordinadora de Mumalá.


Finalizando, Sosa aseguró que están conformes con el proyecto de ley en emergencia a las violencias de genero: “Ojalá que en buena hora sea aprobado cualquier tipo de proyecto, que sea aprobada la emergencia o que sea aprobado este proyecto que presente el Ejecutivo, porque es asumir lo que nosotros estamos planteando, que estamos en una situación grave”, además, agregó que “aprobar implica un presupuesto, y si algo hacemos las feministas es estar controlando y monitoreando lo que hace el Estado”.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Hacia la masificación de agroecología: 3.000 hectáreas de arroz agroecológico
content:
Por Nahuel Lag


Traducción: Paula Veliz


La Cooperativa de Trabajadores Asentados de la Región de Porto Alegre (Cootap) lleva adelante desde Brasil una de las mayores producciones de arroz agroecológico de América Latina: 14.000 toneladas anuales en 3.000 hectáreas. La Cootap, que reúne a 600 familias nucleadas en el

Movimiento Sin Tierra (MST)

, trabaja además otras 2.000 hectáreas con producción diversificada de hortalizas, frutas, ganado para la producción lechera y piscicultura. “Somos generaciones de familias que lucharon por la tierra”, reivindica Nelson Krupinski, presidente de la Cootap.


La cooperativa no solo produce materia prima sino que agrega valor y tiene su propia marca,

Terra Livre Agroecológica

, para comercializar mermeladas, jugos y salsas de tomate, jugo de naranja, cerveza de arroz y la estrella de la cooperativa: el arroz blanco e integral. Como parte del MST, la Cootap avanza en un proceso que el movimiento campesino brasileño define como la “masificación de la agroecología”, cuenta con biofábrica, produce semillas y comenzó a tecnificar las tareas, incluyendo, la implementación de drones para aplicar los biopreparados sobre los cultivos.


La marca consolida “la convicción de que es posible producir alimentos más saludables y con mayor justicia social, valorando y preservando tanto a las personas como a los recursos naturales”. La agroecología no está solo en la ausencia del uso de agrotóxicos en la producción sino en el resto de sus dimensiones: sociales, culturales y éticas. “Trabajar la tierra, resistir por la vida”, sostienen.


Foto:  Cootap - MST Tierra Livre


Luchar por la tierra para alimentar


La historia de la Cootap es parte de la lucha por la reforma agraria en Brasil. Krupinski recuerda desde la

Guerra del Contestado

 —protagonizada por productores yerbateros y madereros del sur de Brasil entre 1912 y 1916 frente al Estado brasileño y la empresa de ferrocarriles estadounidense que los expulsó de sus tierras—, a la formación del Movimiento Sin Tierra y la consolidación de la organización a fines de la dictadura (década del 80), junto con otras fuerzas como la Comisión Pastoral de la Tierra (CPT), la Central Única de los Trabajadores (CUT) y el Partido de los Trabajadores (PT).


“Soy hijo de un pequeño agricultor. Mi padre luchó por la tierra en la década de 1990. Yo me sumé a esa lucha en el año 1999. La Cootap la integran familias asentadas entre 1992 y 2008. Dos, cuatro, seis años de campamento y ocupación del latifundio, de marchas, de presión al gobierno para conseguir la tierra”, pone en palabras una lucha que lleva años de poner el cuerpo.


Los asentamientos son la estrategia con la que los campesinos y campesinas sin tierra de Brasil hacen cumplir la “función social de la tierra”, un principio redactado en la Constitución brasileña de 1988. Bajo ese principio, la propiedad privada de la tierra no es un derecho absoluto sino que debe servir al bien común, priorizando su uso productivo y responsable por encima del mero lucro. El Instituto Nacional de Colonización y Reforma Agraria (Incra)


es el organismo que institucionalizó esa norma y está a cargo de comprar las tierras improductivas o degradadas para cederlas en concesión con destino a producción.


Las familias asentadas no son propietarias, pero tienen tierra pública para producir alimentos. Para continuar en esas tierras siempre

debe cumplirse con la función social: producir alimentos y preservar el ambiente

 sino el Estado puede reasignarlas. “La lucha por la tierra nos hizo crear una identidad de unión, de cooperación y de trabajo mutuo, de ayuda entre las personas, que es fundamental en nuestro trabajo”, cuenta Krupinski, que este año viajó fuera de Brasil, por primera vez, para visitar las

experiencias productivas de la Federación Rural

.


Foto: Rafa Dotti


Organización cooperativa para la producción


La organización de 600 familias en 35 asentamientos es un desafío cooperativo que se organiza con un representante cada cinco o quince familias productoras para representarlas en las asambleas de toma de decisiones. Cada familia cuenta con alrededor de diez hectáreas para la producción de arroz y hortalizas, en su mayoría, pero también ganado lechero, frutas y peces.


Organizar esa producción también fue un aprendizaje, cuenta Krupinski, porque las familias sin tierra eran del norte de Río Grande do Sul, donde cultivaban porotos, soja y maíz, y las tierras las consiguieron en el sur del estado …

author: La Zarzamora
title: AUTISTICI/INVENTATI (A/I) cierra – Seguir siendo humanos
content:
En cuanto descubrimos que habíamos acabado en la lista de organizaciones terroristas globales, escribimos, declaramos y prometimos que intentaríamos resistir todo lo que fuera posible, que no nos rendiríamos mientras viera alguna posibilidad legal. Hemos mantenido y defendido con orgullo una infraestructura libre, confidencial, autónoma y, sobre todo, partidista.

Para nosotras, «seguir siendo humanas» no es un simple eslogan. Significa que, ante todo, son las usuarias, las personas que construyen las redes humanas en las que nos apoyamos y las comunidades que nos han inundado de mensajes, amor y solidaridad, las que deben ser protegidas.

No podemos aceptar un enfrentamiento ni prestarnos a instrumentalizaciones que pongan en peligro sus vidas y las de sus seres queridos, dejándolas a merced de autócratas, fascistas y agencias que actúan por vías extralegales. La posibilidad concreta de poder ser la causa de consecuencias penales o financieras para alguien cercano a nosotros, o que simplemente interactúe con nosotros, no nos deja otra opción.

A/I cierra. El colectivo Autistici/Inventati cierra y suspenderá todos los servicios a corto plazo. No hay una forma fácil de decirlo ni de explicarlo.

Cada día que hemos permanecido en línea desde el 26 de agosto ha sido una victoria, pero hoy debemos detenernos. A ninguna de nosotras nos atraen los gestos heroicos y mucho menos los mártires, así que no los haremos ni los pediremos.

En este clima, seguir ofreciendo nuestros servicios solo supone un peligro más para nuestras usuarias y para todas las personas que forman parte de nuestras comunidades. En un mundo de acusaciones desligadas de los hechos, no podemos sino esperar una nueva represión desproporcionada. Esto nos enfrenta a la imposibilidad de mantener nuestro proyecto original: ofrecer herramientas seguras y no mercantilizadas.

Han sido 25 años maravillosos. Ha sido una «bonita historia». Ahora dejad el ordenador, salid, luchad, abrazáos y no perdáis la sonrisa. Porque nosotras nos detenemos. Pero la resistencia y las ideas no. Sigamos siendo humanos.

En breve explicaremos cómo guardar el contenido de los blogs, correos electrónicos, páginas web y daremos otros consejos técnicos. No obstante, tened siempre presente que, al igual que se ha cerrado sin previo aviso el dominio autistici.org, entretanto podrían surgir otros problemas de este tipo que no podemos prever.

title: ECMPOs desde adentro: Microserie muestra cómo contribuyen a generar trabajo, economía local y protección sustentable del mar
content:
El Observatorio Ciudadano lanzó recientemente la microserie documental 

«Zonas de Resguardo»

 , que muestra en video el funcionamiento de los Espacios Costeros Marinos de Pueblos Originarios (

ECMPO)

 en la Región de Los Lagos. En sus dos primeros capítulos, Comunidades como Caulín Bajo y Piedra Blanca gestionan espacios costeros para extracción sustentable de algas y captación de semillas de choritos, generando economías locales, autonomía y protección de ecosistemas.


Por: Equipo Comunicaciones Mapuche


Microserie documental revela el funcionamiento de los ECMPO desde adentro


El 

Observatorio Ciudadano

 y 

Espacios Costeros Marinos de Pueblos Originarios en Acción

 lanzaron 

«Zonas de Resguardo»

 , una microserie documental que por primera vez muestra en video los 

Espacios Costeros Marinos de Pueblos Originarios (ECMPO)

 aprobados y en funcionamiento en la Región de Los Lagos.


A través de cuatro capítulos de cinco minutos, la serie recorre espacios costeros gestionados por comunidades indígenas, revelando historias de convivencia cotidiana, economías locales y protección biocultural, desafiando la narrativa de que los ECMPO frenan el crecimiento y no permiten el desarrollo.


ECMPO Caulín Bajo: ciencia y tradición para el repoblamiento de algas


En el sector de 

Caulín Bajo, Chiloé

 , la comunidad gestiona un ECMPO donde han desarrollado un laboratorio para la reproducción de algas. 

Patricia Yohana Avendaño Gallardo

 , integrante de la comunidad, explica:

«

Nosotros con mi colega no teníamos idea sobre el crecimiento y el desarrollo de Sargazo. De hecho ahora nos reímos porque somos casi técnicos especialistas en Sargazo. Siempre lo digo, me siento haciendo ciencia

«.

Su testimonio refleja cómo la gestión del ECMPO ha permitido a las comunidades adquirir conocimientos técnicos y científicos.


El ECMPO Caulín ha permitido que la comunidad se involucre en la extracción de algas de manera sustentable

. «

Caulín siempre se ha destacado por trabajar el alga. Para muchas familias el sustento de sus hogares

«

, señala Avendaño. La comunidad ha implementado un sistema de repoblamiento de sargazo (huiro flotador), utilizando un laboratorio para producir esporas y plantarlas en el fondo marino, generando un bosque submarino que sustenta la biodiversidad y la producción de recursos pesqueros.


«

El cuidado del mar para la próxima generación es importante porque es un legado que le dejamos a nuestras futuras generaciones. La posibilidad de vivir el mar

«,

 afirma Avendaño. La comunidad ha entendido que el sargazo no es un estorbo, sino un ecosistema clave:

«

Sin ese sargazo en el espacio donde está sería imposible tener producción. Que ellos no podrían tener algunos recursos que se alimentan y viven en ese espacio

«

. La visión de la comunidad es expandir el laboratorio: «

Soñamos en algún momento en poder vender nuestras esporitas y generar dinero para la gente, para la comunidad

«.


ECMPO Piedra Blanca: captación de semillas y autonomía territorial


En el sector de 

Piedra Blanca, Quellón

 , el werken 

Alex Mansilla

 describe cómo la comunidad ha desarrollado la captación de semillas de choritos.

 «

Todo parte que es algo natural. Que se da porque hay un banco natural. Acá estamos sobre el banco natural. Que nos proporciona a nosotros el alimento también de los choritos

«

, explica. La técnica consiste en colocar mallas recicladas en el mar para captar las semillas que se pegan naturalmente, luego esas semillas se venden a empresas de engorda de choritos, generando un ingreso económico para la comunidad y permitendo que la región de Los Lagos sea el segundo productor mundial de choritos..


Mansilla destaca que el ECMPO ha permitido a la comunidad mantener sus actividades tradicionales:

«

El aporte más grande que hace un espacio costero (ECMPO) en un territorio es que la gente, por ejemplo, pueda seguir haciendo sus usos consuetudinarios de muchos años

«. La ley, enfatiza, fue creada «

pensando en los territorios y en las comunidades que se mantengan y sigan teniendo sus formas de vida

«.


«

Parte de los espacios costeros es eso, entregar autonomía a la gente, que la gente vuelva a tener una actividad económica en su territorio

«

, sostiene Mansilla. La comunidad de Piedra Blanca valora la posibilidad de seguir con sus tradiciones:

 «

Yo veo a mi familia mariscar, mis sobrinos mariscar en el mar. Yo quiero que mis hijos también hagan lo mismo. Que hagan lo …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Will the National Contact Point System Help Resolve Wrongdoing by Taiwanese Companies Abroad?
content:
AT THE START of this month, Taiwanese and Indonesian groups submitted the first complaint to the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) under the new National Contact Point (NCP) complaint system. As the name implies, the system designates the MOEA as the place where complaints about wrongdoings by Taiwanese companies internationally should be directed. Nevertheless, the Taiwanese government was criticized for announcing that the MOEA would serve as Taiwan’s NCP in September 2024, but delaying its actual rollout.

A number of criticisms from Indonesian groups centered around Taiwanese companies in the environmentally destructive nickel mining industry. Among the groups present were Action for Ecology and People Emancipation, the FSPIM Morowali Labour Union, as well as Fagawene, a local organization based out of the Weda Bay Area.

Nickel mining is a highly carbon-intensive endeavor, and it is reliant on coal-burning power plants. In addition to air pollution, wastewater discharge has led to coral deaths. This has damaged fishing grounds, killed coral reefs, and impacted river and lake ecosystems in Sagea. Tourist sites such as the Boki Maruru Cave have also been put at risk of irreversible damage. Deforestation affects residential areas, worsening issues of flooding while depriving local communities of access to clean water.

Likewise, safety practices were criticized as lacking for workers. Apart from dangerous accidents, workers have not been provided with dust collection equipment and personal protective gear, even in smelting facilities. Furthermore, facilities are poorly ventilated.

The Taiwanese government was called on to comply with international mechanisms in accepting the complaint, as well as implementing the NCP system. The Taiwanese civil society groups present, which included the Taiwan Association for Human Rights and Taiwan Labour Front, suggested that a failure to take action would worsen Taiwan’s international image. The MOEA was criticized, however, for still failing to disclose the details of the complaint review process, as well as for delays in releasing the National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights at a time when Taiwanese companies such as Giant Bicycle have fallen afoul of a Withhold Release Order in the US over forced labor allegations.

In this sense, Taiwanese companies and the government were called on to undertake responsible corporate diligence in line with international standards. But it may not be surprising if one continues to see the government continue to drag its feet, acting to defend corporate interests instead of calling them to account.

author: rti_admin
title: Bablai Mata Yatra: How Does Development Politics Affect Madia Culture?
content:
For the Madia Adivasi community in the Bhamragad region, the Bablai Mata Yatra (pilgrimage/fair) is not just a religious pilgrimage but a living symbol of cultural, environmental, and constitutional rights.

However, in recent times, the politics of development, religious conversion, the administration, and Naxalism have begun to significantly impact the Bablai Yatra.

For the Madia Adivasi community in the Bhamragad area, the Bablai Mata Yatra is not merely a religious fair but a living symbol of their cultural, environmental, and constitutional rights. Every year, thousands of Madia Adivasi people from the Bhamragad tract come together to worship Bablai Mata and to renew their generations-old culture, traditions, and relationship with nature. Yet, in the name of development, the pilgrimage of Bablai Devi is slowly disappearing.

According to Adivasi tradition, Bablai was the sister of a man named Morka. Bablai was married to Thakur Dev, who is still worshipped at a shrine on Surjagad today. After their marriage, Thakur Dev went to Surjagad for a second wife, but Bablai did not go away with her people. She stayed in this region, remained among the people here, and became one with this land and forest.

The locals say that their faith was born from this sacrifice:

She left her husband for us, but she never left us, and that is why she is a goddess for us.

Today, Bablai Mata is the presiding deity of Adivasis across the Bhamragad region. This story is not found in written form, but this tradition has been carried forward from generation to generation through the words of the ancestors.

Traditional Governance: Bhoom Perma, Bhoomiya, and Kathdi

The Bablai Yatra is not only about worshipping the deity; it is also where the traditional self-governance system of the Adivasis becomes visible. The highest position in this system is “Bhoom Perma” (in simple terms, the “President” of this traditional system). The Bhoomiya (or Bhoom Bhoomiya) is considered the owner and protector of that place. There are also traditional office bearers like Bhoom, Kotwal, and Kathdi (village-level customary officials). This group consists of around 22 members and includes active participation of women. Together, they handle the worship of Bablai Mata, management of the Yatra, decision-making processes, and the entire religious and cultural programme. In essence, this structure is the local expression of the gram sabha (village assembly), self-governance, and collective decision-making. The Adivasi community believes that Bablai Mata protects all the water, forests, and land in the region. Therefore, the central focus of the Yatra is not only religious rituals but a spiritual relationship with nature.

People from many villages in the Bhamragad area come together to clean the sacred groves in the forest, consider trees, water bodies, and hills as deities, and follow a code of conduct that ensures no harm to nature.

Law, Constitution, and Cultural Protection

Before 2013, the Bablai festival was not celebrated in this form. Even after Independence, the influence of the princely state remained here. After India became independent, the kings of the Aheri State used to visit this tract. People here worshipped them like Brahma Dev — falling at their feet, washing their feet, and serving them through performances like dancing by women performers. The kings would come once or twice a year and enjoy such festivities. This practice continued until about fifteen to twenty years ago. People used to come to Bejur village only for Bablai Mata’s darshan (sacred viewing/audience with the deity).

Later, local scholar-youth took the initiative and made people aware that before Independence they were subjects of the British, and that after Independence the Constitution abolished the princely order. They formed a traditional Kuthul committee (customary coordinating body) in the Bhamragad belt and, by bringing all gram sabhas together, decided that they would gather right here and organise Bablai Mata’s traditional worship and a traditional convention in a proper way. Along with this, all the gram sabhas in the Bhamragad area began discussing the Forest Rights Act and PESA. The Yatra thus became not only a cultural symbol for the Madia community but also a space for public awareness.

Social activist Chinu Mahaka from Bhamragad says that “when the Bablai Yatra began in this way, all the gram sabhas started coming together, and they began discussing the …

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Gov’t urged to respect right to protest vs. Pax Silica
content:
Police arresting paralegal Mara Peralta (left) and Agham member Jona Yang. (Photo by Pinoy Weekly)

MANILA – The people have the right to protest.

Progressive groups asserted this after authorities arrested five paralegals who responded during the September 10 protest at the Grand Hyatt Manila, where the Luzon Economic Corridor forum was held, attended by 600 foreign investors, industry leaders, and government officials.

The arrested paralegals were released on bail on September 12.

In particular, human rights group Karapatan criticized Presidential Spokesperson Claire Castro’s statement that those who oppose Pax Silica should course their objections through “proper channels,” claiming that “proper protest uses reason and intelligence.”

Philippine National Police Chief General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., meanwhile, said that the right to protest must remain “within the bounds of the law” and urged cause-oriented groups to raise their concerns through “lawful means.”

Karapatan maintained that the arrests were unlawful and arbitrary and impeded the peoples’ right to protest.

“It is the State that carries out unlawful and arbitrary arrests through Marcosian laws such as Batas Pambansa 880. Whose interests are you protecting, that of the people or that of big business who will benefit from the Pax Silica?” Karapatan Secretary-General Cristina Palabay said in a statement.

Batas Pambansa 880 is also known as the Public Assembly Act, a relic of the dictatorship of Ferdinand Marcos Sr., used against activists and community leaders for expressing their grievances and dissent to the government.

Karapatan’s three paralegals — Jona Yang, Kenneth Castro, and Mara Peralta — were arrested during the dispersal and brought to the Tuktukan Police Station. While two other paralegals, Daya Juliano and RC Placido, were arrested while providing legal assistance to the 3 arrested paralegals.

“The President recognizes the freedom of expression. But not in a manner that could cause harm or potentially lead to violence. If they have something they wish to convey regarding the Pax Silica issue, the government agency concerned with the Pax Silica project is open to hearing their concerns,” Castro said in Filipino.

In reaction, Palabay said, “The right to protest is not conditional on whether the government approves of what people are saying. People have the right to dissent, to oppose government policies, to expose their consequences and to demand accountability. People’s rights do not become suspended whenever the President is courting foreign investors.”

The LEC Investment Forum was organized by the United States, Philippines, and Japan, convening 600 investors. The site of Pax Silica is in New Clark City, positioned as the anchor of the LEC connecting Subic Bay, Clark, Manila, and Batangas.

Center for Environmental Concerns, an environmental research institution, noted that the project will require not only 5 million gallons of water for cooling and other operations, but also displace an estimated 20,000 Aeta indigenous peoples.

Amnesty International Philippines also condemned the police violence. “Almost without exception, this wave of mass protest has been met with obstructive, repressive and often violent responses by state authorities. Instead of facilitating the right to protest, this government is going at greater lengths to quash it.”

On September 11, the police reportedly disrupted the protest caravan against LEC and Pax Silica by conducting arbitrary checkpoints in Pampanga and Tarlac. The security personnel of New Clark City also blocked the protest at the entrance of the former US Clark Base.

The police also filed a case against three individuals, including Bayan Chairperson Teddy Casiño. For Bayan, these tactics mirror the Martial Law tactics used to silence the activists during the dictatorship of Ferdinand Marcos Sr.

“The police violence and Malacañang’s response are reminiscent of the tactics used during Martial Law to quell protests. They highlight the government’s desperation to undermine the people’s rising dissatisfaction against the worsening poverty and corruption, while Marcos and his cronies are treasonously promoting the imperialist agenda of their US patrons,” Bayan said in a statement,

The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) also announced that it will deploy 15,000 personnel in the upcoming Martial Law commemoration on September 21. (AMU, DAA)

title: Contribution to the 2026 International Ecumenical Peace Convocation Seoul, Republic of Korea
content:
Contribution to the 2026 International Ecumenical Peace Convocation Seoul, Republic of Korea 09 September 2026

Cristina Palabay KARAPATAN Secretary General

Good day to everyone, and thank you for having us in the panel.

The Philippines is in a seemingly chronic state of crisis as far as human and people’s rights are concerned. The violations of human rights and international humanitarian law are systematic and systemic, which means that these are deliberate acts, which were planned methodically, instigated and funded by State authorities and actors, and that these are borne out of a system that breeds and maintains injustice, despite the Philippine government’s accession or ratification of almost all international covenants on human rights.

From the Marcos dictatorship in the 1970’s to the current Marcos the son’s administration, government campaigns pertaining to the most-often used bywords of “national security,” “peace and order,” “peace and development,” “human security,” and others have been used to justify and legitimize the gravest atrocities and the most brutal and inhumane crimes against humanity.

Filipinos are still reeling from the sham drug war of former President Rodrigo Duterte which resulted in the mass murder of more than 30,000 citizens accused of peddling or using drugs, including more than 300 children and minors who were considered “collateral damage.” The killings, conducted in the name of “peace and order,” were done during legitimate police operations or by so-called vigilante or gun-for-hire groups, but the rhetoric of Duterte made it worse – the policy made more forceful and palpable by direct statements of the former president to kill, kill, kill and his guarantees of immunity.

Under Marcos the son, the killings continue with more than a thousand people killed, according to the UP Third World Studies Center Dahas Project. Arbitrary listing of drug users or peddlers continue at the village level, and the police memoranda issued by Duterte were never rescinded, and are thus effectively enforced to this day.

Violations of human rights and international humanitarian remain unabated, Marcos the son continues the counter-insurgency programs of his predecessors.

KARAPATAN has documented 147 individuals killed by the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police since July 2022, while attempted murder of 87 individuals was also recorded. Majority of the victims were poor peasants, who were publicly portrayed as armed rebels, even if their families and communities attest to the fact that they weren’t combatants.

Among those recently killed were nine civilians, including a journalist, youth organizers, and Filipino-American activists, in Negros Occidental, together with ten hors de combat. The Negros 19 as they are referred to were killed in broad daylight, in a fishpond where they had nowhere to escape to. The incident is the fourth case of massacre in the island of Negros – an island whose vast tracts of productively agricultural lands are owned by the country’s biggest landlords, while generations of peasants have tilled lands which were taken from them and when they take seasonal work, they get paid with slave wages.

Also killed were Kuni Cuba, a 16-year old student from an indigenous tribe, while he was chanced upon by soldiers when they were walking home from a community event; 16-year old Everly Kee Jacolbe who was killed with her mother and a family friend at their home in Negros Oriental; and a 4-year old boy and his 11-year old brother who were killed with their peasant activist parents in their home in Negros Occidental.

None of these killings have been thoroughly investigated by government agencies, and no perpetrator among the State forces have been made accountable.

This pattern is similar to the acts of abduction and enforced disappearances documented by KARAPATAN. Currently, there are 16 victims of enforced disappearances who remain missing to this date. This includes environmental advocates, women’s rights activists, and peace consultants. There were those who were abducted and then surfaced, and they testified that those who captured them and kept them incommunicado from their loved ones and lawyers were the soldiers. None of these enforced disappearances have been thoroughly investigated by government agencies, and no perpetrator among the State forces have been made accountable.

author: groundxero
title: ‘This Land Is Ours’: North Bengal Convention Demands Land Rights for Tea Workers, Adivasis and the Poor
content:
A convention held in North Bengal has called for a united movement against the continuing denial of land rights to tea workers, Adivasis, forest villagers, bustee residents and other working-class communities across the region.


 


Groundxero Desk


SEP 13, 2026


 


More than 100 people representing 10 organisations came together at the Convention on Land Rights of the People of North Bengal’s Tea-Growing Region, demanding an end to a land regime that, they said, has consistently protected the interests of tea garden owners and other powerful interests while leaving generations of workers without secure rights over the land on which they live and work.


 


Speakers at the convention included Rajkumar Kashyap of United Forum for Adivasi Rights (Terai), Ashish Kujur of Ulgulan Bharat Adivasi Ekta Manch (Nagrakata), Abhijit Nag of AICARD (Kalchini), scholar Neh Indwar, Rabi Rabha of Uttar Banga Jan Van Shramajivi Manch, Mohar Ali Mondalof Bhukha Manusher Adhikar Abhijan (North 24 Parganas), Rahul Barman of Paschim Banga Khet Majoor Samity (Cooch Behar), and Parimal Oraon of Rajipahra Prathna Sabha (Madarihat). Babul Lama and AnuradhaTalwar spoke from Paschim Banga Chai Majdoor Samity (PBCMS).


 


The convention underlined a fundamental contradiction in North Bengal’s tea economy: the labour of generations has sustained the tea industry, but the people who produced its wealth remain effectively landless. The state has protected the rights of tea garden owners while leaving generations of workers without rights to the homes they occupy and the land they have cultivated for decades.

 


 


‘Stop the acquisition of Torsa land’


 


The convention expressed solidarity with the people of Torsa, who have been resisting the acquisition of their ancestral land for the proposed Jaigaon Land Port.


 


The convention demanded an immediate halt to the proposed acquisition of 22 acres of land belonging to the people of Torsa. Instead, it called upon the government to resume 20 acres of unused and vacant Torsa tea-garden land located across the road.


 


The question raised at the convention was pointed: why should the land of people who have lived there for generations be taken when tea-garden land lying unused is available?


 


The meeting began with 15 members of the Torsa Bagan Zameen Bachao Samity, led by Miriam, formally releasing a fact-finding report on the threatened displacement. The report was prepared by Professor Virginius Xaxa, Siraj Dutta and Anupradha Singh. Participants also heard an account of the community’s more than two-month-long struggle, while advocate Tamalika Bera provided an update on the public interest litigation filed by Paschim Banga Chai Majdoor Samity (PBCMS) in the High Court.


 


A region-wide land crisis


 


The convention placed the Torsa struggle within a much wider history of land dispossession in North Bengal.


 


Tea workers were brought to the region as indentured labour and settled in labour lines. In many cases, they were also given land on which to cultivate food as part of their wages. Yet neither the colonial government nor successive governments after Independence recognised their rights over the land they occupied and cultivated.


 


Instead, according to the convention, the State continued to protect the leasehold interests of tea garden owners while treating workers’ claims to land as though they did not exist.


 


That historic injustice is now being intensified by the expansion of tourism and urbanisation. The Convention noted that with the development of tourism and Siliguri city, workers in gardens in Terai and the hills were facing accelerated dispossession.


 


The crisis, however, extends beyond the tea gardens. Forest villagers continue to face eviction despite the Forest Rights Act. Bustee settlements that have existed for decades remain without secure land rights. Rapid urbanisation has carried the struggle into towns such as Jaigaon, Birpara, Nagrakata, Metelli and Mal, where many residents and landholders still lack secure rights over their land.


 


Speakers also raised land conflicts along the India-Bangladesh border and in Madarihat, pointing to a wider problem: even possession of land documents does not necessarily protect people from the threat of dispossession without meaningful consultation.


 


The Convention also very strongly said that the government cannot continue taking land from the poor for the benefit of the powerful. The …

title: Sleeper-Cell Report July 2026 – Global Coalition reports 0 confirmed ISIS attacks
content:
An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside


 


Key Points


– Six sleeper-cell attacks recorded by RIC, but the Global Coalition claims 0 attacks were officially claimed by ISIS


– One military personnel was killed, and a further five injured


– A minimum of seven alleged ISIS members were arrested


– A total of 36 civilians were injured, two killed


– An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in Deir ez-Zor


–

Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS mercenaries repatriated from Roj camp


 


In-Depth


In July of 2026, RIC

recorded six sleeper-cell attacks which some publications have attributed to ISIS, according to


North Press Agency

 one of these attacks was claimed by ISIS whereas the


Global Coalition


reported that July was the first month since the territorial defeat of ISIS in 2019, where they claimed 0 attacks. Also this month at least 7 members of ISIS cells were arrested.


On July 7, Bombings struck central Damascus near the Ministry of Tourism and the Four Seasons Hotel, during the visit of Macron the president of France to Syria. Ministry of Interior has attributed the attack to ISIS, the bombing resulted in the killing of one civilian and injury of 36.


On July 8, three attacks happened during the same day and the are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.

Unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle used machine guns to target an oil truck in Abrahyah town in eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, killing the driver.


Similarly, unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle, attacked a checkpoint of the Internal Security Forces near al-Baserah city bridge.


According to North Press Agency, also on July 8 ISIS

claimed responsibility for the killing of Rashad Khalaf al-Ghurair in the northern countryside of Deir ez-Zor.


On July 15,

unknown gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire on a member of the 72nd Division on the road linking al-Arimah and Manbij in eastern Aleppo countryside, injuring the him.


On July 18,

two unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire directly on member of the Defence Ministry


near al-Awsajli junction in eastern Manbij city.


On July 9,

Syria’s Interior Ministry announced its security forces had dismantled several ISIS cells in southern Syria, arresting a senior leader and several members accused of involvement in assassinations and financing terror.


On July 28,

Syrian Internal Security Forces and the General Intelligence Service in Aleppo announced the arrest of individuals allegedly affiliated with the ISIS, during a security operation in Aleppo and its surrounding countryside.


An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, in an incident that sparked widespread concern among residents.


During July, Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS were repatriated from


Roj Camp, which houses families of ISIS members, and returned to Tunisia. Additionally, Tunisian citizen Bilal Chawachi was sentenced to 55 years in prison after being convicted on terrorism-related charges, specifically traveling to Syria and fighting alongside the extremist organization.


Germany sentenced an Iraqi man to life imprisonment and his former wife to nine years and six months in prison after convicting them of enslaving and torturing two Yazidi girls while they were members of ISIS in Syria and Iraq between 2015 and 2017.


Three U.S. citizens pleaded guilty to terror charges, prosecutors said the defendants communicated through encrypted messaging applications between July and November 2025 and planned to travel to Turkey before crossing into Syria to join ISIS. 


* Due to the low rate of confirmed ISIS attacks RIC has decided to stop publishing monthly sleeper-cell reports and instead share a bi-annual summary of ISIS activity throughout Syria.

author: Unknown
title: Temelli: We need a new vision of socialism and the economy
content:
The Kurdish Political Movement has recently been discussing communes and the communal economy in the context of the municipalities it has won and the economic programme it has developed. A series of conferences have been organised under the slogan “Municipalities are communes, communes are municipalities”, most recently the “Democratic Economy and Economic Organisation Workshop”, organised by the Democratic Regions Party (DBP) in Amed (Diyarbakır).


Work led by the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and the DBP has focused on how the commune system and communal economy can be put into practice, as well as the role of local governments and economic organisation within this model.


Sezai Temelli, DEM Party MP for Muş (Mûş), spoke to ANF about the work on communes and the communal economy and their broader significance.


Real socialism failed to transform capitalist modernity’s production model


Temelli said real socialism had failed to transform the production model of capitalist modernity, arguing that merely changing the ownership of capital was not enough.


Temelli said: “At the heart of capitalist modernity’s approach to production lies the accumulation of capital. Capital can only increase in value through surplus value, and an ever-expanding model of production makes greater exploitation and colonialism necessary in the pursuit of ever greater surplus value. We are talking about a complex system of capitalist modernity that grows for the sake of growth and accumulates for the sake of accumulation, subjugates labour and nature, shapes the public sphere in order to mould social and political formations accordingly, and structures the state, particularly the nation-state and its globalised relations.


Socialism is a counter-system that seeks to liberate labour, nature and life from this subjugation and system of exploitation. Looking at the long history of modernity, the socialist struggle developed on this basis, albeit through different approaches. Yet looking back from where we stand today, socialist modernity, or real socialism, unfortunately failed to transform the production model of capitalist modernity. Simply changing who owned the capital was not enough.


We may express our criticisms through concepts such as state capitalism, bureaucratic socialism and many other definitions, but ultimately the failure to change the production model meant that relations of surplus value and social formations could not be transformed either, and the expected results were not achieved. This is a highly complex debate. Looking at this history helps us understand today’s world much more clearly. Capitalist modernity, together with its nation-state and global system, continues to produce catastrophe for humanity through exploitation, colonialism, wars and destruction. Humanity is still searching for liberation.”


A new future requires a new vision of socialism


Temelli stressed that humanity’s search for liberation is embodied in the principle of “insisting on socialism means insisting on being human.” 


Temelli continued: “This search for liberation undoubtedly develops through the thinking embodied in the words, ‘To insist on socialism is to insist on being human.’ But a new future requires a new understanding of socialism and the economy. The communal economy is also an expression of this search. We are talking about an approach in which those who produce also govern, which prioritises the flourishing of life rather than the accumulation of capital, encompasses all structures of society, exists in harmony with nature, and organises against all relations of domination and mechanisms of exploitation. We are thinking and working towards the political economy of this new socialism.


As the DEM Party, we have developed a transition programme, a democratic economy programme based on the perspective of communal economy, for an anti-capitalist economy that is neither statist nor reproduces the existing system. As we advance our Third Way Strategy from the present towards the future, our priority is an approach that struggles for the transformation of political economy, takes social organisation as its basis, resists the pressures of the present and seeks to transform them. But we are not idealists detached from reality. As we pursue our aspirations, we do not neglect an analysis of concrete conditions.

author: Roy Barbosa
title: ‘DOLE, itigil ang drama! Wage increase, ipatupad na!” – KMU
content:
Sa halip na ipatupad ang umiiral na NCR Wage Order No. 27 na inilabas ng Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board-National Capital Region noong Hunyo 23, naglabas ng panibagong Wage Order No. 28 na nagbawas sa dapat sanang dagdag-sahod ng mga manggagawa mula P85 tungong P60.

Ayon sa WO 27, ang P85 na dagdag-sahod ay ilalabas sa magkahiwalay na tranche: P60 simula Hulyo 25 ng kasalukuyang taon at P25 simula Enero 20 sa susunod na taon. Mismong si Department of Labor and Employment Secretary Francis N. Tolentino ang nagsabing tinatayang 1.1 milyong minimum-wage earners ang makakabenepisyo sa naturang dagdag-sahod.

Ngunit sinuspinde naman ang pagpapatupad nito kaugnay sa temporary restraining order (TRO) at kalaunan ay writ of preliminary injunction mula sa Pasig Regional Trial Court bunsod ng mga petisyon mula sa Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. at R-II Builders.

Iginigiit ng Defend Jobs Philippines na mahalagang tingnan ang lawak ng operasyon ng mga kumpanyang kumukuwestiyon sa wage increase, partikular ang Readycon Trading and Construction Corp.

Ang Readycon Trading & Construction Corp. ay isang construction company na nasa industriya mula pa noong 1988. Kabilang sa mga serbisyo nito ang asphalt paving, highway construction, ready-mix asphalt at concrete, construction materials at equipment rental. Mayroon din itong AAAA classification sa ilalim ng Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board (PCAB), ang pinakamataas na contractor category sa bansa.

Kabilang sa mga pribado nitong kliyente ang Ayala Corporation, Bell Construction, C&F Construction, I.M. Construction, Hony Trading & Construction, Red Matrix Builders, Persan Construction at Sta. Clara, bukod sa iba pa. Mayroon din itong mga concrete supply project para sa Meralco Industrial Engineering Services Corporation, Super Globe at Frankhaus International Corporation. Kabilang din sa government clients at projects nito ang mga kontrata para sa Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) at Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA).

Sa mga rekord ng MIAA, nakalistang winning contractor ang Readycon para sa Rapid Exit Taxiways – Civil Works na nagkakahalaga ng P212.802 milyon; Repair and Maintenance of Asphalt Pavement na P50 milyon; Repair and Upgrading of Taxiway Hotel and Charlie na P881.415 milyon; at Repair and Overlay of Runway 06/24 – Civil Works na P540.783 milyon.

Kung pagsasamahin, nasa humigit-kumulang P1.685 bilyon ang listed contract value ng apat na proyekto.

Bukod pa, naging contractor din ang Readycon sa rehabilitation ng J.W. Diokno Boulevard na may contract amount na P185.26 milyon para sa asphalt overlay ng pangunahing kalsada noong 2024. Sa sumunod na taon naman, isang DPWH project sa Antipolo na nagkakahalaga ng P37.98 milyon ang may Readycon bid para sa installation ng safety roller barrier system sa kahabaan ng Sumulong Highway. Idineklara itong lowest calculated responsive bid at inirekomenda para sa award sa kumpanya.

Para sa DJP, hindi sapat na tingnan lamang ang labor cost bilang dagdag na gastos ng employer; anila, dapat ding suriin ang kapasidad ng mga kumpanyang nagbibigay ng serbisyo sa mga proyektong nagkakahalaga ng daan-daang milyon o bilyun-bilyong piso na magbigay ng mas mataas na sahod sa mga manggagawa.

“Kung ang isang kumpanya ay may kakayahang humawak ng mga proyektong nagkakahalaga ng daan-daang milyon at bilyun-bilyong piso…BAKIT ANG ₱60 DAGDAG-SAHOD ANG KAILANGANG ISAKRIPISYO? Hindi natin sinasabing libre ang business operations. Hindi natin sinasabing ang project value ay profit. Ang sinasabi natin: MAY GASTOS ANG PRODUKSYON. At kasama sa produksyon ang paggawa ng manggagawa,” ani DJP.

Kung pagbabatayan ang P60 mula sa unang tranche ng WO No. 27 at ang tinatayang 1.1 milyong minimum-wage earners sa NCR, nasa humigit-kumulang P2.1 bilyon ang halaga ng dagdag-sahod na hindi pa natatanggap ng mga manggagawa batay sa tinatayang 32 araw na dapat sana itong naipatupad.

Sa kabilang banda, giit ng Defend Jobs Philippines maging ng iba’t ibang grupo ng mga manggagawa ang kagyat na pagbibigay ng umento sa sahod na hindi nakabinbin sa sinasabing “tranches”.

“Ang P85 dagdag-sahod sa ilalim ng Wage Order No. 27 ay hindi dapat nakabitin. Hindi ito pabor. Mas lalong hindi ito limos. Ito ay bunga ng pakikibaka ng manggagawa at dapat nang ipatupad!” pahayag ng Defend Jobs Philippines.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Taiwan Hits Out at Chinese Checkbook Diplomacy, Even as Also Engaging In It
content:
ACCORDING TO TAIWANESE national security officials, leaked Chinese government documents show the extent to which China engages in checkbook diplomacy.

Specifically, in an interview with the Liberty Times, National Security advisor Alex Huang comments on documents that purport to show Beijing offered Micronesia 1 million yuan–subsidizing the purchase of a vehicle. This was reportedly in exchange for blocking Taiwan’s participation in the World Health Organization.

Other documents in the leaked tranche of documents appear to show China’s influence over African Union countries. The documents apparently show that the African Union accepted 200 million yuan in a “renovation grant” from China, but sought further funding in order to upgrade its headquarters, to the tune of 50 million USD.

Efforts by China to constrain Taiwan’s diplomatic influence in Africa have become increasingly visible, especially after a trip to Eswatini by President Lai Ching-te for the 40th anniversary of King Mswati III’s accession to the throne was canceled at the last minute. This was because the Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar revoked overflight privileges for Lai’s aircraft at the last minute, though Lai later traveled to Eswatini aboard Mswati III’s personal plane at a later date.

Likewise, Taiwanese participants were blocked from attending a United Nations conference on the ocean in June, with delegates detained and held for over 20 hours and their passports confiscated. Morocco has begun to suspend the issuing of visas to Taiwanese, while there have also been cases reported in Uganda of Taiwanese having their passports confiscated. To this extent, the cancellation of RightsCon in Zambia in July is thought to have occurred due to the planned participation of Taiwanese delegates, who were expected to make comments critical of China.

Still, one notes that Taiwan itself frequently participates in checkbook diplomacy. Eswatini is, for example, an absolute monarchy that Taiwan financially backs in spite of its repressive regime–in which King Mswati III presides over a country in which the constitution is suspended, democratic elections are forbidden, and dissent is put down by force. There have also been other cases in which Taiwan provided financial support to authoritarian regimes in return for recognition, such as Honduras, and a number of other cases.

Nevertheless, Taiwan cannot outspend China, as a result of which it has become increasingly common for Taiwan’s diplomatic allies to switch recognition to China in past years. Likewise, in consideration of that Taiwan is larger than all of its diplomatic allies in terms of the size of its economy and population; for small countries, China is the larger market. In the cases highlighted by Huang, these were also mostly countries that Taiwan does not have diplomatic relations with, but which China does.

On the whole, there is little domestic awareness that Taiwan’s diplomatic allies are mostly such countries with checkered human rights records, and if the Taiwanese government has often hit out at China’s diplomatic checkbook, many Taiwanese are unaware of similar actions by Taiwan. It remains to be seen if this will change.

author: rti_admin
title: The Haldwani Purification Ritual and the Untouchability of Presence: Caste, Purity and the Politics of Belonging
content:
Two days after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a public rally at Haldwani’s Ramlila Maidan in Uttarakhand on August 8, a shuddhikaran havan was conducted at the same venue. Members of the Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas Sangathan performed the ritual to purify the site. The organisation cited the slogans raised at the rally and Kharge’s criticism of the BJP and RSS as its justification for the ceremony. But a political disagreement does not make a public space impure, and it certainly does not justify cleansing a venue after it has been used by a person from the Dalit community. The act reproduced the caste logic of purity and pollution that lies at the heart of untouchability. Kharge subsequently raised the matter in the Rajya Sabha, calling it an experience of untouchability and humiliation and seeking action under the law.

The incident should be called what it is: an expression of caste-based untouchability. The fact that the organisers offered a political justification does not erase the social meaning of the act. A public space was subjected to a ritual of purification after a political event addressed by a person from the Dalit community. In a society where Dalit communities have historically been treated as polluting and subjected to exclusion on that basis, such a ritual reproduces an idea that should have no place in a democratic society. Political disagreement can be answered with argument, protest, or criticism. It cannot justify treating a space as impure because of who has occupied it.

Purification is never simply about cleanliness. It establishes a boundary between what is considered pure and what is considered impure. In the caste order, this distinction has historically been imposed upon human beings themselves. Certain communities were treated as closer to ritual purity, while others were placed at the bottom of the hierarchy and treated as polluting. Their touch, presence and proximity were regulated accordingly. The Haldwani incident brings this logic into a contemporary public space. A person from the Dalit community addressed a political gathering, and the venue was subsequently subjected to a purification ritual. The symbolism is unmistakable: something associated with the event was treated as requiring cleansing. When such a ritual follows the presence of a person from a community historically subjected to notions of pollution, it reproduces the very social imagination that sustains untouchability. This is why the incident deserves criticism not merely as an act of political provocation, but as an act that reproduces caste hierarchy. It is not necessary for the organisers to explicitly announce that Kharge’s caste was the reason for the purification for the caste meaning of the act to matter. Caste often survives through symbols, rituals and practices whose social meaning is inherited from a much longer history. The caste system does not merely divide society into communities. It ranks those communities. The distinction between purity and pollution has historically provided one of the mechanisms through which this ranking is maintained. It determines who can enter certain spaces, who can share food and water, whose touch is acceptable, whose presence is welcome, and whose presence must be kept at a distance.

The most disturbing feature of this system is that impurity is attached to birth. A person is not treated as impure because of an individual action but because of the caste into which they were born. Caste therefore turns social difference into inherited hierarchy and makes inequality appear natural.

Untouchability is the most brutal expression of this logic. It transforms the body into a marker of social status. The question is no longer simply who a person is as an individual, but what caste the person’s body is understood to represent. When a public space is purified after a person from the Dalit community has occupied it, the act invokes this same logic. It suggests that the presence of a particular social body has altered the status of the space. That is the caste imagination that must be confronted.

The distinction between the sacred and the profane provides another way to understand why purification is so significant. Societies create boundaries around what they consider sacred, pure, and worthy of protection. The problem begins when these boundaries are transferred from objects and rituals to human beings. Caste has historically transformed this distinction …
