author: Deaglan Godwin
title: Another property developer collapses. We need to abolish them entirely
content:
The collapse of Bathla Group, a multi-billion-dollar property developer, illustrates how broken housing is in Australia.

Bathla entered voluntary administration in late August after it could no longer repay almost $3.4 billion in debt. Its collapse has left hundreds of workers unpaid and unemployed, and hundreds of buyers in limbo. The company owes millions to subcontractors and suppliers.

Bathla made immense profits from building dodgy houses and apartments in western Sydney. Harris Mazoudier, who purchased an apartment from Bathla in Schofields, spoke to the

Sydney Morning Herald

 about the defects that littered his unit. Like many other property developers, Bathla has struggled to admit responsibility for these problems.

Profits also came from unsafe work practices. In 2015, a surveyor on a Bathla site fell nearly four metres and was impaled on concrete bars. SafeWork fined the company just $135,000 despite the surveyor’s long-term injuries. Industrial accidents are never treated with the same severity as criminal cases of the same magnitude.

Bathla’s founder, Bhart Bhushan, was once nicknamed “the Baron of Blacktown”. This appropriately sums up the power that property developers have over housing and urban planning. They wield this power to ensure the highest short-term profits, regardless of the social, economic and environmental consequences.

Baron Bhushan had a track record of using lawsuits to bully councils into approving his development applications. According to former Blacktown Mayor Stephen Bali, the council racked up $1 million a year in legal fees after slightly reducing the number of units in Bathla’s development proposals.

Before you weep for the baron’s downfall, know that construction continues on the family’s $5.5 million Dural mansion. “Sierra Morena”, named after a Spanish mountain range, features several swimming pools, a four-car detached garage and a basketball court. Renovation work is still underway to expand this palatial dwelling to include another garage and a “French fan cobblestone” driveway, whatever that is. Somehow, business owners have an uncanny way of never letting a corporate collapse get in the way of their own luxury lifestyle.

The ideologues of the system tell us that the free market is the most efficient way to allocate resources in our society. The profit-seeking of individual enterprises allegedly results in the best outcomes for consumers and society more broadly. Housing in Australia shows the exact opposite.

Defective apartments and injured workers are inevitable consequences of developers and construction companies seeking to cut costs and maximise profits. The pressure to build the houses as quickly as possible with as little delay, in order to cash in on Sydney’s inflated housing market, produces example after example of this. A 2021 survey found that four in ten new apartment buildings have serious defects. According to SafeWork, 44 construction workers died in Australia in 2024.

The anarchic housing market system does not ensure the best outcome for renters, homebuyers or society as a whole. The private housing market has delivered immense profits to developers, banks and landlords. But it has given most workers rental stress and burdensome mortgages: average unit rents have increased 65 percent in the last six years; average house prices have grown by 60 percent.

Property developers have reshaped how our city looks and works—for the worse. Developers build with an eye only to profit, not to holistic urban planning. The amenities people need—schools, parks, public transport, community spaces—are never their concern. Bathla currently owes an unspecified amount to Blacktown City Council for public infrastructure improvements it had committed to building. The worst-hit spots of Sydney are precisely those in the west, where existing urban infrastructure is not designed for increasingly dense populations.

The housing market is propped up by government policies, contrary to claims from free-market apologists. Tax policies such as negative gearing and capital gains tax discount incentivise investment and speculation. The hue and cry from the establishment about the Albanese government’s minor tax changes shows how well the property market has operated as a wealth generator for a minority. The policies remain government interference in the market—interference in favour of the rich.

author: AWSM
title: The anarchist case for abstentionism in elections
content:
The right to vote is seen by most as a necessary prerequisite for freedom across the world. People have fought and died for the right to vote in elections. Women across the world fought bitter battles for the right to vote. So why should anarchists question this as a right worth having?

The entire electoral show is designed to encourage us to believe that not only does our vote matter, but that it is the most important decision we could possibly make. Indeed, voting is held so sacred by many that the mere mention of not voting is enough to cause outrage. Pointing out that our vote makes no difference anyway, will see you accused of being apathetic, privileged, immature, and even being part of the alt-right!

But as noted anarchist Vernon Richards wrote,

“So long as we have capitalism and government, the job of anarchists is to fight both, and at the same time encourage people to take what steps they can to run their own lives.” [“Anarchists and Voting,” pp. 176–87, The Raven, No. 14, p. 179].

Electoralism ensures that a statist perspective becomes dominant. Everything is seen in terms of state intervention and following the decisions of the leaders, which has always proved deadly to encouraging a spirit of revolt, self-management, and self-help – the very keys to creating change in a society. Rather than being something other people discuss on behalf of working-class people, anarchists argue that politics should not be a specialised activity in the hands of the so-called experts (i.e., politicians) but instead lie in the hands of those directly affected by it in the process of participation, direct action, and self-management. Those that channel any “political” conclusions into electoral politics distort discussions into only what is possible within the current system. Given this, is it surprising that anarchists argue that the people “must organise their powers apart from and against the State?” [Bakunin, The Political Philosophy of Bakunin, p. 376].

Abstentionists get told, “If you don’t vote, you have no right to complain about the outcome,” but we consider the opposite to be true. It is those who have voted, who have agreed to the rules, and agreed to be governed by the winners who cannot complain. It is those who do not participate who have the right to complain about the outcome more than anyone else.

We get told that the reality is that voting does change things, but we can, and do, deny that. Voting attempts to provide the population with the illusion of change while in reality it reinforces the current system. A policy here and there may change, the faces may change, but the system of a wealthy minority ruling a poorer majority remains. People will continually be telling us that abstaining from voting will help the right-wing win the election, that it is better if the lesser evil wins. This may possibly be the case (although the argument is far from convincing), but why should we base our society on a compromise with evil? In fact, the “progressive” left wing party you vote for will often be ready to take the same actions as a right-wing government when it comes to imposing anti-working-class action upon us, (as we shall show later in this essay the state has a corrupting effect on those who enter politics with high principles). There should be a better way, and we say the dismantling of government, in all its existing and potential forms is that way.

Most of the left wing in Aotearoa, and quite a few people who claim to identify as anarchists, will support reformist parties in the upcoming election. You will hear them saying things like “vote Labour (or Green) without illusions,” or “vote Labour/Green but build a socialist alternative.” The slogans that these others may shout only reflect the idea that change can and should be brought about by a small number of elite politicians. Abstentionists do not say things like this. There are many problems with our electoral system of democracy, which we shall run through, but we must state that first and foremost, as anarchists, we see voting as against running contrary to our anti-statist and anti-hierarchy principles, and we see electoralism as contrary to our goals and practice. It reinforces the idea that society is divided into order-givers and order-takers. Famed French anarchist, Elisee Reclus, put it well when he said,

“Everything that can be said about the suffrage may be summed up in a sentence. To vote is to give up your own power. To elect a …

author: Pip Hinman
title: Socialist Alliance candidate says One Nation can be combatted
content:
The following piece is based on Jacob Andrewartha’s speech to an election launch on September 6. He is standing for Socialist Alliance in the Victorian seat of Pascoe Vale.

At the beginning of Israel’s latest genocide in Gaza in October 2023, alongside many other comrades, I helped initiate the first local protest in Coburg for Palestine, which drew more than 1000 people. It helped broaden the movement for Palestine at the local level.

It is inspiring to join people taking action and become more organised against the establishment.

That, after all, is the only way we can counter the rise of One Nation and the neoliberal politics of Labor and the Liberals.

We saw that power with the thousands of high school students who walked out against Pauline Hanson and One Nation earlier last month.

We also saw it at the massive turnout against Israeli Prime Minister Isaac Herzog’s visit to Gadigal Country.

Our collective power is how we push back against capitalist politicians and their billionaire mates.

The rising support for One Nation can be demoralising, just as the Labor Party’s pursuit of right-wing policies.

The only way to combat this is to advance the self-organisation and collective power of working people.

The very conditions that have led to the rise in support for One Nation have to be changed. But that can only change with a fight-back.

The industrial action waged by teachers and education support staff is a recent inspiring example. Their campaign — on the streets — not only pushed the Australian Education Union leadership, it won teachers and support staff a better pay offer from Victorian Labor.

However, while Socialist Alliance is dedicated to building struggles in workplaces and in our communities for concrete demands, this is not enough. We also need to talk about what sort of society we want and how to get it.

The billionaire class is united around their vision — a society where they can continue to enrich themselves from exploiting workers and the Earth. The billionaires won’t stop pushing for low or no taxes on the rich, subsidies and the total privatisation of public services. They also want to continue to drive down wages.

Our vision is one of solidarity. We believe in a society where everyone has the right to housing. We want essential services, like education and healthcare, to be fully funded and resourced. We want real action on the climate emergency. We want fully funded public transport. We want to see a world free of conflict, genocide and oppression.

We want a world where everyone can live their lives to the full — the only way of doing that is if their basic needs are met.

But we have to fight against the ruling class’ marketisation of everything.

Victorian Labor is now considering privatising Melbourne Water. In Britain, such a move led to the return of cholera.

We have to stop Labor from demolishing all 44 high-rise public housing estates and demand it build more public housing. Everyone knows that by leaving housing to the market, the housing affordability crisis will intensify.

We have to fight laws that restrict our ability to protect the rights of working-class people, including restrictions on the right to protest and the right of workers to take industrial action.

Victorian Labor’s plan to destroy the Retail and Fast Food Workers Union (RAFFWU), after having tried to destroy the Construction Forestry and Maritime Employees Union, shows up just how anti-worker it is.

But a society where people’s needs are met and where people can lead fulfilling lives will only be achieved if there is broad support for socialist ideas and solutions. For that, we need a much greater level of self-organisation and preparedness to struggle.

Even without many MPs, One Nation has pressured the establishment parties into adopting parts of its program. Labor has cut temporary visa programs, and it continues to allow refugees to rot on Nauru.

With polls showing a growing alienation from the mainstream parties and many people only relating to politics at election time, Socialist Alliance has to be there to put our vision forward. The far right, and its media supporters, is managing to con people into believing that migration is the cause of the housing crisis, despite the evidence.

Socialist Alliance has been contesting elections since we formed in 2001, because we see the electoral arena as one theatre of struggle to win more people to join the movements for a fairer, more just society …

author: Editors
title: 9/11: How the US turned tragedy into barbarity
content:
Twenty-five years ago, the world changed irrevocably. Not because terrorists from the al-Qaeda network attacked the United States, bringing down the World Trade Center’s Twin Towers in New York, hitting the Pentagon in Virginia and killing nearly 3,000 people. It changed because of US imperialism’s response.

The day after 9/11, the editors of

Socialist Alternative

 magazine, one of the precursor publications of

Red Flag

, warned: “The real threat to people around the world is not terrorism, but the racism, militarism, repression and nationalism that has been unleashed in the wake of the terrorist attacks”.

A week later, President George W. Bush, in an address to a joint session of Congress, announced his so-called War on Terror: “Every nation, in every region, now has a decision to make. Either you are with us, or you are with the terrorists”. His administration rode the wave of outrage over al-Qaeda’s assault to open a new era of imperialist aggression that has cost millions of people’s lives. 

First came Afghanistan in October. It didn’t matter that the ruling Taliban

offered to hand over Osama bin Laden

, the alleged mastermind of the terrorist attacks, to a neutral country to face trial. The US was interested only in war. Condoleezza Rice, then Bush’s national security adviser, admitted as much to the

New Yorker

’s Nicholas Lemann several months later. In the wake of the 9/11 attacks, she had asked senior national security staff to think about how to “capitalise on these opportunities”. 

The Bush administration soon began making a public case for invading Iraq—which had no ties to 9/11—declaring the country part of an “axis of evil” with Iran and North Korea. Undersecretary of State John Bolton soon expanded the axis list to include Cuba, Libya and Syria. The bombs started raining down on Baghdad in March 2003.

These invasions would have been followed by more had the resistance in Iraq not bogged down the US military in an intractable counterinsurgency. Nevertheless, Brown University’s

Costs of War research

 estimates the direct death toll from US military operations in the post-9-11 era in Iraq, Afghanistan, Syria, Yemen and Pakistan to be close to 1 million people. It estimates a further 3.6 to 3.8 million “indirect” deaths resulting from the “destruction of economies, healthcare systems, infrastructure and the environment”. 

The US also set up a global kidnapping network, which it termed “extraordinary rendition”, and a series of “black sites” in which prisoners were held without charge and tortured.

The Open Society Foundation estimates

 that 54 governments collaborated in the program. Then there is the notorious

Guantánamo Bay torture camp

, used since 2002 and still holding ageing prisoners from the War on Terror. This all served as notice that the US empire would stop at nothing to maintain its global domination.

A more enduring legacy of this era of “forever wars” has been the construction of vast internal security and surveillance states, which have trampled civil and democratic rights. 

More than 140 governments have adopted “counterterrorism” legislation since 9/11, beginning with the USA PATRIOT Act, which green-lit mass surveillance and delayed-notice search warrants and bolstered spy agency resources. Mega-departments, such as Homeland Security in the US and Home Affairs in Australia, were established as Western states have become more authoritarian.

Indeed, Australia is one of the worst offenders. “No other nation can match the volume of Australia’s counter-terrorism laws”, wrote legal academics Rebecca Ananian-Welsh and Keiran Hardy in

a 2021 piece for the University of Queensland’s

Contact

 magazine

. They describe the scope of the laws as “staggering”, “unprecedented” and “extreme”, noting that they go beyond even “historical wartime powers”.

They include control orders, preventive detention, and compulsory retention of all telecommunication and online data of every resident. The

Surveillance Legislation Amendment (Identify and Disrupt) Act

 of 2021 gave law enforcement agencies the power to take control of a person’s individual online accounts, modify or delete their data and even take over entire networks. That is, they can legally alter a person’s text messages.

Death and destruction abroad and authoritarianism at home: such is the “rules-based order”, the purported demise of which we are supposed to lament. This post-9/11 era normalised authoritarianism …

author: Susan Price
title: Singapore’s unfinished anti-colonial struggle
content:
The dominant history of modern Singapore was meticulously constructed under the banner of the “Singapore Story”. By presenting the material interests of the ruling elite as the universal interests of the nation, the state narrative reduces the mass anti-imperialist movement of the mid-20th century into a fable; one wherein a heroic bourgeois leadership single-handedly navigates a vulnerable island state through the perils of communism to construct a prosperous capitalist metropolis.

In his six-part oral history series with Pintjin (PJ) Thum, Dr Poh Soo Kai, former student activist, co-founder of the People’s Action Party (PAP) and the Barisan Sosialis (Socialist Front) — and former political prisoner detained for nearly 17 years without trial — delivers a vital historical materialist counter-narrative.

In 36 minutes of personal testimony, Poh unpacks the class dynamics, state coercion, and geopolitical shake-ups that dismantled working-class power and shaped Singapore's transition into a disciplined capitalist state.

Poh begins by recalling how post-World War II Malayan households were adorned with portraits of Indonesia’s Sukarno, India’s Nehru and Gandhi, and China’s Chiang Kai-Shek, who were seen as regional anti-colonial leaders. The struggle in Singapore was bound to broader anti-imperialist movements across Malaya, Indonesia, and Vietnam.

Poh’s account of the 1954 Fajar Trial undermines the state’s origin myth, which positions the trial of eight members of the editorial board of Fajar (Dawn) — the University of Malaya Socialist Club’s newspaper — as Lee Kuan Yew’s (LKY’s) personal legal breakthrough.

[Editor’s note: Harry Lee Kwan Yew co-founded the PAP, was a barrister and opposition figure and became Singapore’s first Prime Minister in 1959.]

As president of the University of Malaya Socialist Club, Poh helped publish Fajar, an anti-colonial paper opposing the anti-communist South East Asian Treaty Organisation (SEATO) and foreign military bases. When the editorial board was charged with sedition, Queen’s Counsel DN Pritt arrived to lead the defense. Poh recounts Pritt greeting him warmly at the Dolphin Hotel before turning to LKY, who was acting as local junior counsel, and saying, “Harry, now you can go.”

Pritt dismissed LKY specifically to formulate an anti-colonial strategy directly with the student activists, recognising that the trial was a political battlefield rather than a legal technicality.

This moment symbolises the clash between the radical student movement and LKY’s legalism, and how official history later repackaged a left-wing victory as an LKY solo masterstroke.

As the PAP rose to power, internal contradictions between its left-wing mass base and moderate leadership erupted.

Poh recounts how the left wing consistently pushed for true self-determination, confronting PAP Chair Toh Chin Chye to issue a public statement supporting then-Chief Minister David Marshall’s 1956 call for internal self-rule — a move that infuriated LKY upon his return from London.

[Editor’s note: Marshall was appointed Chief Minister after contesting the 1955 election as a candidate for the Labour Front. After failing to secure self-rule, he resigned as Chief Minister in June 1956.]

Chief Minister Lim Yew Hock’s violent crackdowns on trade unions and Chinese school students from 1956 onward served a dual purpose: suppressing working-class organisation while allowing LKY to position himself as the sensible alternative acceptable to British imperial interests and local capital.

When dissident MPs and activists walked out to form the Barisan Sosialis in 1961, every PAP branch including LKY’s own Tanjong Pagar constituency defected to the new party. The PAP was left as a hollow electoral vessel without organic mass support.

To preempt an electoral defeat, the state deployed Operation Coldstore in February 1963. Officially framed as a security operation against a communist plot tied to the 1962 Brunei Revolt, Coldstore was a draconian political purge that sought to decapitate the political opposition, dismantle union leadership and ensure PAP hegemony.

The state weaponised identity politics to divide the multi-ethnic working-class by branding Chinese-educated labour leaders and Barisan Sosialis members as “Chinese chauvinists”. It replaced class-based solidarity with state-directed multiracialism that contained labour organising within non-threatening boundaries.

Declassified British colonial intelligence …

author: Anonymous
title: “There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band touring Australia …”
content:
I was contacted a little while ago by somebody raising concerns about a couple of upcoming black metal gigs. Below is the text they sent.

There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band, Helleruin, playing in Melbourne at the Northcote Social Club on September 11 and in Sydney at Crowbar on September 12.

Most of Helleruin’s records have been released on New Era Productions, which has put out a number of releases by fash black metal bands and which is run by Jasper Velzel, a NSBM and RAC musician. In addition, another project of Helleruin’s Carchost — Orewoet — is on the label Heidens Hart, which — along with releasing some far-right stuff — is owned by a former live guitarist of prominent fash band Graveland.

Moreover, a number of the local supporting acts have sketchy connections.

Order of Orias, one of two supports in Melbourne along with Petrol (see below), are on World Terror Committee, which releases fashy stuff and is owned by Sven Zimper, a member of prominent NSBM group Absurd.

Of the bands playing Sydney with Helleruin (Krvna, Pestilential Shadows, Destruktor, Vicissitude, Gravgöt, Grotesque Bliss, Petrol, Blasfemancia and Akhoth) at the ‘Call from the Grave’ festival:

Pestilential Shadows have released music on the Chinese label, GoatowaRex, who are very friendly to NSBM acts. Additionally, PS is part of a collective called Ordo Ater Anguis/Order of the Black Serpent, which includes numerous far right acts. Michael W Ford of Black Funeral appears to be a former Order of Nine Angles (09A) member in the United States who — after distancing himself from O9A — attempted to formulate a social Darwinist version of the Satanic Temple (lol), which coalesce around the Australian fash-friendly label, Dark Adversary. Indeed, one of the members of PS is also a member of Varw, a band on Dark Adversary. Further, Akhoth released a demo, ‘Storm of Pagan Fury’, on CD on Dark Adversary this year.

Grotesque Bliss are on Iron Bonehead which, along with the suspect name, appears to be run by a (if only barely) crypto-fascist.

Destruktor is on a label, Hells Headbangers, which has previously released and re-released stuff by Satanic Warmaster and Deströyer 666, including re-releasing Deströyer 666’s debut album, ‘Unchain the Wolves’, on a few different mediums over the last few years. Additionally, Inquisition had a few releases on Hells Headbangers after their lead singer (who is also a Satanist pedo) released openly fash music on fash label Satanic Skinhead Propaganda (a label which the Iron Bonehead guy sold in his old fash-friendly record store).

The most recent (2024) EP of Krvna, formally of PS, was released on Zazen Sounds, run by Greek nazi black metaller Acherontass of Αχέροντας (Krvna played guest guitar on their most recent album). For what it’s also worth, Third Eye Temple — the Polish label on which Krvna’s 2022 album was released — have released one split and re-issued an EP by Voidhanger, a side project of Polish far right black metallers, Infernal War.

Finally, Petrol were previously on a cancelled bill with Gurn. They also played a gig with Japanese band Abigail, who are signed to Nuclear Now Productions, a fash-friendly label linked to Iron Bonehead (similarly exposed by the nsbmboneheads blog linked above). In addition, Petrol played at Crowbar Sydney last year with Bolzer (see nsbmboneheads blog), who released all but their last record on Iron Bonehead. The other headliner was Portal, who have released lots of records on Hells Headbangers including, recently, a split with Blood of Kingu — a side-project of the Ukrainian ultra-nationalists from Drudkh — on the label in 2014.

author: Editors
title: FROM THE ARCHIVE—Tragedy in America: how should the left respond? (12 September 2001)
content:
Today, there is no shortage of mainstream commentators prepared to speak out strongly against the war policy of the George W. Bush era. Even current US President Donald Trump claims to have been an opponent of the Iraq invasion and of the broader orientation of the Republican administration of 2001-09.

But in the days after 9/11, no major media outlet would hear a word against the US. Those of us who said that US imperialism, not terrorism, posed the greatest threat to the world were vilified, marginalised and condemned as terrorist sympathisers.

Socialist Alternative is proud that we took an unequivocal anti-imperialist stance, even in those early and dark days when doing so was deeply unpopular. The article republished below was put out on 12 September 2001. We think its arguments, unlike so much written then and since, stand the test of time.

Socialist Alternative

 magazine editorial

The September 11 attacks in New York and Washington, D.C., are a horrific tragedy.

The bodies of thousands of ordinary working-class people—of all races, religions and political beliefs—lie in the rubble of New York’s World Trade Centre.

But the response of the world’s leaders, and of the media commentators and opinion writers, has been marked by a hideous hypocrisy.

US President George Bush, along with others such as Tony Blair, and our own John Howard and Kim Beazley, have fallen over themselves to condemn terrorism, violence and murder.

They have vowed to fight the “uncivilised” actions of people who they accuse of having no regard for the sanctity of human life. But it is the likes of Bush, Blair and Howard who preside over a system that condemns millions to death and misery all around the world.

Up to 200,000 civilians were murdered in the oil-driven Gulf War in 1991. More than 500,000 children have died since as a result of crippling sanctions.

Around the world—in Indonesia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America—despotic regimes financed and supported by the US government have slaughtered hundreds of thousands of people.

The genocide of one-third of the East Timorese population was directly supported by the US, Australia and Britain. The brutal Israeli occupation of Palestine is propped up by the $1.5 billion in aid it receives from the US every year.

And the logic of the capitalist system has condemned millions to death through war and poverty around the globe. 20,000 children starve to death and die of preventable diseases every day because US grain is dumped in the ocean to keep prices up, and because multinationals conspire to stop medical treatments being accessible to the world’s poor.

And while George Bush rails against terrorism, the fact is that Bin Laden, accused of being behind the September 11 attacks, shares with Timothy McVeigh the distinction of having been trained in terrorism by the US government.

The CIA trained Bin Laden as a commander in its proxy army that fought the USSR after its invasion of Afghanistan in 1979. Bin Laden was “so effective a recruiter [for the Afghan guerrillas] that close comrades at the time actually thought he was working for the CIA”.

The same US government that today denounces Bin Laden and the Taliban lauded them as “freedom fighters” in the 1980s.

The rulers of the world have no interest in human rights, or in the lives of ordinary people. As Leon Trotsky said over 80 years ago:

“[We have] nothing in common with those bought and paid for moralists who, in response to any terrorist act, make solemn declarations about the ‘absolute value’ of human life. These are the same people who, on other occasions, in the name of other absolute values—for example, the nation’s honour or the monarch’s prestige—are ready to shove millions of people into the hell of war.”

That millions of people around the world passionately hate imperialist US policies is the fault of the US ruling class; of the politicians and businessmen who grow fat through the suffering and death of ordinary people.

The tragedy of the attacks on the US is that ordinary Americans have had to suffer for the genocidal and inhumane policies of their rulers. In answer to the question of where responsibility lies for this senseless loss of life, there can only be one answer: Capitalism.

But whilst we understand the anger directed against America, Marxists are not terrorists.

We utterly oppose the idea that, by killing ordinary people, a tiny minority can change the world for the better. It is only through …

author: Pip Hinman
title: Bob Brown: Australian government ‘culpable’ for climate disasters like Nepal
content:
Former Greens leader Bob Brown said Australia is “culpable” for the devastation in Nepal because it was not acting seriously on the dangers of carbon emissions changing the climate.

Australia is co-hosting the COP31 summit in November, along with Türkiye. Yet despite talking up climate action, Labor set about lowering expectations after it was first elected in 2022.

Green Left’s Alex Bainbridge spoke with former Greens leader Bob Brown about Labor’s refusal to take climate action seriously, even though it is a co-host of COP31.

What do you think of Labor’s approach to the climate emergency and does Australia deserve to be co-hosting COP31?

The symbolism of turning on Beetaloo in the wake of the Nepali avalanche disaster is very hard to ignore.

But this Labor government, much like the far-right alternatives, is captured by the corporate sector, including Woodside and BHP, selling off Australian’s rights for a secure future.

They won’t be the only culpable governments in Türkiye, however. Labor appears to be better than Pauline Hanson, but One Nation and Labor are both culpable of making climate change worse.

Federal Labor is set to debate the so-called “improved native forest management” method. Supporters claim it is going save some native forests. However, it allows state governments to earn carbon credits to then plough back into an already dodgy carbon trading system. Should saving forests be contingent on companies being able to buy carbon credits?

We’ve got more than 600 national parks in Australia, and world heritage areas, and they’ve all been set aside for the nation’s future because of their natural and cultural heritage values.

They were never set aside because of the dollars that could be made out of it.

But we’ve got a watershed moment; if Labor gets away with this, we have this new dynamic whereby future national parks will depend, to some degree or another, on whether the corporate sector can extract money as a result.

The NSW Chris Minns Labor government went to the last election in 2023 promising a great koala national park. It never put a condition on that, nor would it have, because polls showed that 80% of Labor voters wanted that park created and want koalas saved.

But, since the election, Minns has added a rider that you cannot have the koala park unless you agree to a scheme that measures the carbon absorbed by the saved forest and sells it to polluters as a cheap “offset”, so they can continue polluting. This way the polluting corporation can keep putting greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and make climate change worse.

We need to look at this through the lens of United Nations Secretary General António Guterres, who has repeatedly said the quickest and cheapest way to deal with climate change is to stop logging forests. This Minns manoeuvre destroys that advantage.

Energy minister Chris Bowen is once again criticising the Greens’ decision in 2009 to block the flawed carbon pollution reduction scheme (CPRS), which we called the “continue polluting regardless scheme”. There’s a lot of rewriting of that history. Looking back, were the Greens right to block the CPRS?

How do you respond to Labor’s argument that the decision set the climate movement back by a decade?

Bowen and Labor have a blind spot on the Julia Gillard years, when the Greens got Labor to put through the carbon pricing scheme in 2011, which was a world leader and really did make a difference because it almost instantly lowered greenhouse gases emissions for the first time in decades and lowered electricity prices.

The CPRS, which came two years before that, was flawed. It had been negotiated by then Prime Minister Kevin Rudd with the Coalition. It was only when the Coalition pulled out that they said, “Well, now the Greens have got to put it through.” The Greens said we’ll amend it and they said “No”.

Large sections of the Canberra press gallery have glossed over the real action that was needed to tackle climate change and which the Greens got two years later with Gillard. Our scheme was so effective that [former Coalition Prime Minister] Tony Abbott had to try to dismantle as much of it as he could.

Let me just go back to the CPRS. The Greens said it is simply feather bedding for multinational polluters and we are not going to pass it. The media said: “The Greens have had it. There’s five Greens in the parliament. They’re going to lose at the next election.”

At the next election, our vote went up by 50% and …

author: Mick Armstrong
title: FROM THE ARCHIVE—US imperialism (November 2002)
content:
Four weeks after the 9/11 attacks, the US invaded Afghanistan. By early 2002, the Bush administration began making the public case for invading Iraq, declaring the country part of an “axis of evil” with Iran and North Korea. Undersecretary of State John Bolton soon expanded the list to include Cuba, Libya and Syria. (The name “axis of resistance”, including Iran, Syria, Hezbollah and Hamas, was reportedly coined in response to all this.)

It became clear very quickly, however, that the analysis laid out in our 12 September editorial was substantially correct. In March 2022, Condoleezza Rice, then Bush’s national security adviser, admitted to the New Yorker’s Nicholas Lemann that, in the wake of the 9/11 attacks, she had asked senior national security staff to think about how to “capitalise on these opportunities”, which were “shifting the tectonic plates in international politics” to US advantage. “I really think this period is analogous to 1945 to 1947”, she said. “And it’s important to try to seize on that and position American interests and institutions and all of that before they harden again.”

It is obvious to more and more people that the [impending] US war on Iraq has got absolutely nothing to do with defending democracy or stopping “terrorism”, let alone with liberating the people of Iraq. It is a good old-fashioned imperialist war—like when the British sent in the gunboats to prove to the locals who was boss.

The September 11 terrorist attacks were a godsend for George Bush. They gave the US establishment carte blanche to accelerate military expenditure, crack down on dissent at home and to adopt a much more aggressive posture on the world stage.

Following hard on the heels of the Afghan war, the war on Iraq is just another step by the US ruling class to assert its military and economic dominance over global capitalism.

But why Iraq?

At one level it doesn’t matter all that much to the US who they attack. They are out to demonstrate that the US is the sole superpower that can assert its might right across the globe, and provided they are victorious, the Pentagon planners don’t care whether the next target is North Korea, Sudan, Colombia, Central Asia or Libya.

The strategists of Bush’s “war on terrorism” have spelt it out very clearly—they are planning permanent war, with the US military engaged in country after country. They want to establish a US armed presence in every corner of the globe and over the next decade they want to launch a first strike nuclear attack somewhere.

The US ruling class increasingly see the enormous military superiority they have over all their capitalist rivals as their key bargaining chip to shore up the profits of US multinationals and to force their economic competitors in Europe, Japan and China to make concessions to them in terms of opening up markets for US goods. Taking out Iraq will be a graphic illustration to all the other powers of the US’s willingness to resort to force to protect its interests.

There are of course additional factors. To start with—oil.

The Middle East has long been of central importance to US imperialism because of its enormous oil reserves—control over which is vital to the interests of all the advanced capitalist powers. By putting an upstart like Saddam Hussein in his place, not only does the US military defend the economic interests of its multinational oil companies, it also gives the US vital leverage over Japan and the European Union, which are more dependent on Middle Eastern oil than the US itself.

Partly it is settling scores with Saddam. The US backed Saddam’s brutal rise to power in Iraq to crush the powerful working-class movement there and to secure Western interests. They armed him to the teeth with chemical and biological weapons.

But then he got too big for his boots, and as with so many other US-backed dictators—Milosevic in Serbia, Noriega in Panama, the Taliban in Afghanistan—they moved to eliminate him.

The problem was that Saddam was more cunning than most; he managed to survive defeat in the Gulf War and has played fast and loose with the US for years. His defiance encourages other lesser powers to stand up to US hegemony.

This makes him a marked man whom Bush is determined to eliminate. Cutting Saddam down sends a message to every other US client state—don’t step out of line or you’re next.

The other reason that Iraq and Afghanistan are important to the US is China. The US establishment sees China as the rising …

author: Unknown
title: Alliance of Iranian Kurdistan political parties thanks people for successful general strike
content:
The Alliance of Political Parties of Iranian Kurdistan has issued a statement thanking the people of Kurdistan for their widespread participation in the general strike on Wednesday, 16 September.


The Alliance described the strike as successful despite security pressure and restrictions. The statement said the strike was held on the fourth anniversary of the death of Jina Amini and in remembrance of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” uprising.


The Alliance also thanked dozens of political parties and groups, women’s organizations, civil society groups, political and academic figures, as well as political prisoners who supported the strike, including some who joined through hunger strikes.


The Alliance also expressed appreciation for the support shown by Baluch, Turk, Persian, Turkmen and Arab political groups and figures, saying this solidarity reflected broader support for the action beyond Kurdistan.


The Alliance said it would continue to represent and raise the legitimate demands of the people of Kurdistan and stressed the importance of unity and cooperation in future political and civil activities.

author: Unknown
title: ‘İktidar, işçi sınıfını da gazetesini de güvenlik sorunu olarak görüyor’
content:
Gözde Tüzer Korkmaz [email protected]

Gazetemiz Evrensel’in X hesabı hakkında “milli güvenlik ve kamu düzeninin korunması” gerekçesiyle erişim engeli kararı getirilmesi tepki toplarken, bir yandan da işçilerin grevleri, eylemleri, açıklamaları yine aynı madde gerekçe gösterilerek yasaklanıyor. Sendikalar devletin artık bir “sermaye çıkarlarını koruyan aygıta” dönüştüğünü belirtirken, işçi sınıfının ve halkların gazetesi Evrensel’in de baskılardan nasibini aldığını belirtti.

AKP iktidarının yargı ve kolluk gücüyle, “Ailem Güvende” adı altında insan hakları ve LGBTİ örgütleri ile çok sayıda hak savunucusuna yönelik düzenlediği operasyonlarla eş zamanlı yürüttüğü dijital sansürün son adreslerinden biri gazetemiz Evrensel'in X (Twitter) hesabı oldu. Bakırköy 4. Sulh Ceza Hakimliği X hesabımızın erişime engellenmesi kararı alırken, bunu “milli güvenlik ve kamu düzeninin korunması” gerekçesini öne süren 5651 sayılı Kanun’un 8/A maddesine dayandırıldı. Erişim engeli kararı henüz X tarafından uygulanmadı. Bu karar birçok kesim tarafından sansür olarak yorumlandı.

5651 sayılı Kanunun 8/A maddesi, “gecikmesinde sakınca bulunan hallerde yaşam hakkı, millî güvenlik, kamu düzeni ve genel sağlığın korunması” gibi gerekçelerle internetteki içeriklerin “derhal engellenmesine” imkân tanıyor. Cumhurbaşkanlığı veya ilgili bakanlıkların talebi, Bilgi Teknolojileri ve İletişim Kurumu (BTK) Başkanı'nın kararı veya hâkim onayı ile karar erişim sağlayıcılara bildiriliyor.

Benzer bir uygulama da işçi sınıfının hak arama mücadelesinde karşısına çıkıyor. Pek çok grev ve eylem “milli güvenlik” gerekçesiyle yasaklanıyor. Grevleri en çok yasaklanan sendikalardan Birleşik Metal-İş’in Genel Başkanı Özkan Atar “Bu uygulamalar AKP iktidar bloğunun politikalarının ne denli demokrasi karşıtı noktaya geldiğini, basını ve aynı zamanda emekçilerin, işçilerin hak ve özgürlüklerini, haber alma hakkını ne derece engellediğini gösteriyor” dedi. Atar, iktidarın “mili güvenlik” adı altında yerli ve yabancı sermayenin çıkarlarını öncelikli olarak kolladığını, bu doğrultuda da her türlü demokratik hak ve özgürlükleri baskıcı bir şekilde engellendiğini belirtti.

Atar şöyle devam etti: “Ama şunun da bilinmesi gerekir… Ne kadar baskıcı, anti demokratik ve faşizan uygulamalar hayata geçerse geçsin, mutlaka emekçilerin ve toplumun hak ve özgürlük mücadelesi de doğrultuda sürecektir. Bu yaşanan kara tablo mutlaka yırtılacaktır. Biz de Evrensel’e sahip çıkmaya devam edeceğiz.”

BİRTEK-SEN Başkanı Mehmet Türkmen bizzat BİRTEK-SEN’in pek çok grevinin, işçi direnişinin “milli güvenlik” gerekçesiyle engellendiğini ve yasaklandığını belirterek “İşçilerin hak arama mücadelesi hangi gerekçe ile engelleniyorsa Evrensel’in de ‘milli güvenlik’ gerekçesiyle engellenmesi aynı sebepten gerçekleşiyor. İktidar, düzen ve karar vericiler, işçilerin patronlara karşı sermaye düzenine karşı mücadele etmesinden nasıl rahatsız oluyorsa, o mücadelenin bütün Türkiye’de duyulmasına ve mücadelesine yol göstermesine imkan sağlayan bir gazetenin engellenmesi de aynı anlayışın ürünü” ifadelerini kullandı.

İşçilerin hak arama mücadelelerinin engellenmesi ve gazetelerin hesaplarına getirilen erişim engelleri arasında doğrudan bir bağ bulunduğunu belirten Mehmet Türkmen “Son dönemlerde LGBTİ’leri, sivil toplum örgütlerini, tüm muhalif kesimleri hedefleyen bu otoriterliğin amacı neyse, işçi sınıfını açlığa, sefalete ve köleliğe mahkum eden anlayışın da amacı aynı. Bir avuç sermayedarın, işçilerin hayatına çökmesine engel olmak istemiyorlar. İşçi sınıfı mücadelesi, sermayedarlar için nasıl bir engelse, işçi sınıfının gazetesi de aynı şekilde engel” ifadelerini kullandı.

Türkmen son olarak şöyle devam etti: “Nasıl ki bütün baskılara rağmen işçi sınıfının mücadelesi engellenemiyorsa, işçi sınıfının 30 yıldır sesi olan Evrensel’i de susturamayacaklar. Çünkü Evrensel sadece muhabirlerinden, editörlerinden ibaret değil, işçi sınıfının kendi kavgasında ortaya çıkardığı bir mücadele aracı. İşçi sınıfını engellemek nasıl mümkün olmadıysa, onun sesi ve soluğu olan gazetesini de engellemek mümkün olmayacaktır.”

Ankara’ya yürümeleri engellenen, gözaltına alınan ve eylemlerinde sürekli müdahalelere maruz kalan maden işçilerinin sendikası olan Bağımsız Maden-İş Sendikası'nın örgütlenme uzmanı Başaran Aksu, devletlerin geçmişte yurttaşlarının haklarını korumaya çalışan bir yapı olarak kendisini göstermeye çalıştığını ancak bugün tüm çıplaklığıyla sermayenin çıkarları doğrultusunda hareket ettiğini belirterek …

author: Battlescarred
title: Book Review: Anarchist Popular Power: Dissident Labor and Armed Struggle in Uruguay, 1956-1976.
content:
A review of book on Uruguayan anarchism.

Anarchist Popular Power: Dissident Labor and Armed Struggle in Uruguay, 1956-1976. Troy Andreas Araiza Kokinis. 365 pages. 2023. £21.00

The anarchist movement in Uruguay was one of the most important in South America, and yet few works in English have appeared on the subject. There is Direct Action in Montevideo: Uruguayan Anarchism, 1927–1937 by Fernando O’Neill Cuesta, which appeared in 2020, and before that, a single 50-page pamphlet The Federacion Anarquista Uruguaya: Crisis, Armed Struggle and Dictatorship, 1967-8, written by FAU members, which appeared in 2009.

The longest existing and perhaps strongest specific anarchist organisation in Latin America is the Federacion Anarquista Uruguaya (FAU) of Uruguay.

Unlike other countries in South America, Uruguay was known as a stronghold of bourgeois democracy and social reform. Under its president Battle y Ordonez, a whole raft of legislation was introduced in the mid-1910s. He separated Church from State, banned crucifixes in hospitals, removed references to God and the Bible from public oaths, gave widespread rights to unions and political parties and organisations, brought in the eight hour day and universal suffrage, introduced unemployment benefits, legalised divorce, created more high schools, promised and practised no residency laws against exiled anarchists and other radicals, opened universities to women, and led a campaign to take away the control of industry and land from foreign capitalists (the British capitalists had huge influence in Uruguay) and nationalised private monopolies. This disoriented some elements within this fairly strong anarchist movement in Uruguay.

Between 1948 and 1954 the working class in Uruguay was comparatively well off, with good conditions and pay, in a country presided over by a ruling class with a liberal outlook. This all changed between 1955 and 1959 with an increasing cost of living.

The FAU was set up in 1956. Militants within it like Juan Carlos Mechoso began to agitate for the creation of a specific anarchist organization as opposed to the anarcho-syndicalists who thought that work in the unions was enough to bring out radical social change. At first the FAU had been an alliance of different anarchist currents, from the anarcho-syndicalists on one hand, through those who believed in setting up anarchist communities in the here and now, traditional anarchist communists, on to the group around Mechoso, Gerardo Gatti and Leon Duarte.

Kokinis deals in detail with the period of both an initial orientation by the FAU to mass agitation and the armed struggle initiatives that intermeshed with it. His book is based on many personal contacts and interviews, 27 in all, with surviving FAU militants of that period. Sometimes the huge number of acronyms for various union centrals, armed groups, and struggle fronts is overwhelming, and one finds oneself constantly referring to the list of abbreviated terms which number 36 in total!

Within the FAU itself there was intense debate over the Castro regime between 1961 and 1965 with Mechoso, Gatti and co. supporting the Cuban regime. This led to a split in the FAU in late 1962 with the Gatti/Duarte/Mechoso faction retaining the FAU name and symbols, affirming the class struggle nature of anarchism, but also giving critical support to Cuba. Kokinis deals with the controversy in the FAU over this, describing the debates between the FAU secretary, Jose Jorge Martinez, and Luce Fabbri (who he wrongly calls Lucce), daughter of the celebrated Italian anarchist Luigi Fabbri. Martinez had a Third Worldist position, seeing the principal contradiction between imperialism and liberation-”one in which the global core directly benefitted from the underdevelopment of the global periphery by accessing cheap resources and labour.” Fabbri, on the other hand, had criticisms of the Castroist move towards state capitalism, totalitarianism, and growing relationship with the Soviet Union.

Kokinis rather misleadingly designates the Fabbri position as traditionalist, and fails to mention other leading militants, admittingly in a minority, like Debora Cespedes, Luis Albert Gallegos, Gomensoro, Iriondo, De Ottone, the Errandonea brothers, and Cresatti, who had left the FAU by the end of 1962. He does point out that among other anarchist groups in Latin America, the Argentine Libertarian Federation (FLA) was publicising the testimonies of Cuban anarchists talking about …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Intervención de la UOM impuso el primer banco de horas metalúrgico
content:
El intento de compensar horas sin usar extras había fracasado una y otra vez en el gremio metalúrgico por la negativa de la conducción a cargo de Abel Furlán. Ahora, en un trámite exprés, las autoridades judiciales impuestas en el sindicato acordaron el mecanismo con una automotriz china que empezó a instalarse en Campana, el pago chico de Furlán.


Alberto Biglieri


La

intervención judicial de la Unión Obrera Metalúrgica (UOM)

 impuso el primer acuerdo de banco de horas de ese gremio con una automotriz de origen chino emplazada en la ciudad de Campana, de donde surgió el desplazado líder sindical Abel Furlán. El banco de horas es una herramienta que flexibiliza y permite estirar la jornada laboral más allá de su límite legal y fija mecanismos de compensación diferentes de las horas extra.


Se trata de la primera acción de alto impacto -y alineada con la reforma laboral de Javier Milei- resuelta por la gestión del abogado Alberto Biglieri, designado por la Cámara laboral con el alegado propósito de reiniciar el proceso electoral de los metalúrgicos. De los 180 días que debía tomarse Biglieri para llamar a elecciones pasaron casi 120 sin visos todavía de dar inicio a ese proceso. En lugar de eso el interventor tomó el control integral tanto del sindicato como de su obra social y en ese último espacio repuso a funcionarios que habían reportado antes al Grupo Olmos, a cargo de esa prestadora durante el mandato de Antonio Caló en el gremio metalúrgico.


En una comunicación interna de gestión a la que accedió El Destape, la intervención de la UOM dio cuenta de un “acuerdo colectivo con FTN Motors”, la razón social con la que opera en la Argentina la automotriz Foton, en proceso de montar una fábrica en Campana en sociedad con el local Grupo Corven. El entendimiento incluye la inauguración de “un banco de horas por treinta y seis meses, con un máximo de 200 horas, compensación dentro de doce meses, jornada efectiva no superior a las diez horas diarias ni cuarenta y ocho semanales, descanso mínimo de doce horas entre jornadas y treinta y cinco horas semanales, registro digital individual, control de una comisión mixta, preservación íntegra del salario y exclusión de licencias, vacaciones, enfermedad, accidentes y actividad gremial”.


Detalle del banco de horas 


El documento suscripto con las autoridades de Foton prevé que “los saldos a favor del trabajador deben compensarse o abonarse” mientras que “los saldos a favor de la empresa se extinguen al vencer el período o al finalizar el contrato y nunca pueden descontarse de salarios o indemnizaciones”. El acuerdo cuenta con el aval de Biglieri y la firma de su delegado en Campana, el contador Javier Lucchetta, nombrado a cargo de la seccional Campana. Lucchetta cumple funciones desde 2011 como administrador del laboratorio Surar Pharma, un establecimiento que se vio involucrado en el escándalo por el fentanilo mortal y que, más de una década atrás, fue clausurado en el contexto de otro episodio policial por irregularidades relacionado con el hospital Posadas.


Previo al desplazamiento de la conducción nacional, el sindicato metalúrgico había rechazado varios planteos empresarios para la instauración de bancos de horas. Sólo en la seccional de Furlán habían corrido esa suerte los pedidos de los dueños de Industrias Guidi, en Zárate, y Maro, de Baradero, dos autopartistas que abastecen mayoritariamente a la firma Toyota. El único antecedente reportado hasta ahora de un banco de horas acordado entre una patronal y un gremio desde la sanción de la ley 27.802 es el de Mirgor para sus autopartistas en Garín y Baradero, con la firma del sindicato de mecánicos Smata.


“Es inaceptable que esto se firme a espaldas de los trabajadores. El interventor debería estar preocupado por hacer lo que le ordena la Justicia, que es llamar a elecciones en Campana, y en lugar de eso toma decisiones sobre el convenio colectivo de trabajo y firma esta aberración. Perjudican a los trabajadores y al futuro de sus derechos”, le avisó a este medio Walter Piriz, dirigente local de la UOM y representante gremial en la firma Tenaris. Piriz es uno de los referentes desplazados por Biglieri, que eligió rodearse en la intevención de dirigentes opositores a Furlán con quienes incluso llegó a un acuerdo por una paritaria demorada varios meses y con una pérdida de al menos 11 puntos en el poder adquisitivo de los obreros de la actividad.

What it means to be libertarian

Yes, it is that time of the year again – the London Anarchist Bookfair. This year’s Bookfair will be on Saturday 28th October from 10am to 7pm at Park View School, West Green Road, London, N15 3QR. As usual, I have a talk entitled – after some humming-and-hawing about doing a Poverty of Philosophy related one (too niche) – as follows:

2017 marks 160 years since Joseph Déjacque coined the word “libertarian” in an open letter challenging Proudhon’s patriarchal and market socialist views. By the dawn of the twentieth century, anarchists across the world had embraced the term. Today, it is now increasingly associated with the far-right. How did this happen? What does it mean to be a libertarian? Can you be a right-wing libertarian? Can we reclaim the word for the twenty-first century? These questions as well as the history of “libertarian” will be explored by Iain McKay, author of “An Anarchist FAQ”.

There seem to be a lot of Russian Revolution ones this year, so just as well I got in early last year with The Bolshevik Myth Reloaded. Talking of the Russian revolution, I have a chapter in a new book by AK Press entitled Bloodstained: One Hundred Years of Leninist Counterrevolution. title: Was Trump 2019 in den USA begann breitet sich international aus: Die (stellvertretende) Verfolgung der Antifa-Bewegung als „terroristischer Organisation“
content:
Dossier


Wie es begann:

„Einstufung als Terrorgruppe?“ am 28. Juli 2019 in der taz online


 ist eine dpa-Meldung, die zu den Drohungen gegen die Antifa berichtet – unter anderem, dass dies eine Parteiaktion sei: „

US-Präsident Donald Trump erwägt nach eigenen Worten, die Antifa-Bewegung in den USA als terroristische Organisation einzustufen. Man ziehe diesen Schritt in Betracht, schrieb Trump am Samstag auf Twitter. „Das würde es der Polizei erleichtern, ihre Arbeit zu machen“, fügte er noch hinzu. Trump hatte die Antifa zuletzt mehrfach kritisiert. So sprach er etwa bei einer Wahlkampfveranstaltung davon, dass es sich bei den Aktivisten um „kranke, schlimme“ Menschen handele. (…) Die beiden republikanischen Senatoren Ted Cruz und Bill Cassidy hatten vor wenigen Tagen eine Resolution eingebracht, in der sie sich dafür aussprechen, dass Gruppen, die der Antifa-Bewegung zuzuordnen seien, als inländische Terrororganisationen eingestuft würden. Bei Aktivisten der Antifa handele es sich um „gewalttätige, maskierte Tyrannen“, erklärte Cassidy..

.“ Siehe unsere damalige Berichterstattung und die neue Entwicklung in den USA, aber auch Niederlande und Ungarn…


Die USA sanktionieren das italienische Tech-Kollektiv „Autistici/Inventati“ (u.a. NoBlogs.org) als Infrastruktur zur „Unterstützung von Terrorismus der extremen Linken“ 


Autistici/Inventati: Geht hin und vermehrt euch! Mögen 10 – 100 – 1000 Server entfacht werden (Zerschlagt ihr eine Kommunikationsstruktur, pflanzen wir viele neue nach)


„

In diesen Zeiten fanatischer, ideologischer und unbegründeter Unterdrückung habt ihr uns oft gefragt: „Wie können wir euch unterstützen?“


Die erste Antwort, die uns in den Sinn gekommen ist, lautet: Wenn ihr helfen wollt, schafft neue Räume im Internet. Es gibt viel zu wenige autonome Server da draussen, sei es für E-Mail und Webhosting oder für andere nützliche Kommunikationsmittel. Diese Idee ist keineswegs neu. Wir wiederholen sie schon seit März 2001, als A/I sein Abenteuer begann. Schon damals hatten wir dazu aufgerufen, unzählige selbstverwaltete Server zu schaffen, und mit dieser Hoffnung im Hinterkopf prägten wir den pseudobiblischen Satz: „Geht hin und vermehrt euch, sagten die Heuschrecken!“


So sehr diese Worte damals auch wie eine paranoide Cyberpunk-Prophezeiung geklungen haben mögen, so erweisen sie sich heute als dringende Notwendigkeit.


Geht also hin und vermehrt euch. Kopiert uns. Kopiert, was wir getan haben. Kopiert den Code, den wir verwendet haben. Kopiert die Idee, der wir Gestalt zu geben versucht haben. Oder nehmt einfach, was ihr von uns braucht, und remixt es. Wenn es etwas gibt, das unsere Gegner fürchten und verabscheuen – jetzt, in der Vergangenheit und für immer –, dann ist es unsere Fähigkeit, den Virus der Selbstverwaltung und Selbstbestimmung zu verbreiten und Infrastrukturen des Widerstands fraktal zu replizieren.


Autistici/Inventati, das sind nicht nur wir. Autistici/Inventati mag sterben, aber Tausende sind bereits geboren worden und Tausende weitere werden entstehen.


Und das ist noch nicht alles. Was sich überall um uns herum abspielt, ist eine koordinierte Strategie zur Verschärfung der Repression mit dem Ziel, nicht nur die Spielregeln, sondern das Spielfeld selbst grundlegend zu verändern. Das bedeutet, dass das, was gerade geschieht, nicht nur eine Handvoll Menschen betrifft, sondern gemeinsam und so breit wie möglich angegangen werden muss – von Einzelpersonen, autonomen Projekten, Organisationen und der gesamten Gesellschaft.


Auf dem Spiel stehen die Meinungs-, Informations- und Vereinigungsfreiheit sowie die blosse Existenz einer Infrastruktur, die in der Lage ist, dem Autoritarismus Widerstand zu leisten (nicht nur in den Vereinigten Staaten). Auf dem Spiel steht die Möglichkeit, überall weiter dafür zu kämpfen, grundlegende Gemeingüter – wie Kommunikationsinfrastrukturen – vor dem Imperialismus bestimmter Akteure zu verteidigen.


Das geht weit über uns selbst hinaus. Es betrifft jeden, der leben will, ohne sich als Ware zu fühlen, und danach strebt, sein Leben und seine Beziehungen selbst zu bestimmen. Wenn wir diesem voranschreitenden Technofaschismus Widerstand leisten wollen, brauchen wir eine breite internationale Solidaritätsbewegung, um Rahmenbedingungen zu schaffen, die autonome Infrastrukturen und Räume schützen, die frei von jeglicher autoritärer Absicht sind

…“

Statement von Autistici/Inventati vom 12.9.2026 im Untergrund-Blättle am 15. September 2026 …

author: Redazione_web
title: Patriot Platform. Un nuovo volto per il fascismo
content:
Pubblichiamo la traduzione di un articolo pubblicato dal media anarchico organise.org.uk


magazine della Anarchist Federation in UK


Sabato 5 settembre, diverse centinaia di fascisti mascherati hanno paralizzato Dover. La notte successiva, un numero simile di persone ha bloccato le strade a Portsmouth, in seguito alle notizie sull’arrivo di rifugiati soccorsi dalla RNLI (Royal National Lifeboat Institution). Chi erano, come sono riusciti ad andarsene senza essere arrestati e cosa potrebbe succedere ora?


I retroscena


Nonostante quanto riportato da alcuni giornalisti e da una dichiarazione della polizia del Kent, questa azione era ben lungi dall’essere «spontanea»; è piuttosto chiaro che fosse stata preparata con largo anticipo. Alcuni streamer di orientamento di destra hanno parlato con i partecipanti durante l’azione, i quali hanno ripetutamente affermato che fosse stata organizzata dalla Patriot Platform. Hope Not Hate ha persino rivelato che la polizia del Kent ne era sicuramente a conoscenza in anticipo, poiché il giorno prima erano state ricevute segnalazioni dirette al riguardo.


Patriot Platform (PP) è un’organizzazione relativamente nuova, lanciata nel giugno di quest’anno, ma le sue radici risalgono a molto tempo prima. PP è guidata da Daniel Thomas (che preferisce farsi chiamare Danny Tommo – forse nel tentativo di nascondere il fatto di aver frequentato una scuola privata). Thomas è salito alla ribalta per la prima volta quando è stato condannato per il tentato rapimento di un uomo che aveva (erroneamente) accusato di aver rubato droga per un valore di 10.000 sterline. È stato dopo questo episodio che si è dedicato all’attività organizzativa di estrema destra, acquisendo notorietà come “guardia del corpo” di Tommy Robinson e diventando uno degli organizzatori di ciò che restava dell’UKIP dopo l’uscita di scena di Nigel Farage. Thomas ha continuato a tessere legami in tutto l’ambiente dell’estrema destra, stringendo amicizia con gruppi come i South East Patriots, che in seguito avrebbe reclutato per le azioni del PP. Ha attirato ulteriore attenzione per i suoi viaggi internazionali e per le sue azioni contro rifugiati e altri migranti. Si è recato in Francia con Raise the Colours, finendo per essere espulso dal Paese per aver molestato operatori umanitari e rifugiati. Cosa che ha poi ripetuto anche da questa parte della Manica. Si è recato anche a Belfast in occasione delle rivolte razziste e dei pogrom che vi hanno avuto luogo. Come molti esponenti dell’estrema destra, parla di proteggere le donne, ma si circonda di persone con precedenti di violenza domestica.


In questo contesto di estrema destra, ha iniziato a reclutare figure di spicco per dare vita alla Patriot Platform. Ha organizzato una serie di incontri in tutto il Paese, durante i quali ha reclutato fascisti locali alla sua causa. Sebbene alcuni filmati di questi incontri siano stati pubblicati online, essi erano – per la maggior parte – segreti, organizzati con largo anticipo e “solo su invito”. Il gruppo che hanno creato non è affatto discreto nella sua ideologia o nelle sue intenzioni. Gli incontri si svolgevano come rievocazioni militari e il loro sito web è pieno di messaggi in codice tipici dell’estrema destra. Hanno chiaramente preso spunto dal fascismo di stampo nazionalista cristiano americano. Fanno riferimento alla «patria», al «futuro dei vostri figli» e alla «vera Gran Bretagna». Sul suo profilo Instagram personale, Thomas si definisce un «difensore della fede» e descrive le sue routine di allenamento come «preparazione alla guerra», paragonando il suo gruppo all’English Defence League, con l’obiettivo di «prendere il controllo del Paese». Sebbene la narrazione degli streamer di estrema destra e la stessa cronaca di Thomas abbiano sottolineato la non violenza di quel giorno, sembra importante evidenziare questi richiami all’estetica fascista, l’uso del linguaggio della violenza, le origini del gruppo nella militanza regionale di estrema destra e i precedenti di violenza dei membri chiave quando si valuta la loro capacità di compiere azioni violente in futuro.


Mentre il gruppo si stava formando dietro le quinte, i suoi membri hanno iniziato a parlare pubblicamente dei preparativi per “lanciare un messaggio”, con un’azione che avrebbe avuto luogo “molto, molto presto”. Un’organizzazione di questa portata richiede o un lungo lavoro di mobilitazione dal basso, oppure un ingente conto in banca. PP ha scelto la seconda opzione …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Modern-Day Fascism Isn’t a Rerun — It Is “End Times Fascism”
content:
A new book examines how wealthy elites are preparing for “the end of the world” even as they drive growing crises.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor launch their new book, End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World on Democracy Now! It examines how wealthy elites are preparing for “the end of the world,” even as they contribute to growing inequality, political instability and the climate crisis. The rise of modern-day fascism is “not simply a rerun,” explains Klein. “We don’t believe that history repeats on a loop. We believe that we’re in something more like a sequel, where the logics of fascism, which are the logics of dehumanization, of othering, of racial supremacy and hierarchy, are now being applied in a time of global existential crisis.” In response, says Taylor, the growing movement seeking to resist this fatalistic vision “fundamentally needs to be grounded in a desire to stay here on Earth, to commit to this place.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, Democracynow.org, the War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman in New York joined by Democracy Now! cohost Juan González in Chicago. Hi, Juan.

JUAN GONZÁLEZ: Hi, Amy, and welcome to all of our listeners and viewers across the country and around the world.

AMY GOODMAN: “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us by the end of the decade.” That was the warning last week from former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon that set off an escalating debate over how to regulate increasingly powerful AI systems. Coxon spoke to the BBC.

COXON: So it’s not at all an exaggeration to say that the people who were involved with both founding these companies and building the tech believe there is a possibility of human extinction. And many of the people who are sort of deep in the weeds on actually coding the thing believe that there is like a greater than 10% chance or even greater—some smaller, but they all have different numbers—for a probability that humans might die. And they all keep this in their head on a daily basis while working on the technology.

AMY GOODMAN: Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei also called for the pace of development of artificial intelligence models to slow down. In an essay, he wrote that within six to 12 months a swarm of AI agents could be capable of taking over the entire internet and cause hundreds of billions of dollars in damage. He wrote, “The scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails.” But President Trump has rejected growing calls for placing regulatory guardrails on the AI industry and has called concerns over AI a “hoax.” On Monday, Trump called Jensen Huang, the CEO of the computer chip maker Nvidia, while Huang was speaking at an AI summit in Los Angeles. Huang put the president on speakerphone.

PRES. TRUMP: The data centers are great and they make people wealthy and they make states wealthy and it’s the oil of the next 20, 25 years. It’s bigger than the Internet. And the AI, you know, much more so. And they are just playing right into the hands of a lot of people that don’t want to see it happen. And that could be political people; it could also be China. And we’re not going to let that happen. It’s a hoax. And [crosstalk]—

JENSEN HUANG [laughs] You’re right. We’re not going to let that happen, sir.

PRES. TRUMP: No, we’re not going to let it happen. The robots are not going to be taking over the world.

AMY GOODMAN: As the debate over AI intensifies, the award-winning journalists and writers Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor have a new book out today that is connected to all of this. It is titled End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World. It examines how wealthy elites, including tech CEOs, are preparing for the end of the world even as they contribute to growing inequality, political instability, wars and the climate crisis. They will join us in a minute but first, here is a short excerpt from a video that was released with the book.

ASTRA TAYLOR: End-times fascism is not a monolith. It’s a dangerous and fractious alliance of three main groups.

NARRATOR: Religious end-timers.

ROBERT JEFFRESS: From the very beginning it has been clear that god has a special plan and purpose for the nation of Israel.

SAM ALTMAN …

title: Budapest: Revision gegen Maja beginnt
content:
Budapest: Revision gegen Maja beginnt


Am 18. September 2026 beginnt in Budapest das Revisionsverfahren gegen Maja, Gabri und Anna, die im sog. Budapest-Komplex beschuldigt werden, sich an körperlichen Auseinandersetzungen mit Nazis beteiligt zu haben. Im Gegensatz zu den Mitangeklagten ist Maja seit über zwei Jahren unter menschenunwürdigen Bedingungen in ungarischer Haft, nachdem die deutschen Behörden die non-binäre Person aus Jena im Juni 2024 offen rechtswidrig ausgeliefert hatten. In der ersten Instanz war Maja zu acht Jahren Zuchthaus verurteilt worden, doch die Staatsanwaltschaft beharrt auf der Forderung der Höchststrafe von 24 Jahren. Als zweiten Verhandlungstag im Revisionsprozess ist der 30. September 2026 festgesetzt, an dem das Urteil fallen soll.

Der konkrete Vorfall, der im Budapest-Komplex verfolgt wird, ist juristisch gesehen ein banales Körperverletzungsdelikt: Gemeinsam mit weiteren Antifaschist*innen sollen sich Maja, Gabri und Anna an körperlichen Auseinandersetzungen mit Nazis am Rand des

NS

-verherrlichenden Großevents „Tag der Ehre“ im Februar 2023 in Budapest beteiligt haben. Seither läuft eine deutsch-ungarische Hetzjagd auf Antifaschist*innen, in deren Zuge Maja im Dezember 2023 in Berlin verhaftet wurde. Ende Juni 2024 lieferten die deutschen Behörden die non-binäre Person aus Jena in einer offen rechtswidrigen Nacht-und-Nebel-Aktion an das rechtsautoritäre und offen queerfeindliche Ungarn aus. Gegen die folterähnlichen Haftbedingungen im Budapester Untersuchungsgefängnis trat Maja im Sommer 2025 in wochenlangen Hungerstreik. Am 17. Juli 2026 eskalierten die Schikanen durch das Gefängnispersonal, als eine Gruppe vermummter und bewaffneter Wächter Maja brutal misshandelte, verletzte und für die danach nötige ärztliche Untersuchung unter Zwang entkleidete. In der Folge wurde die non-binäre Person noch mit Disziplinarstrafen und verschärfter Dauerisolation wegen angeblichen Angriffs auf die Wächter belegt, die erst nach mehrwöchiger anwaltlicher Intervention aufgehoben wurden. Anlass war, dass Maja selbstbestimmt Kleidung getragen hatte, die das queerfeindliche ungarische Personal als missliebige Frauenkleidung einstufte. Der erstinstanzliche Prozess in Budapest, der im Frühjahr 2025 begann, war von Anfang an vom systematischen Verzicht auf alle rechtsstaatlichen Minimalstandards geprägt: Majas Vorbereitung wurde massiv behindert, indem Gespräche mit der Verteidigung nur mit Trennscheibe stattfinden konnten, die meisten Akten nicht übersetzt wurden und Unterlagen und Videos in der Haft kaum einsehbar waren. Der Charakter eines offenen politischen Schauprozesses wurde durch die absurden Sicherheitsmaßnahmen und die Inszenierungen an jedem Verhandlungstag deutlich: Indem Maja in Hand- und Fußfesseln und an einer Hundeleine in den Gerichtssaal geführt wurde, wollte das Gericht die angeklagte Person zusätzlich demütigen. Gegen die beiden mitbeschuldigten Antifaschist*innen Gabri und Anna wurde in Abwesenheit verhandelt.Der Prozess erbrachte keinerlei Beweise, dass die drei Angeklagten an den körperlichen Auseinandersetzungen beteiligt oder auch nur vor Ort waren. Trotzdem forderte die Staatsanwaltschaft für Maja eine „möglichst hohe Strafe zur Abschreckung“, was 24 Jahre Zuchthaus bedeutet. Am 4. Februar 2026 wurden Maja zu acht Jahren Zuchthaus, Gabri zu sieben Jahre Haft und Anna zu einer Bewährungsstrafe von zwei Jahren verurteilt. Die Staatsanwaltschaft ging umgehend in Revision, woraufhin sich die Verteidigung anschloss.

„In der ersten Instanz machte das Budapester Gericht deutlich, dass bereits die Beschuldigung des engagierten Antifaschismus in Ungarn als Kapitalverbrechen gilt. Der Schauprozess sollte ganz offensichtlich ein Exempel statuieren, um die antifaschistische Bewegung einzuschüchtern. Auch für die Revision ist zu befürchten, dass rechtsstaatliche Standards mit Füßen getreten werden“, erklärte Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. V. „Umso wichtiger ist es, politischen Druck aufzubauen und den Prozess aufmerksam zu beobachten: Das Unrechtsurteil gegen Maja, Gabri und Anna muss aufgehoben werden. Die deutsche Regierung und die zuständigen Behörden müssen endlich das Urteil des Bundesverfassungsgerichts umsetzen und sich nach der rechtswidrigen Auslieferung für Majas Freilassung und Rückkehr einsetzen.“ Abschließend erklärte er: „Unsere volle Solidarität gilt Maja und den beiden anderen verurteilten Antifaschist*innen. 12. September 2026


In diesen Zeiten fanatischer, ideologischer und unbegründeter Unterdrückung habt ihr uns oft gefragt: „Wie können wir euch unterstützen?“


Die erste Antwort, die uns in den Sinn gekommen ist, lautet: Wenn ihr helfen wollt, schafft neue Räume im Internet. Es gibt viel zu wenige autonome Server da draußen, sei es für E-Mail und Webhosting oder für andere nützliche Kommunikationsmittel.


Diese Idee ist keineswegs neu. Wir wiederholen sie schon seit März 2001, als A/I sein Abenteuer begann. Schon damals hatten wir dazu aufgerufen, unzählige selbstverwaltete Server zu schaffen, und mit dieser Hoffnung im Hinterkopf prägten wir den pseudobiblischen Satz: „Geht hin und vermehrt euch, sagten die Heuschrecken!“


So sehr diese Worte damals auch wie eine paranoide Cyberpunk-Prophezeiung geklungen haben mögen, so erweisen sie sich heute als dringende Notwendigkeit.


Geht also hin und vermehrt euch. Kopiert uns. Kopiert, was wir getan haben. Kopiert den Code, den wir verwendet haben. Kopiert die Idee, der wir Gestalt zu geben versucht haben. Oder nehmt einfach, was ihr von uns braucht, und remixt es. Wenn es etwas gibt, das unsere Gegner fürchten und verabscheuen – jetzt, in der Vergangenheit und für immer –, dann ist es unsere Fähigkeit, den Virus der Selbstverwaltung und Selbstbestimmung zu verbreiten und Infrastrukturen des Widerstands fraktal zu replizieren.


Autistici/Inventati, das sind nicht nur wir. Autistici/Inventati mag sterben, aber Tausende sind bereits geboren worden und Tausende weitere werden entstehen.


Und das ist noch nicht alles. Was sich überall um uns herum abspielt, ist eine koordinierte Strategie zur Verschärfung der Repression mit dem Ziel, nicht nur die Spielregeln, sondern das Spielfeld selbst grundlegend zu verändern. Das bedeutet, dass das, was gerade geschieht, nicht nur eine Handvoll Menschen betrifft, sondern gemeinsam und so breit wie möglich angegangen werden muss – von Einzelpersonen, autonomen Projekten, Organisationen und der gesamten Gesellschaft.


Auf dem Spiel stehen die Meinungs-, Informations- und Vereinigungsfreiheit sowie die bloße Existenz einer Infrastruktur, die in der Lage ist, dem Autoritarismus (nicht nur in den Vereinigten Staaten) Widerstand zu leisten. Auf dem Spiel steht die Möglichkeit, überall weiter dafür zu kämpfen, grundlegende Gemeingüter – wie Kommunikationsinfrastrukturen – vor dem Imperialismus bestimmter Akteure zu verteidigen.


Das geht weit über uns selbst hinaus. Es betrifft jeden, der leben will, ohne sich als Ware zu fühlen, und danach strebt, sein Leben und seine Beziehungen selbst zu bestimmen. Wenn wir diesem voranschreitenden Technofaschismus Widerstand leisten wollen, brauchen wir eine breite internationale Solidaritätsbewegung, um Rahmenbedingungen zu schaffen, die autonome Infrastrukturen und Räume schützen, die frei von jeglicher autoritärer Absicht sind.


Kommen wir also zurück zu der Frage, mit der wir begonnen haben: Wir sind euch allen dankbar, die ihr die Geschichte dessen erzählt habt, was uns widerfahren ist. Wir sind dankbar für die große Solidarität, die ihr uns entgegengebracht habt, und für euer Verständnis dafür, dass das, was uns widerfahren ist, nur ein kleiner Schritt in der Kette von Ereignissen ist, die sich wahrscheinlich noch entfalten werden – sicherlich zum Schlechten, aber vielleicht auch zum Guten.


Diese Vision erfüllt unsere Herzen. Doch nun ist es an der Zeit, einen Schritt weiter zu gehen und unsere Vorstellungskraft über die schrumpfenden Horizonte des Möglichen hinauszuschieben, die uns diese dunklen Zeiten aufzwingen. Unsere Hoffnung ist, dass dieser Angriff auf die Freiheit der Netzwerke einen kraftvollen und kreativen kollektiven Widerstand entfesselt. Mögen tausend Plattformen erblühen, mögen tausend Hacktivisten-Kollektive entstehen, mögen tausend Server aufleben! Möge das Ende von A/I eine Unzahl von Infrastrukturen des Widerstands hervorbringen, wie wir sie uns zuvor nie hätten vorstellen können.


Geht hinaus und vermehrt euch, sagten die Heuschrecken! Und während ihr dabei seid, versucht euch eine Welt des Kampfes, des Widerstands und der Selbstverwaltung vorzustellen, wie ihr sie noch nie gesehen habt.


AUTISTICI/INVENTATI COLLECTIVE
