author: anred
title: Otra vez la amenaza de desalojo a comunidades mapuche en las Lof Melo y Kinxikew
content:
Foto: Pilar Mateos


La Justicia neuquina volvió a avanzar con el desalojo de las comunidades mapuche Lof Melo y Lof Kinxikew, en el paraje El Pedregoso, entre Villa La Angostura y Bariloche. Mientras permanece pendiente la ejecución de la medida, la Confederación Mapuche de Neuquén reclamó al gobernador Rolando Figueroa que intervenga para detenerla. Tambièn, el propio Gobierno provincial reconoció este viernes la personería jurídica del Lof Melo, después de 14 años de trámite. Por ANRed


La nueva amenaza surge luego del operativo del 19 de agosto, cuando efectivos de la Policía de Neuquén y del grupo especial GEOP ingresaron al territorio para ejecutar una orden judicial. En aquella jornada fue desalojada una parte del predio recuperada por integrantes del Lof Melo. El procedimiento quedó inconcluso cuando las fuerzas debían avanzar sobre otro sector donde se encontraban menores y no estaban presentes funcionarios de organismos de protección de la infancia. Ahora, el juez Francisco Astoul Bonorino libró un nuevo mandamiento para completar el desalojo del sector donde permanecen integrantes del Lof Kinxikew. La medida todavía no tiene fecha de ejecución pero las cominidades ya anunciaron que permanecen en alerta y movilizados. En aquella fecha, una multitud se acercò para solidarizarse y logrò la suspensiòn del desalojo.


La nueva orden judicial vuelve a colocar a las comunidades en estado de alerta. El conflicto se desarrolla sobre un predio de unas 625 hectáreas atravesado por la Ruta Nacional 40, en el paraje El Pedregoso. El expediente se inició en 2011 y la denuncia por usurpación fue presentada en 2012 por María Cristina Broers, quien sostiene ser propietaria del inmueble desde 1969. Con el paso de los años, integrantes de la familia Quintriqueo se incorporaron a la recuperaciòn de su ancestral territorio y conformaron el Lof Kinxikew. Distintas instancias judiciales mantuvieron la orden de restitución del inmueble.


Pero para las comunidades y la Confederación Mapuche el conflicto no puede reducirse a una disputa entre particulares. Los Consejos Zonales reclamaron al gobernador Figueroa una intervención urgente y señalaron que el territorio del Lof Melo fue relevado como

Ocupación Tradicional y Pública (OTP)

. También cuestionaron que la comunidad haya tenido que atravesar durante años el trámite para obtener su personería jurídica.


La situación suma ahora un elemento particularmente significativo:

el 11 de septiembre, un día después de que se conociera el nuevo mandamiento de desalojo, el Gobierno de Neuquén reconoció oficialmente la personería jurídica del Lof Melo

. El Decreto 1402/2026 sostiene que la comunidad cumple con los requisitos establecidos por la Constitución Nacional y Provincial, el Convenio 169 de la OIT, la Ley 23.302 y demás normativa vigente, y reconoce su domicilio en el paraje Paso Coihue, departamento Los Lagos.


La Confederación Mapuche sostiene que el reconocimiento llega después de

14 años de trámites

, y reclama que esa nueva situación sea considerada en el expediente de desalojo. En una comunicación dirigida al gobernador, las autoridades mapuche advirtieron sobre la gravedad de ejecutar una medida de estas características y reclamaron que la Provincia intervenga para evitar una nueva avanzada policial.


Mientras tanto, la Justicia mantiene abierta la posibilidad de completar el operativo. La nueva orden está dirigida principalmente al sector donde permanece el Lof Kinxikew, luego de que en agosto la Policía avanzara sobre la fracción ocupada por el Lof Melo. La ejecución aún no tiene fecha, pero el mandamiento ya fue librado.

author: Nahuel Lag
title: El modelo Arauco en Misiones: amenazas, detenciones y casas quemadas con complicidad estatal
content:
Por Clarisa Néztor


Puerto Argentino 1, 2 y 3, Palmera Boca y San Juan Bosco son parajes rurales del municipio de San Pedro, en el nordeste de Misiones. La Comisión Vecinos Unidos por las Chacras reúne en esos parajes a cerca de 200 familias que producen alimentos en pequeñas parcelas para sostener sus economías.

Desde hace años sufren una persecución sistemática de violencia institucional y un hostigamiento permanente por parte de la forestal Arauco,

 que los acusa de ocupar tierras a pesar de no presentar cargos formales ante el Poder Judicial. En las últimas semanas, la violencia escaló con una represión cuyo objetivo fue sembrar el terror y forzar a las familias a abandonar sus chacras. “Ni Arauco, ni el gobierno municipal ni el provincial nos mostraron un título de propiedad”, sostiene Diego Antúnez, productor y presidente de la comisión de vecinos a quien le incendiaron su casa a fines de agosto.   


Los productores describen cómo el personal de Arauco, acompañado por la Policía de Misiones, ingresa a las chacras sin órdenes de desalojo, realiza amenazas, detenciones y prende fuego las viviendas de madera. Las denuncias de las familias campesinas fueron públicas y radicadas ante el Poder Judicial de San Pedro. Las personas perjudicadas exigen la respuesta del gobernador de Misiones, Hugo Passalacqua, y la regularización de las tierras. 


La situación desatada a mediados de agosto, llevó a los vecinos a mantener varios días de acampe frente al Municipio de San Pedro, donde el intendente Miguel Ángel Dos Santos lleva tres años sin darles respuestas. En Posadas, la comisión de vecinos se reunió en varias oportunidades con Daniel Behler, subsecretario provincial de Tierras y Colonización, quien se comprometió a avanzar con un relevamiento de las familias afectadas, solicitar información sobre el accionar policial denunciado y abrir una mesa de diálogo con Arauco, al que la empresa nunca se presentó.


La última reunión de la comisión de Vecinos Unidos por las Chacras con el subsecretario Behler ocurrió este miércoles. Antúnez contó a

Tierra Viva

 que el funcionario provincial volvió a pedirle a las familias un relevamiento de las chacras en las que producen para poder cruzarlo con la documentación oficial. La comisión de vecinos, que ya había dejado una carpeta con el relevamiento de las chacras, actualizó la información y precisó que son 164 familias que cultivan sus alimentos en 2.300 hectáreas. Sin embargo, no todas las hectáreas son productivas: muchas de ellas mantienen el monte nativo. 


El presidente de la Comisión Vecinos Unidos por las Chacras, Diego Antúnez (izquierda) y una comitiva de familias tras la reunión en la Subsecretaria de Tierras y Colonización. Foto: XR-Misiones


“

Le pedimos (a Behler) la paz. Pedimos que intervengan ante Arauco y la Policía para que cesen con la violencia que están ejerciendo

: el hostigamiento, la persecución, el desalojo arbitrario, la quema de casas. Responsabilizamos al gobierno, directamente, de todo lo que pasó y de lo que va a seguir pasando. El gobierno de Misiones no nos da seguridad y nuestras vidas corren peligro con Arauco”, exigió Antúnez desde Posadas. Allí, junto a una comitiva de colonos, también radicó denuncias ante la Defensoría del Pueblo y la Jefatura de Policía de Misiones. 


La violencia de la empresa forestal recrudeció en espejo con dos normativas tratadas en el Senado nacional con particular interés para Arauco: tras la media sanción de la

“Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada”

 —que mantuvo el capítulo sobre desalojos exprés— y durante el dictamen en el Senado de un proyecto para crear

mercados de carbono

, impulsado por la

Mesa de Carbono Argentina

, integrada por la forestal. 


La multinacional, de capitales chilenos, es

una de los principales propietarios privados de tierras de Misiones

. Está presente en esa provincia desde 1996 y fue adquiriendo hectáreas de plantaciones forestales y áreas naturales por un total aproximadamente 230.000 hectáreas. La vasta extensión territorial está mantiene continuos conflictos por la posesión de la tierra con

familias campesinas

 y

comunidades Mbya Guaraní

, pero el caso de las familias rurales de San Pedro

 se transformó en una emergencia social, habitacional y territorial por los constantes ataques registrados en el último mes

. 


Producir alimentos no es delito

title: AI: Iran committed crimes against humanity during the suppression of 'Jin, Jiyan, Azadi' uprising
content:
In a landmark new report marking the fourth anniversary of the start of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadi’ (Woman, Life, Freedom) uprising, Amnesty International warns that those responsible for crimes against humanity committed to brutally crush nationwide protests in 2022 continue to control Iran’s deadly state machinery of repression today.  


The report, 

Architects of Atrocities: State Machinery Orchestrating Crimes Against Humanity in Iran’s 2022 Woman Life Freedom Uprising

 –more than 1,000 pages long – details how Iranian authorities committed the crimes against humanity of murder, torture, enforced disappearance, imprisonment, rape and persecution on political, gender, ethnic and religious grounds in order to crush the uprising. It also documents deadly protest repression operations and command structures, identifying 87 officials who should be criminally investigated for crimes against humanity.  


Amnesty International is calling for an international criminal justice mechanism to be established urgently by the UN General Assembly to ensure Iranian authorities responsible for crimes against humanity are held to account and to deter further atrocities such as the large-scale protest massacres committed on 8-9 January 2026.  


In light of the ongoing hostilities following unlawful attacks by the USA and Israel on Iran, Amnesty International also reiterates its call for an enduring ceasefire and independent investigations into attacks committed during the conflict. The organization calls for the UN to address accountability for violations of the UN Charter and of international humanitarian law, including possible war crimes.  


“The extensive evidence gathered and analysed in our report leaves no doubt: Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity to crush the 2022 Woman Life Freedom uprising. They waged a widespread and systematic attack against a civilian population demanding dignity, human rights and fundamental political change, pursuant to a state policy of using lethal force to obliterate dissent,” said Agnès Callamard, Amnesty International’s Secretary General. 


“Our report also unveils how crimes against humanity in Iran are sustained by an architecture of impunity built into the country’s constitutional, legislative, political and judicial frameworks. The horrifying result has been intensifying cycles of mass protest killings, culminating in the massacres of thousands of protesters within just 48 hours on 8-9 January 2026. The UN General Assembly must end the unconscionable normalization of mass protest killings in Iran and create an international criminal justice mechanism aimed at prosecuting those most implicated in crimes against humanity.  


“This report is being published at a time when people in Iran are also facing the devastating consequences of unlawful attacks by the USA and Israel. Amnesty International unequivocally opposes violations of international law by all parties and rejects any attempt to instrumentalize the suffering of victims of human rights violations in Iran to justify unlawful attacks that inflict further civilian harm.  


“For years, Iranian people have faced brutal repression, persecution and impunity at the hands of their own authorities. Today, many are also bearing the human cost of unlawful military action carried out by the USA and Israel. A principled response requires rejecting both impunity for crimes against humanity and unlawful use of force. The international community must pursue people-centred diplomatic strategies that place civilian protection, atrocity prevention, justice and accountability at their core. After more than six months of air strikes that have killed and injured civilians, damaged the environment, and caused significant destruction of civilian infrastructure, an enduring ceasefire is urgently needed alongside independent investigations and action by the UN General Assembly to address accountability for violations of the UN Charter and of international humanitarian law and possible war crimes committed by all parties to the conflict.” 


Amnesty International’s report, released four years after the death in custody of Zhina Mahsa Amini at the hands of the “morality” police sparked nationwide protests, documents how the Iranian authorities mobilized security forces armed with military-grade firearms and shotguns loaded with metal pellets and issued orders that facilitated the unlawful killing of hundreds of protesters and bystanders …

title: Kundgebung: Iraner*innen fordern mehr Klarheit von Beat Jans und dem SEM
content:
Heute ab 12 Uhr demonstrieren abgewiesene Iraner*

innen vor dem Staatssekretariat für Migration (SEM) in Wabern. Die Kundgebung wird von der Gruppe Empathie und Einheit organisiert. Kritisiert werden Beat Jans und das SEM, die die verallgemeinerte Gewalt im Iran nicht genügend klar anerkennen. Dies führt für Iraner

*

innen in der Schweiz zu einschneidenden und weitreichenden Problemen.


«Die Vogel-Strauss-Politik muss ein Ende haben.»


 (Empathie und Einheit

)


Die Sicherheitslage im Iran sei unübersichtlich.

 So lautet die unbefriedigende Einschätzung von Bundesrat und SEM seit Anfangs dieses Jahres. Ausschaffungen in den Iran wurden deshalb zwar sistiert, jedoch nicht eindeutig als unzumutbar, unzulässig und/oder unmöglich eingestuft. Gemäss dem Asylgesetz liegt es an Beat Jans, sich hierzu politisch zu positionieren. Falls die Lage im Iran einer Situation allgemeiner Gewalt entspricht, müsste den insgesamt knapp 300 abgewiesenen Iraner*innen mindestens eine vorläufige Aufnahme gewährt werden.


Es ist die neunte monatliche Kundgebung vor dem SEM.

 Die abgewiesenen Iraner*innen engagieren sich für eine Asylpraxisänderung, die den Schutz iranischer Asylsuchender in der Schweiz verbessert. Mit diesem Ziel begannen Iraner*innen gestern auf dem Bundesplatz einen Hungerstreik, nachdem es bereits im Juli in Zürich zu einem

einwöchigen Sitzstreik

 kam. Damals wurde ein

offener Brief

 mit Forderungen an Bundesrat Jans und das SEM geschickt. Dieser blieb bisher jedoch unbeantwortet.


15.9.2026: Hungerstreik auf dem Bundesplatz.


Der Iran ist kein sicheres Land.

 Die Angriffe der israelischen und der US-amerikanischen Armee sowie die zunehmende Repression durch das iranische Regime führen im Iran zu einer Situation allgemeiner Gewalt. Diese trifft die gesamte Bevölkerung.

Die Schweizerische Flüchtlingshilfe kommt deshalb zum Schluss, dass abgewiesenen Iraner*innen mindestens eine vorläufige Aufnahme zustehen würde

.


Juli 2026: Sitzstreik in Zürich.


Die Berichte über die Lage im Iran sind eindeutig.

Hier nur einige neuere Beispiele:


Am 3. September 2026 kritisierte die UN-Fact-Finding-Mission für den Iran

 ein geplantes Gesetz, das dazu führen würde, dass iranische Medienschaffende, Forschende und politisch Aktive zu Freiheitsstrafen von bis zu 30 Jahren verurteilt werden können, wenn sie Kontakt mit ausländischen Medien, NGOs oder Universitäten haben.


Am 6. August 2026 kritisierten UN-Expert*innen

, dass das iranische Regime eine eskalierende Praxis willkürlicher Inhaftierungen, des Verschwindenlassens von Personen, der Folter und anderer Misshandlungen sowie willkürlicher Hinrichtungen von Angehörigen ethnischer Minderheiten, insbesondere der kurdischen und belutschischen Minderheiten, anordne.


Am 28. Juli 2026 kritisierte Amnesty International

, dass das iranische Regime mit einer erschreckenden Welle von Hinrichtungen und Todesurteilen vorgehe, um abweichende Meinungen zu bestrafen und zu unterdrücken sowie nach dem Aufstand im Januar und angesichts der anhaltenden Angriffe durch die USA und Israel ein Bild absoluter Kontrolle zu vermitteln.


Empathie und Einheit organisiert etwa einen Drittel aller abgewiesenen Iraner*innen in der Schweiz.

 Die meisten von ihnen sind vor mehr als fünf Jahren in die Schweiz geflüchtet. Aufgrund eines negativen Asylentscheids sind sie auf unbegrenzte Zeit blockiert. Als Nothilfebezüger*innen wird ihnen Prekarität aufgezwungen. Sie müssen von lediglich 10 Franken pro Tag leben und werden an freiheitsbeschränkenden Orten ohne Privatsphäre untergebracht. Sie dürfen zudem nicht arbeiten, haben kein Recht auf Bildung und nur einen eingeschränkten Zugang zu Gesundheitsversorgung und anderen Grundrechten.

: Retrieved on September 5 2026 from https://www.instagram.com/anarchist_front/p/Dc5QNClDfyv/


What can we actually do?


 The continued rule of a political system does not necessarily mean that it is effective or powerful. The Islamic Republic is a wounded and deeply dysfunctional system when it comes to governing the territory of Iran. Every day, it imposes greater costs on the people and on the country. Yet, relying on its machinery of repression and military forces, it continues to stand against a significant part of Iranian society. And it continues to engage in plunder and crime. The question is: given the current situation, what can we actually do?


We, as a political organization


 As a political organization, we consider institution-building and organizing to be among our responsibilities. This organizing does not take place solely through demonstrations or street actions. It also means building institutions and networks that can increase human and social resilience in times of crisis.


Institutions for times of crisis


 Human rights reporting groups, security educators, support organizations, and other independent initiatives can all play an important role during times of crisis. They can help people survive, remain standing, and preserve their dignity in the face of repression and instability. Building such structures can also reduce the human cost of confronting a heavily armed and highly organized state.


How do we do this?


 Anarchism is fundamentally defined through its connection with society and through the creativity of diverse individuals acting independently of centralized authority. We are among you. To this day, the activities of the Anarchist Front have been made possible primarily through voluntary participation. This institution-building can only happen with the support and participation of the people who follow and stand with the Anarchist Front. Our skills and abilities, combined with yours, can create the foundations for helping people and protecting our society and our land.


What will we do in the streets?


 We believe that life under domination and oppression is unacceptable. At the same time, life is precious and worth protecting, and we do not advocate pointless martyrdom. For this reason, we must take the realities on the ground into account and learn from the experience of mass killings, avoiding the loss of large numbers of lives for little or no meaningful gain.


Learning from experience


 Street demonstrations in Iran cannot simply be understood outside the reality of state repression. The Islamic Republic has created a situation in which peaceful protest faces severe repression. Iranian society will inevitably confront the question of how to respond to this reality-a reality imposed upon it by the Islamic Republic, against its will. And if society is to move beyond this situation, it will require organization, awareness, resilience, and a serious understanding of the realities it faces.


Conclusion


 When street protests alone have failed to dismantle the structure of repression, the more important question is: What can we build? Change does not happen only in the moment of an uprising. A society that wants to endure repression and crisis needs mutual aid, organization, education, documentation, and independent social institutions.


 For us, anarchism is not merely the rejection of power; it is also an effort to build capacities that emerge from within society itself.


Neither forgetting the streets, nor reducing everything to the streets.


Building society is part of the struggle.

author: Saba Chaudhry
title: A popular movement in Kashmir defies severe repression
content:
This article

A popular movement in Kashmir defies severe repression

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


When activist Shahzaib Habib was killed by unidentified men on the night of June 6 in Rawalakot, Pakistan, protesters took custody of his body from the combined military hospital and staged a sit-in outside the hospital, demanding that an investigation be opened into his murder. Habib was a close associate of the leadership of the Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee, or JAAC, a coalition of local traders, civil society members and political activists who spent the past three years organizing demonstrations across Pakistan-administered Kashmir. 


According to JAAC, security forces opened fire on the vehicle Habib was traveling in. Police say they intercepted a “suspicious vehicle” whose armed occupants fired first.


Habib’s killing came in a week when a crackdown on the JAAC was intensifying day by day. Two days earlier, on June 5, Pakistan’s government had banned JAAC, declaring the nonviolent coalition — which came together around electricity bills and wheat prices — a proscribed organization under the 2014 anti-terrorism act. In the days that followed, a curfew was imposed on Rawalakot, phone and internet were cut across the region of Azaad Jammu and Kashmir, and the government deployed the Pakistan Rangers, a paramilitary force. Protests were met

with violence

, leaving 11 dead. 


Previous Coverage


Kashmiri human rights defenders continue to fight injustices amid growing repression


Since the June 5 declaration, dozens of protesters have been arrested and many have reportedly been killed. But putting a precise number on either remains difficult. Media access to the region has been tightly restricted since the crackdown began, with phone and internet remaining suspended across much of the region.


Among those killed was one of the main student organizers: Usama Jamil, a PhD student at Quaid-i-Azam University in Islamabad who was deputy secretary general of the Jammu Kashmir National Students Federation, or JKNSF. On July 27, according to student groups and civil society organizations, he was marching in Rawalakot, chanting for people’s rights, when he was shot and killed by security forces. 


The crackdown was not confined to Kashmir. Solidarity protests in Lahore, Islamabad and Karachi were met with arrests. In Lahore, police arrested activists and dozens of bystanders outside the press club during a peaceful demonstration on July 31. In Islamabad, the capital, 88 people were sent into 14-day judicial remand after a solidarity protest the same day. Human rights groups called the arrests part of a broader attempt to criminalize solidarity with Kashmir.


I asked Omer Khan, a member of JKNSF, about the current situation. “I don’t know how to answer this or where to begin,” he said. “A living hell was unleashed upon us, something this region has not witnessed in recent history. Our region was once one of the most peaceful, and now it has almost been turned into a war zone.”


“Dozens have been killed through direct state violence, and countless others have been injured,” he continued. “Food and medicine have been blocked. Frisking, raids and searches have violated the privacy and sanctity of people’s homes” and the entire region is under an undeclared curfew. 


He describes collective punishment as one of the more visible forms of state pressure, but says the psychological toll is harder to measure.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


But for now, despite the killings, crackdowns and internet restrictions, the movement the government tried to outlaw is still organizing. On Sept. 9, the JAAC led a region-wide shutter-down and wheel-jam strike, a form of general strike that aims to shut down all businesses and halt all road traffic. As of today, protesters remain in the streets. 


How the movement got there 


Organizers say that the keys to the movement’s durability have been its flat structure, the strong participation of women, and how it has built trust and solidarity by delivering victories that affect people’s everyday lives. 


“I consider it the world’s most modern and well-organized movement, and its biggest achievement is that it built solidarity among people,” said Haris Ahmed Khan, a member of Progressive Student Collective, or PSC, who was arrested at a peaceful solidary protest in Lahore on July 31 and later …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Marcha de antorchas por la ciencia, la tecnología y la educación
content:
Denunciaron el despido de 60 trabajadores y trabajadoras de la Comisión Nacional de Energía Atómica (CNEA), también la destrucción de áreas estratégicas. Estiman que los salarios cayeron entre 40 y 45% desde noviembre de 2023 hasta la fecha.


Por Jesús Cabral @CabraAbelardo


Bajo el lema “Sin Malvinas no hay soberanía, ¡sin ciencia, trabajo y educación, tampoco!”, este jueves los trabajadores y la comunidad de la Comisión Nacional de Energía Atómica (CNEA), el Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Industrial (INTI) y la Universidad Nacional de San Martín (UNSAM), realizaron una Marcha de Antorchas.


Los manifestantes denunciaron el despido de 60 trabajadores y trabajadoras de la CNEA y el desguace por parte del Ministerio de Desregulación del Estado que conduce Federico Sturzenegger. Estiman que los salarios cayeron entre 40 y 45% desde noviembre de 2023 hasta la fecha.


Desde el Polo Tecnológico Miguelete -donde están ubicados los organismos- cruzaron por el puente peatonal hacia la colectora del lado de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, luego cruzaron por Constituyentes y volvieron a la CNEA, ubicada en Av. General Paz 1499. Se hizo en defensa de la soberanía científica, tecnológica e industrial del país.


Contra la destrucción estatal


Los manifestantes denunciaron los “despidos y el vaciamiento de los organismos científicos que son tecnológicos, la privatización de áreas que también son estratégicas, y los bajos salarios”.


También participaron ciudadanos de la comunidad sanmartinense y de los barrios aledaños al corredor de la General Paz, quienes se sumaron con sus reclamos: “La falta de acceso a la salud, la educación públicas, la vivienda, el endeudamiento y la precarización del trabajo”.


Vecinos contaron que se sumaron por los despidos y cierres de fábricas, las jubilaciones de miseria y el colapso de PAMI. Y además plantearon que “es necesario unir todas las luchas para frenar el saqueo y derrotar al gobierno libertario”.


Bases industriales destruidas


Giselle Santana es miembro de la Asamblea Multisectorial del INTI. “Una vez más salimos a las calles para denunciar el vaciamiento de los organismos de ciencia, tecnología, la privatización de áreas estratégicas y los salarios de miseria que reciben los profesionales”, aseveró a

Tiempo

.


Santana también señaló el incumplimiento de la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario por parte del gobierno libertario y completó recordando que San Martín fue la “capital de la industria”. Haciendo referencia a que hoy sus bases industriales están destruidas.


Destrucción del campo científico y educativo


Yamila Mathon, es especialista en Tecnologías de Gestión y del Conocimiento del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Industrial (INTI). En diálogo con Tiempo, denunció que el Ministerio de Desregulación del Estado que conduce Federico Sturzenegger, está ejerciendo “la máxima expresión del desguace” en el campo de la ciencia, tecnología, la industria y la educación.


Mathon contó que en el marco de las acciones de articulación que vienen haciendo las y los trabajadores del INTI, CNEA y la UNSAM , la semana pasada realizaron una feria de ciencias en el predio de la Municipalidad de San Martín.


Ataques del Gobierno a la ciencia y la tecnología


“Lo hicimos para mostrarle a la sociedad cuáles son nuestros trabajos y la importancia del desarrollo tecnológico para la comunidad. Y pudimos difundir los ataques que estamos sufriendo por parte del Gobierno Nacional”, repasó la profesional.


Y completó: “Este jueves para darle continuidad a ese tipo de acciones que nos permiten -dentro del corredor del Polo Tecnológico Miguelete- llevar acciones mancomunadas hicimos esta marcha de antorchas en defensa de la ciencia y sus trabajadores”.


Mathon siguió denunciando el despido de 60 compañeras y compañeros de la CNEA. También el ataque permanente del Gobierno con los salarios de miseria que cobran las y los científicos, técnicos y administrativos.


Concluyó remarcando que son parte del Sistema Científico Nacional y que la política actual tiene como objetivo la destrucción de todo el Sistema. Y que es imprescindible que la sociedad tome conciencia sobre las consecuencias que esto acarrea para el país.


Fuente:

https://www.tiempoar.com.ar/ta_article/ciencia-tecnologia-educacion-marcha/

Marcha de antorchas por la ciencia, la tecnología y la educación

author: Simon Childs
title: Anti-Migrant Protesters Invade Hotel of Pakistani Cricket Team
content:
Protesters banged on the bedroom doors of Portsmouth’s Marriott hotel on Tuesday night, believing they had found a group of migrants to harass. However, they went home after discovering they were protesting a visiting Pakistani cricket team.


Protesters reportedly reached the floor the professional athletes were staying on, believing the four-star hotel was being used to house asylum seekers. 


The chief operating officer of the Pakistan Cricket Board, Sumair Syed, told the BBC the team reported people “knocking on their doors”, but the cricketers “behaved responsibly and didn’t escalate the situation” he said. 


Councillor George Madgwick, the leader of Reform UK in Hampshire was in attendance.


In a since deleted Facebook post he wrote: “A number of concerned local residents spotted what they believed to be migrants going into the Marriott hotel.


“I visited the manager and the hotel explained it was a Pakistani Cricket team staying. The cricket team coach came to speak to me personally and I saw proof (hotel were happy to provide).”


Madgwick claimed he spoke directly to the crowd of “40/50 people” who he said “respectfully accepted” that the guests weren’t asylum seekers and left within five minutes. 


The incident comes as Hampshire Police investigate reports of assaults and criminal damage on Sunday night, when far-right activist ‘Danny Tommo’ led hundreds of people to Portsmouth harbour. The crowd, some of whom were wearing masks, confronted riot police in order to stop the arrival of 120 people who had been travelling to the UK in a single dinghy.


Hampshire Police said no offences were committed on Tuesday, and the crowd dispersed at around 9pm.


Madgwick, who has been conducting an extended media round defending the anti-migrant protest on Sunday night, appeared to take credit. “I’m glad I could do my bit to help the situation and stop tensions rising,” he said on Facebook. 


“The hotel manager was very thankful and actually was sympathetic to the local issues at the moment but just wanted her guests not to have to worry, which is fair enough.”


In a caustic post on Facebook, Portsmouth Stand Up to Racism said Madgwick “fell short of claiming that he deserved the Nobel Peace prize for his mediation skills.”


The group added: “Allowing racists to mobilise like this every time they become suspicious of any group of non-white people in Portsmouth is extremely dangerous. It is racism in action and it has to stop.”


The Portsmouth Marriott hotel has been approached for comment.


This is not the first time migrant-mania has led to confusion. Last year, Reform UK politician Ryan Coogan, shared a picture of some people getting out of a minibus in Cromer and asked, “Is this part of another quiet relocation scheme – although these usually happen in the middle of the night?” The image was also circulated on far-right Facebook groups, but it turned out to be a group of young churchgoers on a trip to the seaside.


Anyone who believes that Reform’s anti-migrant stance could improve things for the workers in the UK might be interested in

The Bureau of Investigative Journalism’s (TBIJ) 

 finding that two of Madgwick’s restaurant businesses have been ordered to pay £4,386 to former employees for breaching employment law, by failing to pay holiday and maternity pay. He told TBIJ the rulings were made without the companies having the opportunity to defend the claims.

The Kronstadt Commune 70th Anniversary International Syndicalist Conference

Anarcho-Syndicalism in the USSR Today

Interview with Vadim Damier of the Initiative of Revolutionary Anarchists (IREAN)

Seventy years after the death of Kropotkin, the massacre of the Kronstadt Commune and the rout of Makhno, the Party which outlawed anarchism in Russia has itself become a banned organisation. But anarchy in the USSR, has made a new beginning.

Might anarchism now fill the ideological vacuum, left by the collapse of Marxism?

Here, with commentaries from some of their West-European comrades, the new Russian anarchists speak for themselves about their ideas, and of how anarchy may bring a new order, based on freedom, to the chaos of the USSR.

a harbinger of Russian anarchism

who put resistance to oppression above the

“We do not fear anarchy, but invoke it, convinced as we are that anarchy, meaning the full affirmation of unfettered popular life, must inaugurate liberty, equality, justice, the new order and the clash between Revolution and Reaction”.

On 28 May, 1989, 20,000 people marched through Moscow, demonstrating against the Congress of People’s Deputies. The Guardian’s Jonathan Steele noticed among the banners, “a black flag with a red star carried by the recently formed Anarcho-Syndicalist Club. The slogan read: ‘No confidence in the Supreme Soviet — form a left-wing faction’”.

This was the first open display by anarchists in the Soviet capital since 13 February, 1921, when a crowd of the same size joined the funeral cortege of Peter Kropotkin. Then came Kronstadt, the rout of Makhno and the outlawing of open anarchist organisation[2]. Trotsky boasted: “At last the Soviet government, with an iron broom, has rid Russia of anarchism”.

Anarchism in the USSR was not so easily swept away. The full history of the anarchist underground during the Stalin years has not been told (there were ‘armed anarchist uprisings’ in Siberia, in the late 1920s, of which nothing is known). Yagoda’s OGPU was still busy, breaking-up illegal anarchist groups, well into the early 1930s. From then, until the late 1940s, the only news of anarchists in Russia which reached the west was of those in prisons or labour camps.

In October 1936, a delegation of the Spanish CNT went to Moscow, seeking Soviet aid against Franco. The delegation took with them a long list[3] of exiled or imprisoned anarchists and syndicalists, whose release and passage to Spain they requested of the Soviet government. Heading the list was Aaron Baron, one of the founders of the Nabat Confederation in Ukraine, who had been a prisoner since 1920. The CNT delegation went back to Spain alone.

Baron was unexpectedly set free in 1938 and allowed to settle in Kharkov. Less than a year later, he …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Bush, With Legacy of Torture, Unveils Portrait Book of “Political Prisoners”
content:
The war on terror and PATRIOT Act president is releasing a book of portraits of dissenters called “The Call of Freedom.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Former President George W. Bush, the father of the global war on terror that has suppressed and killed millions of people across the world, has announced that he is releasing a book of paintings called The Call of Freedom: Portraits of Political Prisoners and Dissidents.

The book is being published by Penguin Random House imprint Crown, and includes paintings and biographical information on 44 subjects. It is slated to be released on March 9, 2027.

The foreword is being written by former Soviet Union dissident and Israeli politician Natan Sharansky. Sharansky is a former Israeli cabinet minister across four successive Israeli governments and, at one point, was deputy prime minister under Ariel Sharon. He is also the founder of the Yisrael B’Aliyah political party, which merged with Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party in 2003; today, he defends and cheers Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

The book is slated to extol human rights and dissent, despite the Bush administration’s legacy of having massively eroded those principles. Bush’s presidential library is also selling admission to an exhibit displaying the portraits.

Some subjects include Iranian dissident Mahsa Amini, who died in Iranian custody in 2022, and Nicaragua critic Rolando Álvarez, a Catholic bishop imprisoned in the country after refusing to be exiled in 2023. The cover of the book appears to also include figures like the current Dalai Lama, Malala Yousafzai, and Nelson Mandela.

Bush said that the goal of the book is “highlighting the courage and resilience of political prisoners and dissidents in the face of tyrants.”

“My hope is that these 44 paintings and the stories that accompany them will inspire that same fearlessness and determination in others,” he said. “[T]his project sends a message that the United States cares deeply about people seeking freedom — and that we who live in liberty have a duty to stand with those who do not.”

However, those in the U.S. whose “fearlessness” may be inspired by the book could face punishment by the very federal structures that the Bush administration set up to suppress dissent — structures that every successive president has expanded. The Bush administration established or ushered in the post-9/11 PATRIOT Act, the Department of Homeland Security, the war on terror and “forever wars,” and other sweeping measures that fundamentally transformed the nation’s legal systems to supercharge violence, war, surveillance, and criminalization.

Bush himself imprisoned political dissidents. After 9/11, the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) established a global network of “black sites,” the extent of which are still unknown today, where U.S. operatives extrajudicially imprisoned and tortured countless people. The most famous of these is notorious torture camp Guantánamo Bay.

Bush admitted to authorizing torture in his 2010 memoir, and such tactics were used extensively at torture site Abu Ghraib, in Iraq. There, the U.S. interrogated and tortured many political prisoners, at least hundreds of them civilians. When chilling images of the abuses were leaked in 2003, Bush downplayed them, saying that the abuses were committed by a few “bad apples.” The military launched supposed investigations into the torture that were designed to shield higher level officials from facing consequences, and top officials walked free.

As we look to the next 25 years, we have launched a special fundraising campaign. Looking to a sustainable future for our publication, we have a fundraising goal of $92,000 in the next 8 days.

title: Released prisoners: We were tortured in the Syrian Interim Government’s prisons
content:
The prisoners released today spoke about the conditions of their detention and their transfers between various prisons, stating that they had been subjected to torture.


Şahîn Osman said he had been held in the Al-Rai and Al-Hasiya prisons after he was arrested by Turkish intelligence agents in Jarablus in November 2024 while traveling to Manbij.


Osman stated that more than 250 prisoners from Hesekê, Afrin, Raqqa, Amûdê, Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî were held in Al-Hasiya prison.


Mistefa Yûnis, from Kobanê, said he was arrested on January 12, 2026, and had been held in various prisons. He was transferred from Homs to Damascus, then to Al-Hasiya prison, and later to Deir ez-Zor and Hesekê.


Ehmed Elî El Casim, from Raqqa, said he was arrested in Latakia on August 10, 2025. He was transferred from Al-Hasiya prison to the Al-Rai military prison, then to a prison in Deir ez-Zor, and finally to Manbij Prison.


El Casim said that prisoners were treated poorly and subjected to torture in the prisons.


Şaban Mihemed, from Afrin, said he was captured by armed groups in 2024 and later handed over to the General Security. He was held in Al-Hasiya prison, where prisoners were subjected to torture.


Şaban Mihemed added that his family in the Mabata district of Afrin did not know where he was being held during his detention.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Moreno: Condenaron a policía bonaerense a 16 años de prisión por el homicidio de Sergio Bogarín
content:
El sargento Lucas Caldevilla fue condenado a 16 años de prisión por homicidio agravado por el uso de arma de fuego. Pero el Tribunal Criminal nº 4 de Mercedes mantuvo la situación de arresto domiciliario con salidas laborales del asesino hasta que la sentencia quede firme. “Celebramos que el juicio culminara con la condena por homicidio agravado, como correspondía, pero exigimos que la pena sea de efectivo cumplimiento ya. Nada de domiciliaria al gatillo fácil”, reclamaron desde la CORREPI.


Compartimos el comunicado de la Coordinadora contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI):


¡Justicia por Sergio Bogarín! Condenaron al policía bonaerense a 16 años de prisión por su homicidio


El viernes 18 de noviembre de 2022, alrededor de las 21:30, Hilda Salas estaba tomando mate con su hija María, mientras su nieta de 6 años y su biznieto de 2 jugaban con sus tíos Marcelo y Sergio en su casa del barrio El Paraíso de Las Catonas, Moreno.


Sergio y Marcelo fueron, junto a los chicos, a un kiosko a una cuadra y media, donde compraron una botella de cerveza y helados. En el trayecto, vieron en una esquina a dos vecinos, un conocido “transa” del barrio, Cristian Salguero, y Lucas Caldevilla, policía de Caballería de la PBA, que los miraron mal e hicieron gestos amenazantes.Los muchachos volvieron a su casa. Sergio entró a poner la botella en la heladera, mientras Marcelo se quedaba afuera con los nenes.


En ese momento aparecieron Lucas, Cristian y un tercer hombre que no conocían. El policía empujó y le pegó en la cara a Marcelo, mientras todos gritaban. Cuando Sergio salió, alertado por los gritos, el policía dio la orden: “Matalo, por rastrero”. Salguero disparó el arma que portaba. Cuatro disparos impactaron en Sergio, que cayó herido al mismo tiempo que su madre y su hermana salían a la vereda.


Mientras María atinó a abrazar a su hija y se quedó paralizada junto a la puerta, Hilda y Marcelo corrieron hacia los agresores que, siempre dirigidos por el policía, huyeron hacia la esquina. Allí hubo más disparos, al grito de “correte, vieja de mierda, o te mato al otro hijo”.


Marcelo atinó a sacarse la remera e intentar una defensa tirando una piedra, pero Hilda lo frenó y llevó de vuelta hacia la casa. Sergio ya estaba muerto.


A lo largo de casi cuatro años, la familia Bogarín luchó por justicia. Lograron que se detuviera al policía Caldevilla, pero pronto la justicia lo benefició con un arresto domiciliario. Salguero nunca fue encontrado y sigue prófugo hasta el día de hoy.


La causa fue rápidamente elevada a juicio, pero en tres oportunidades se postergó el inicio del juicio oral y público. Finalmente, este año, empezaron las audiencias, y hoy, gracias al testimonio de familiares, vecinos y vecinas, el sargento Lucas Caldevilla fue condenado como coautor material penalmente responsable del delito de homicidio agravado por el uso de arma de fuego a la pena de 16 años de prisión.Pero siempre hay un pero: El Tribunal Criminal nº 4 de Mercedes dictó la condena por unanimidad, pero mantuvo la situación de arresto domiciliario con salidas laborales del asesino hasta que la sentencia quede firme.


Celebramos que el juicio culminara con la condena por homicidio agravado, como correspondía, pero exigimos que la pena sea DE EFECTIVO CUMPLIMIENTO YA. Nada de domiciliaria al gatillo fácil.

author: Caio de Freitas
title: Câmeras, IA e repressão unem candidatos dos estados com polícias mais letais do país
content:
Propor o uso de inteligência artificial e a integração de bases de dados com imagens em tempo real para lidar com problemas de segurança pública virou uma bandeira comum entre os candidatos ao governo dos estados, independentemente do espectro político. “Centros de comando e controle”, “cercamento eletrônico” e “videomonitoramento” aparecem como solução nas propostas de candidatos de esquerda, direita e extrema direita, ainda que as tecnologias (muitas já utilizadas pelas forças de segurança) não tenham sido capazes de frear a violência em meio ao aumento da letalidade policial no país.


Em 2025, ações de agentes de segurança resultaram em 6.602 homicídios em todo o país, o maior número absoluto da série histórica do

Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública

 desde 2016. Produzido pelo Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, o anuário aponta Amapá, Bahia, Sergipe, Pará, Goiás, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte, Mato Grosso e Alagoas como os 10 estados com as forças de segurança mais letais no ano passado, com índices superiores à média nacional (de 3,1 mortes a cada 100 mil habitantes).


Para o professor de ciência política da Universidade Federal de São Paulo (

Unifesp

) Bruno Konder Comparato, os dados reforçam que só investir em tecnologia e integração não impede a violência policial.

 “A tecnologia não faz mágica, sobretudo quando falamos de letalidade policial: quem mata não é o computador ou um sistema, é o policial com uma arma na mão.

 Se queremos fazer investimentos para diminuir a violência policial, deve-se investir no treinamento de pessoas, no aprendizado e uso de técnicas não-letais”, afirmou Comparato à

Agência Pública

.


Todos os 10 estados com maior letalidade policial utilizam regularmente tecnologias de integração de dados sensíveis – com acesso em tempo real a informações sigilosas dos cidadãos, como RG, CPF e cadastro do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), entre outros – para monitoramento da população. Um exemplo que salta aos olhos é o Amapá: em 2025, o estado foi a unidade da federação

com a maior taxa de letalidade policial do país

 pelo 7º ano consecutivo e, desde 2024, simultaneamente, concentra também o maior índice de

homicídios em geral no Brasil

. Há anos, a polícia local dispõe de iniciativas próprias de integração de dados e produção de inteligência, o que não foi suficiente para mudar essa realidade.


Policiais militares do Amapá, estado que lidera o ranking nacional de letalidade policial desde 2019


O governador Clécio Luiz (União), candidato à reeleição com

apoio do presidente do Senado

, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), anunciou em junho deste ano

a criação de um novo sistema de inteligência estadual

, agregando o Centro Integrado de Inteligência em Segurança Pública do estado a outros órgãos de segurança e agências federais, como a Polícia Federal (PF) e o Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública (MJSP).


O plano de governo de Clécio Luiz defende ainda a “instalação de câmeras inteligentes” nas “entradas e saídas dos municípios, áreas de maior incidência criminal, rodovias e equipamentos públicos”, com um sistema de “reconhecimento de placas, identificação de veículos com restrição, videomonitoramento em tempo real e inteligência artificial, conectado ao Centro Integrado de Operações de Segurança Pública”. A proposta, no entanto, não menciona ou propõe medidas para diminuir os índices de letalidade policial.


O principal adversário do governador, o ex-prefeito de Macapá Dr. Antônio Furlan (PSD), também promete “implantar e expandir o uso de videomonitoramento, inteligência artificial, análise de dados”, com “um sistema integrado de monitoramento eletrônico nas principais rotas logísticas e áreas estratégicas”, integrando “informações sobre criminalidade, apreensões de drogas e armas, atuação de organizações criminosas e disputas territoriais”. Furlan também ignorou a questão das mortes provocadas por agentes de segurança em sua proposta.


Um

estudo

 feito por pesquisadores da Universidade Federal do Amapá e da Universidade de Lisboa sugere que as mortes causadas por intervenção policial no estado teriam relação direta com o avanço do narcotráfico. A conclusão segue a mesma linha de artigo de 2024 da pesquisadora associada ao Núcleo de Estudos da Violência da Universidade de São Paulo (NEV/USP) Ariadne Natal, que descreve como o Amapá se tornou “uma espécie de entreposto para rotas nacionais e internacionais do tráfico de drogas”.

title: Trump'ın Kasım ara seçimleri oyunu bozuldu: Yüksek Mahkeme "mektupla oy kullanmaya eskisi gibi devam" dedi
content:
ABD Başkanı Donald Trump’ın mektupla oy kullanımını zorlaştırmaya yönelik girişimi Yüksek Mahkeme’nin engeline takıldı. Mahkeme, yönetimin ABD Posta İdaresi (USPS) üzerinden getirmek istediği yeni koşulları durduran alt mahkeme kararının kaldırılması talebini reddetti. Böylece düzenleme 2026 ara seçimlerinden önce yürürlüğe giremeyecek. 


Karar, mektupla oy kullanımına ilişkin davayı bütünüyle sonuçlandırmıyor. Yüksek Mahkeme bu aşamada düzenlemenin nihai olarak Anayasa'ya ya da federal yasalara uygun olup olmadığı konusuna girmeyi reddetti. Mahkeme, yönetimin seçim süreci başlamışken yeni kuralları uygulamaya koymasına izin vermedi.


Trump Yüksek Mahkemeye saldırdı 


Trump, Yüksek Mahkeme’nin kararına sert tepki gösterdi. Mahkeme’nin “Radikal Sol’un baskısına boyun eğdiğini” ileri süren Trump, son dönemde bazı kararların ABD’ye büyük zarar verdiğini savundu.


Trump’ın eleştirilerinin hedefinde, ilk başkanlık döneminde kendisinin Yüksek Mahkeme’ye atadığı Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh ve Amy Coney Barrett da vardı. Buna karşılık, yönetimin mektupla oy düzenlemesinin uygulanmasından yana görüş bildiren Clarence Thomas ve Samuel Alito’yu övdü.


Trump’ın mahkeme kararını kınaması oy kullanma tartışmasının ötesine taşıdı. ABD Başkanı, talebini reddeden ve aralarında kendi atadığı üyelerin de bulunduğu Yüksek Mahkeme çoğunluğunu siyasi baskıya teslim olmakla suçladı.


Trump daha önce de aleyhine karar veren federal yargıçları ve mahkemeleri sert biçimde hedef almıştı. Ancak son açıklaması, 6’ya 3 muhafazakâr çoğunluğa sahip ve üç üyesini bizzat kendisinin atadığı Yüksek Mahkeme’yle ve hukuk devleti ilkesiyle yaşadığı gerilimi özellikle görünür kıldı.


Oyların üçte biri mektupla kullanılıyor


Associated Press’e göre karar sayesinde eyaletler, şimdiye kadar kullandıkları usullerle seçmenlere mektupla oy pusulası göndermeyi sürdürebilecek. Mektupla kullanılan oy miktarı son seçimlerde ABD’de kullanılan oyların yaklaşık üçte birini oluşturuyordu.  


Tartışmanın kaynağında, Trump’ın Mart’ta yayımladığı seçim kararnamesinin ardından ABD Posta İdaresi’nin (USPS) 21 Ağustos’ta açıkladığı yeni düzenleme var. 


Buna göre, eyaletlerden mektupla oy pusulası gönderilecek seçmenlere ilişkin listeleri Posta İdaresi’ne iletmeleri ve USPS tarafından onaylanan, özel barkod taşıyan zarfları kullanmaları isteniyordu. Koşullara uymayan seçim postalarının Posta İdaresi tarafından kabul edilmemesi mümkün olabilirdi. 


Eyaletler ve oy hakkı örgütleri, seçim takvimi başladıktan sonra ülke çapında yeni bir sistem kurulmasının ciddi aksamalara yol açacağını, kurallara uygun biçimde oy kullanmak isteyen seçmenlerin pusulalarının gönderilememesi veya geri çevrilmesi tehlikesi bulunduğunu ileri sürerek karara itiraz etti. 


Trump yönetimi ise düzenlemeyi, seçim güvenliğini artıracak ve posta yoluyla oy kullanımında ülke çapında standartlar oluşturacak bir önlem olarak savundu. 


İki federal yargıç düzenlemeyi durdurdu


Trump yönetiminin girişimi Yüksek Mahkeme’ye ulaşmadan önce iki ayrı federal mahkeme tarafından durduruldu.


Boston’daki Federal Bölge Mahkemesi Yargıcı Indira Talwani, yeni posta kurallarının 2026 ara seçimlerinde uygulanmasını engelledi. Talwani seçimlerin yönetiminde eyaletlere tanınan anayasal yetkileri ve seçim takviminin ulaştığı aşamayı dikkate aldı.


Bir federal temyiz mahkemesi de 10 Eylül’de Trump yönetiminin Talwani’nin kararını kaldırma talebini reddetti. 


Ardından Washington’daki Federal Bölge Mahkemesi Yargıcı Carl Nichols da düzenlemeyi durdurdu. Trump’ın ilk başkanlık döneminde atadığı Nichols, Posta İdaresi’nin Kongre’den açık bir yetki almadan mektupla oy kullanmaya böylesine kapsamlı koşullar getiremeyeceğine karar verdi. 


Trump yönetimi bunun üzerine Yüksek Mahkeme’ye başvurarak Talwani’nin kararının acilen kaldırılmasını ve yeni kuralların kasım seçimlerinde uygulanmasına izin verilmesini istedi.


Yüksek Mahkemeden red 


Konuyu ele alan Yüksek Mahkeme üyelerinden yargıçlar Clarence Thomas ve Samuel Alito yönetimin talebinin kabul edilmesinden yana görüş bildirdiler. Yargıç Brett Kavanaugh ise Posta İdaresi’nin gelecekte seçim postası konusunda bazı düzenlemeler yapma yetkisinin bulunabileceğini belirtmekle birlikte, seçim başladıktan sonra kuralların değiştirilmesinin yaratacağı sorunları gerekçe göstererek bu aşamada yönetimin talebine katılmadığını belirtti. Diğer üyeler Trump'ın talebini reddetti. 


Karar özellikle zamanlaması bakımından önemli. Bazı eyaletlerde seçmenlere oy pusulalarının …

SolarPark3

32,5 milioni di euro

.


A proporlo, in quel del Brianco nei Comuni di Santhià e Cavaglià, è un’impresa controllata dalla

Su questo progetto sono state presentate osservazioni critiche sia per gli aspetti tecnici-ambientali (area riso DOP, impatti paesaggistici, connessione alla rete, ecc.) ancorché sulla origine dei capitali e caratteristiche degli investitori, ossia una società co-partecipata da altre società che hanno attività economiche nei territori occupati, interessi nel settore della difesa e produzione di armi, o sostengono direttamente o indirettamente i crimini imputati ad Israele dalla Corte Internazionale di Giustizia (CIG).


In occasione della decisoria CdS il 

Circolo Tavo Burat

title: Week-end contre les CRA
content:
Le weekend de mobilisation régional contre le CRA de Béziers se tiendra... à Montpellier ! RDV le 3 octobre pour une journée complète de tables rondes, débats, pièce de théatre, discussions, projections, concerts... ; et le 4 octobre à 14h place de la Comédie pour manifester en masse notre solidarité envers toutes les personnes enfermées, et contre les CRA, les prisons & les frontières !


Adissiatz !


Le week-end de mobilisation du 3 & 4 octobre contre la construction du CRA (Centre de Rétention Administrative) de Béziers aura finalement lieu à Montpellier. Cela fait des mois que nous recherchons un lieu pour accueillir cet événement à Béziers et aux alentours. Nous n'avons essuyé que des refus. Le contexte local est tendu. La mairie de Béziers via son maire d'extrême droite Ménard appelle à "renvoyer les OQTF chez eux" lors de son dernier discours pour l'ouverture de la féria. Les villes des alentours n'ont pas eu le courage de porter un tel événement dans leurs locaux. Nous avons aussi longuement cherché des terrains agricoles pour accueillir l'évènement (dans les alentours proches de Béziers pour la proximité avec la manifestation du dimanche) : là encore, que des refus. Pour les rares propriétaires politiquement aligné·es avec cet évènement, cela n'a pas marché, pour des questions de manque d'espace disponible, d'incompatibilité avec les cultures en place, ou encore de peur de se mettre à dos la municipalité.


Activation du plan B


Heureusement nous avions prévu que ça allait être galère, et c'est pourquoi nous avons collectivement décidé de basculer sur le plan B(oulet de canon sur le cracra), à Montpellier.


Pourquoi Montpelhièr ? Car d'abord c'est là où se trouve la préfécture de l'Hérault, représentante de l'Etat sur le territoire et responsable de ce projet raciste. Ensuite, notre présence en ville permettra de visibiliser la mobilisation collective contre ce projet répugnant ce qui est un des objectifs du week-end.


Ainsi, nous vous invitons à se retrouver en nombre le 3 et le 4 octobre à Montpellier, pour manifester colère, rage et détermination contre les frontières, CRA et toutes autres formes d'enfermement. Nous sommes résolument opposé·es à la rétention des personnes sans-papiers et en particulier à son industrialisation dont le projet de CRA d'une capacité de 140 personnes à Béziers en est la pointe ! Et à tous les CRA existants et en projet qui sont des camps d'enfermement abjects.


Infos pratiques


En raison de la nouvelle localisation de l'événement, nous ne pourrons pas garantir un lieu d'hébergement collectif pendant le week-end maiiiiiiiis nous organiserons un système d'hébergement militant (infos à venir)


Pendant la journée du samedi, il y aura des tables rondes, discussions et une projection dans deux lieux : la Tendresse et la Carmagnole.


Le soir, il y aura une cantine et des concerts à la Tendresse (avec un jauge limitée à 120 personnes)


Enfin, le dimanche matin aura lieu une conférence gesticulée le matin puis une manifestation qui passera devant la préfecture de Montpellier et qui finira en assemblée. Départ 14h place de la Comédie.


Un programme plus détaillé sera partagé prochainement, ainsi que les informations pratiques sur les lieux, les hébergements et les transports.


Mur par mur, pierre par pierre, nous détruirons les frontières, les prisons et les CRA !

author: Max Hampel Altheide
title: Überwachungsgesetz auf der Kippe
content:
Bild: Alupus CC-BY-SA 3.0 Bearbeitung: Melanie Lübbert

Parlamentarische Anhörungen können eine ziemlich formale Angelegenheit sein. Im Innenausschuss des Thüringer Landtags zeigte sich am 27. August, dass sie auch etwas in Bewegung bringen können. padeluun war dort für Digitalcourage als Sachverständiger zum neuen Polizeiaufgabengesetz eingeladen. Dabei ging es um weitreichende neue Befugnisse für Überwachung und automatisierte Datenanalyse.

Die Grundlage für seinen Auftritt war eine Stellungnahme, die Digitalcourage zuvor zum Gesetzentwurf eingereicht hatte. Statt sie noch einmal vorzulesen, konzentrierte sich padeluun darauf, die problematischen Befugnisse anhand konkreter Beispiele und seiner langjährigen Erfahrung mit Überwachung einzuordnen.

Bei automatisierter Videoüberwachung etwa geht es nicht nur darum, ob eine Software Fehler macht. Entscheidend ist, was nach einem Fehler passiert. Ein falscher Treffer ist im Polizeikontext eben keine falsch sortierte Urlaubsaufnahme. Er kann zu Kontrolle, Durchsuchung oder anderen ganz realen Eingriffen führen.

Auch biometrische Suche im Internet und die automatisierte Verknüpfung großer Datenbestände verändern die Qualität staatlicher Überwachung erheblich. Was bislang verstreut und nur mit Aufwand zusammenzuführen war, kann plötzlich automatisiert ausgewertet werden. Aus einzelnen Informationen entsteht ein immer genaueres Bild von Menschen, auch von solchen, die überhaupt nichts falsch gemacht haben.

Für padeluun gehört deshalb eine einfache Frage ins Zentrum der Debatte:

„Wollen wir diese Instrumente auch einer Regierung in die Hand geben, der wir überhaupt nicht vertrauen?“

Denn Polizeigesetze werden nicht nur für die heutige Regierung geschrieben. Die technischen Möglichkeiten, die heute geschaffen werden, sind auch morgen noch da.

Besonders spannend wurde es nach dem Eingangsstatement. In den Rückfragen konnten viele Punkte vertieft werden. Dabei fiel auch ein Satz, von padeluun, der die grundsätzliche Dimension der Debatte ziemlich gut zusammenfasst:

„Auch ein demokratisch beschlossenes Unrecht bleibt ein Unrecht.“

Und tatsächlich setzte die fast den ganzen Tag dauernde Anhörung von zahlreichen Expert.innen aus Zivilgesellschaft, Wissenschaft und Behörden etwas in Bewegung. Im Anschluss erklärten Abgeordnete aus den Reihen der Regierungskoalition, dass die Anhörung sie bei dem Gesetzentwurf ins Zweifeln gebracht habe.

Damit ist die zuvor erwartete Zustimmung zum Gesetzentwurf zumindest infrage gestellt.

Seit der Anhörung haben sich zudem die politischen Verhältnisse im Thüringer Landtag verändert. Die bisherige BSW-Fraktion hat sich aufgelöst. Zehn ihrer ehemaligen Mitglieder gründeten die neue Fraktion „Thüringen.Gerecht“, die gemeinsam mit CDU und SPD die Regierungskoalition bildet. Zusammen verfügt die Koalition allerdings nur über 39 Stimmen und damit über keine eigene Mehrheit im Landtag.

Auch die Ausschüsse wurden infolge der neuen Mehrheitsverhältnisse neu zusammengesetzt. Ob das geplante Thüringer Polizeigesetz in seiner jetzigen Form eine Mehrheit findet und welche Rolle die nach der Anhörung geäußerten Zweifel dabei spielen werden, ist heute noch offener als an jenem Donnerstag.

Aber genau dafür sollten parlamentarische Anhörungen da sein: nicht als Ritual, bei dem anschließend ohnehin alle so abstimmen wie vorher, sondern als Ort, an dem Argumente tatsächlich etwas verändern können.

Wenn das in Erfurt gelungen ist, hat sich die Anhörung mehr als gelohnt.

Ein Dank geht auch an die Aktivist.innen des Bündnisses „ThürPAG stoppen“, die während der Anhörung den ganzen Tag vor dem Landtag protestiert und informiert haben. Das Bündnis organisiert seit Monaten Widerstand gegen die geplante Verschärfung des Polizeigesetzes und sammelt aktuell mit einer Petition Unterschriften gegen den Gesetzentwurf: https://weact.campact.de/petitions/grundrechte-schutzen-polizeiaufgabengesetz-stoppen

title: Activist Blogging Platform Shuts Down After Terrorism Designation
content:
Washington DC — On August 26, 2026, the U.S. Departments of State and the Treasury

designated

 a volunteer tech collective behind a popular activist blogging platform a terrorist organization. 


Autistici/Inventati (A/I), the Italian collective behind

NoBlogs.org

, now

joins

 such organizations as the Islamic State group and al Qaeda on the list of Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGTs), a category created by former President George W. Bush in an

executive order

 weeks after the 9/11 attacks. Shortly thereafter, Autistici/Inventati lost their domain, autistici.org, and had their Italian

bank account closed

 due to the threat of U.S. sanctions. 


NoBlogs was

hacked

 on August 28, two days after the terrorism designation. A “Free Palestine” button on the NoBlogs homepage was redirected to link to a U.S. government “self deportation” site, and a message was

posted

 claiming that NoBlogs user information had been “saved and given to the United States government.”


The hack was

quickly promoted

 on X by right-wing influencer and Pentagon employee Jennica Pounds. On September 6, Autistici/Inventati

announced

 its imminent closure. 


A/I, which provided its services such as NoBlogs to protect activists, feared that maintaining its services would only expose users to additional risk given the “political climate” now that it was labeled a Specially Designated Global Terrorist. 


“Under these circumstances, we are no longer able to maintain our original mission – offering secure and non-commercial digital tools,” explained the collective in a

statement

. “Now turn off your PCs, get out of your homes, struggle, hug each other and keep on smiling. We are stopping, but the Resistance and ideas do not stop. Stay human.” In an announcement on

September 8

, A/I reported that emails, listservs, and NoBlogs accounts would cease operation within the following ten days. 


May First Movement Technology, a nonprofit that similarly provides internet services for social movement groups, released a statement that “emphatically condemns” the A/I sanctions, which it called “excessive and vindictive.” May First had one of its former members, Samidoun Palestinian Prisoner Solidarity Network, likewise designated as a terrorist group by the Treasury Department in 2024. “US government can effectively isolate any organization without presenting evidence or trial,” May First

stated

, “by simply alleging that they support terrorism.”


“From what we understand,” an A/I member had stated in an

Italian-language interview

, “any American citizen who interacts with us after [a U.S. Treasury Department

deadline

 of] September 25 would risk 30 years in jail.”

Executive Order 13244

 bans the “making or receiving of any contribution of funds, goods, or services to or for the benefit of” Specially Designated Terrorist Groups.


Designated Groups are “cut off” from the

U.S. financial system

, with all financial transactions blocked in areas subject to U.S. law. Significantly, the U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Asset Control reserves the right to levy

secondary sanctions

 against non-U.S. individuals, organizations, or financial institutions that have dealings with SDTGs. A/I’s Italian bank therefore faced the possibility of being itself blocked from the U.S. financial system were it to continue providing banking services to the collective. 


“The real coercive power of the United States lies in progressively making it impossible to bank, host, or provide services to the designated entity,”

said

 Beniamino Irdi of the German Marshall Fund, a U.S. organization promoting transatlantic relations. “The power of sanctions derives from the ability to influence third parties, financial and commercial operators that, for compliance reasons, may decide to sever relations with the designated entity.”


Specially Designated Global Terrorists are distinct from Foreign Terrorist Organizations, which the powerful Atlantic Council think tank

refers to

 as the “gold standard of terrorism sanctions.” 


Former

Biden administration

 Senior Director for International Economics Peter Harrell contended in a

post on X

 that sanctions against A/I might be illegal under U.S. law, given the existence of a carve-out for “any postal, telegraphic, telephonic, or other personal communication” in the Berman Amendments to the 1977 International Emergency Economic Powers Act. author: Alexandra Martinez
title: A New Campaign Is Pushing Ulta Beauty to Drop Flock Cameras From Its Stores
content:
A petition demanding the removal of the surveillance cameras has more than 15,000 signatories.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A national gender justice organization is escalating a campaign against Ulta Beauty over the cosmetics retailer’s use of automated license-plate reader (ALPR) cameras made by the surveillance company Flock Safety, arguing that it threatens customer privacy and could disproportionately harm women and gender-expansive people.

UltraViolet, a women-led gender justice organization, launched its “Drop Flock” campaign this month, calling on Ulta Beauty to terminate contracts with Flock Safety and other mass surveillance companies. The organization said its petition had surpassed 15,000 signatures as of Sept. 8.

“Ulta Beauty has built a multibillion-dollar business on women’s trust,” UltraViolet Campaign Director Jenna Sherman said in a statement accompanying the campaign’s launch. “Putting Flock, an invasive mass surveillance system, right outside its stores without customer knowledge or consent is a direct violation of that trust.”

When asked about the campaign’s privacy and gender justice concerns, a Flock spokesperson pointed to the company’s public media FAQ page outlining its data retention policies and security safeguards. According to the FAQ page, cameras collect vehicle and license-plate data for law enforcement investigations with access and retention controlled by the agencies that use the system. Flock’s website says the company does not sell the data or use facial recognition. Ulta Beauty did not respond to Prism’s request for comment.

The campaign grew out of UltraViolet’s broader work examining the intersection of technology, privacy, and gender-based violence. Sherman said the organization has spent years tracking technologies that can be used to surveil, stalk, or harass women and gender-expansive people, including facial recognition, connected vehicles, location tracking, and other emerging technologies.

UltraViolet became more directly involved in the campaign against Flock Safety after working with Fight for the Future, a digital rights organization that has organized campaigns against Flock’s contracts with major retailers and local governments.

Flock Safety manufactures ALPR cameras that capture license-plate information and other visual details around vehicles. The company has built a large network of cameras used by law enforcement agencies and private organizations. Flock told Axios in August that its network had grown to more than 120,000 cameras across the country.

UltraViolet’s campaign is part of a national backlash against Flock and other ALPR providers. Local governments across the country have faced pressure to reject or end contracts with surveillance companies, while digital rights and civil liberties groups have increasingly turned their attention toward private companies using similar technology. In Florida, for example, state officials recently moved to restrict ALPR cameras on state roads amid concerns about privacy and misuse.

UltraViolet argues that corporations should face the same scrutiny as government agencies when they deploy surveillance technologies capable of collecting sensitive information about the public.

Sherman said UltraViolet was surprised to discover that Ulta was identified by Flock as a retail partner in the company’s public materials. The organization had already seen strong public engagement around campaigns targeting Flock cameras at Lowe’s hardware stores and decided to bring the issue to Ulta.

“We knew that we owed it to them to campaign specifically about Ulta because it is a company with a majority-women shopper base,” Sherman told Prism.

Ulta’s privacy policy contains a dedicated section on “Automated License Plate Recognition Usage and Privacy Policy.”

The policy states that Ulta uses ALPR systems where they are not prohibited by law and that the systems are used for the security of its premises, employees, guests, and assets. It also says information from those systems can be disclosed to third parties, including law enforcement, for specified purposes such as safety, protecting property, and complying with the law.

Sherman argued that the larger concern is the normalization of surveillance technology in everyday spaces. Unlike conventional security cameras, ALPR systems can automatically collect …

Πρόκειται για μια αντιφασιστική, αντιρατσιστική, αντισεξιστική και αντιμιλιταριστική οργάνωση που αντιτίθεται στον καπιταλισμό και τον αυταρχισμό και φιλοξενεί μόνο όσους συμμερίζονται αυτές τις αρχές και που φιλοξενεί 16.000 mails, 1.500 ιστότοπους, 5.500 λίστες αλληλογραφίας και 10.000 ιστολόγια.


Η

Το δηλωμένο μοντέλο είναι ριζικά διαφορετικό από αυτό των μεγάλων εμπορικών πλατφορμών. Καμία διαφήμιση, καμία πώληση προσωπικών δεδομένων, καμία αποζημίωση για εθελοντές. author: EDRi
title: Europe’s cookie law is really a law about surveillance
content:
The ePrivacy framework limits commercial tracking and state access to communications. It is now being weakened from several directions at once.

By Itxaso Domínguez de Olazábal & Chiara Casati (guest author) · September 10, 2026

In 2022, a reporter paid $160 for a week’s worth of location data linked to visits to over 600 Planned Parenthood clinics in the United States. The dataset showed where groups of visitors had come from, how long they stayed, and where they went next. The broker withdrew the product after the story was published. However, the market behind it remained.

Europe has seen a similar market emerge. Journalists have obtained billions of commercially traded location records from Germany and Belgium. The data exposed movements around hospitals, religious sites, trade union offices, government ministries, military sites, EU institutions and NATO buildings. Information gathered through ordinary apps for advertising can reveal intimate details of people’s lives, identify public officials and create security risks for entire institutions.

These examples illustrate a distinction at the heart of what people usually call ‘EU privacy law’ that may seem unnecessarily fussy to readers elsewhere. In the United States, ‘privacy’ often covers the whole problem, while EU law recognises two distinct fundamental rights. Article 7 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the Union protects private life, the home and communications, while Article 8 protects personal data.

The distinction is quite important: whereas data protection largely governs what happens when personal data are processed, privacy and communications confidentiality also protect the space from which information is obtained. They put a boundary on entering that space in the first place. The EU built the ePrivacy framework around that question. ePrivacy adds specific rules for the confidentiality of communications and access to information stored on, or generated by, people’s devices, including rules covering communications, metadata, and location. While the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) primarily governs access to personal data — what organizations might do with data once they have processed it. This distinction matters, and it disappears when ‘privacy’ becomes a casual synonym for data protection.

Most people meet ePrivacy through a cookie banner, and this may be the worst possible introduction. A framework about confidentiality looks like a tedious set of rules about pop-ups, while the tracking industry points to the pop-ups it helped create as proof that the law has failed. Article 5(3), the provision behind many banners, controls when an actor may store information on, or obtain information from, a person’s terminal equipment. But it goes beyond that: ePrivacy is concerned with the act of accessing the device itself. “Terminal equipment” includes phones and laptops, connected cars, televisions, wearables, smart glasses and other parts of the Internet of Things. The rule covers fingerprinting, tracking pixels, local storage, operating-system identifiers and instructions that make a device send information elsewhere. The principle is straightforward: a device does not become open to inspection simply because one fragment of information cannot identify its user on its own. ePrivacy also protects communications confidentiality and regulates the traffic and location data held by communications providers. It limits retention and reuse, covers unsolicited communications, and sets the conditions under which Member States may restrict confidentiality.

The ePrivacy Directive’s scope has never matched the way people use digital services. It was written around traditional telephone and communications providers, meaning that many online services originally were excluded from its protection. Messaging and webmail services can now fall under communications confidentiality rules, but coverage still depends on legal classifications that users cannot see. The same message, location trail, or device data can receive different protection depending on whether the company is labeled a telecom provider, messaging service, or platform: under these conditions, is the law still protecting the underlying right?

The distinction between GDPR and ePrivacy becomes even more important when we look at surveillance. From one side, commercial surveillance commonly starts before the GDPR question even arises, with access to a device or a communications-related …

author: Jian Zharese Joies Sanz
title: Tech professionals warn of privacy risks in proposed ID rule for Meta users
content:
MANILA – The Computer Professionals’ Union (CPU) sounded the alarm over the Department of Information and Communications Technology’s (DICT) proposal to require social media users to have the Philippine National ID.

The DICT claimed that the proposal would be the ‘safest’ way of verifying age of social media users, following the government’s statement blaming social media and online games for the series of school shootings in the country.

The CPU, however, maintained that the proposal is alarming and profoundly intrusive to Filipino citizens’ digital rights. “Rather than fostering a safe online environment, this draconian measure represents a clear and direct attack on the basic human right to privacy without any legitimate grounds that it will protect us from crime, or protect our youth from the culture of violence,” the union said.

Beyond possible violations of citizens’ privacy, the CPU said the rule strips away the right to anonymity, threatens free expression, and can become a dangerous tool for mass surveillance.

The group pointed out that the SIM Registration Law did not address the incidence of cybercrime after it was enacted into law under Ferdinand Marcos Jr’ s administration.

Despite the law’s promise to stop cybercrime and scams, reports of digital crimes have reportedly tripled in 2024, according to the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC). In an online article, the CICC recorded more than 10,004 cybercrime complaints in 2024 and P198 million ($3.16 million) in monetary losses from these incidents.

The CPU asserted that the proposal will also not solve the issues of online exploitation or youth violence. According to them, the real solution is a better system—accessible mental health services, comprehensive digital literacy programs integrated into educational systems, and stricter gun control measures to prevent real-world violence.
